items.question: Do you like eating vegetables, how often?
items.questionZh: 你喜欢吃蔬菜吗？多久吃一次？
items.answer: Yes, I eat vegetables with lunch and dinner most days. I like having something fresh with my meals, although I still prefer some vegetables to others.
items.ideaZh: 先说基本每天午晚餐都吃，再说明喜欢清爽配菜，但不是所有菜都喜欢。

items.question: Were there any vegetables you disliked when you were young?
items.questionZh: 你小时候有没有不喜欢吃的蔬菜？
items.answer: I disliked bitter melon because of the taste. My parents encouraged me to try it, but I usually preferred sweeter fruit, such as mangoes. I was a bit picky then.
items.ideaZh: 小时候不喜欢苦瓜的苦味，较挑食；童年口味为补充设定。

items.question: Where do you usually buy vegetables?
items.questionZh: 你通常在哪里买蔬菜？
items.answer: Usually at a supermarket or a nearby market with my family. I like being able to check the vegetables before buying them, rather than choosing only from a picture online.
items.ideaZh: 超市或附近市场，能实际看看蔬菜再买；把旧稿fruit改为vegetables。

items.question: Do people around you grow their own vegetables?
items.questionZh: 你周围的人会自己种蔬菜吗？
items.answer: Yes, my grandfather grows a few vegetables in his garden. He enjoys looking after them, and sometimes we have what he has picked with a family meal.
items.ideaZh: 爷爷在花园种一点蔬菜，照料过程和收获都让他开心；与旧种植故事一致，属于草稿设定。

items.question: Where do people usually buy vegetables?
items.questionZh: 人们通常在哪里买蔬菜？
items.answer: Around where I live, people buy them from markets or supermarkets. Markets let people choose individual vegetables, while supermarkets are convenient when they need several other things as well.
items.ideaZh: 根据身边观察说菜市场和超市；前者能挑，后者方便顺便买其他东西。

items.question: Did you like eating vegetables when you were a child?
items.questionZh: 你小时候喜欢吃蔬菜吗？
items.answer: Not particularly. I preferred meat and usually needed a reminder to eat the vegetables on my plate. I've become less picky, so eating them feels more normal now.
items.ideaZh: 小时候偏爱肉，需要提醒吃菜；现在没那么挑食。童年偏好是拟写内容。

items.question: Do you remember the first day in secondary school?
items.questionZh: 你还记得中学第一天吗？
items.answer: I remember feeling nervous about meeting new classmates. Once I started talking to the person sitting next to me, I felt more comfortable. The small details are a bit unclear now.
items.ideaZh: 初见同学时紧张，和旁边的人聊天后放松；细节记不太清。
items.vocab: nervous — 紧张的；unclear — 不清楚的

items.question: What was the happiest thing for you in secondary school?
items.questionZh: 中学时最让你开心的是什么？
items.answer: Playing basketball with classmates after school was probably the best part. It gave us a break from lessons, and I liked getting to know people outside the classroom.
items.ideaZh: 借用篮球爱好讲课后和同学打球，放松又交朋友；中学时间设定未确认。
items.vocab: people — 人们

items.question: What's your favourite subject at secondary school?
items.questionZh: 你中学时最喜欢什么科目？
items.answer: PE was my favourite because I enjoyed moving around after sitting in lessons. Basketball was the best part for me, and playing with classmates made the lesson more fun.
items.ideaZh: 喜欢体育，坐久后能活动，尤其喜欢和同学打篮球。
items.vocab: PE — 体育课；classmates — 同学
items.provenance: 中学体育偏好、英语困难、首日情绪和课后打球为补充；不写具体学校。

items.question: Were there any subjects that you didn't like studying at secondary school?
items.questionZh: 中学时有没有你不喜欢学的科目？
items.answer: Physics wasn't my favourite. Some explanations felt quite abstract, and I needed more time to understand them. I enjoyed practical activities more than working through long calculations.
items.ideaZh: 直接回答不喜欢物理，原因是抽象和计算多；不是只答“觉得难”。科目偏好可调整。
items.vocab: practical — 实用的

items.question: Is there anything you miss about your secondary school?
items.questionZh: 你怀念中学的哪些方面？
items.answer: I miss seeing the same friends every day and playing basketball after class. Life was busy, but there was a familiar routine, and it was easy to spend time together.
items.ideaZh: 怀念天天见朋友和课后打球；生活规律，相处方便。
items.vocab: familiar routine — 熟悉的日常安排；miss — 怀念
items.provenance: 中学体育偏好、英语困难、首日情绪和课后打球为补充；不写具体学校。

items.question: Would you recommend your secondary school to other people?
items.questionZh: 你会把你的中学推荐给别人吗？
items.answer: Yes, I probably would. I remember having helpful teachers and friends there. I'd still suggest visiting the school first, because what suits me might not suit every student.
items.ideaZh: 会推荐，给出老师和朋友两个理由，同时承认各人需求不同；学校评价为补充。

items.question: Do you like to buy shoes? How often?
items.questionZh: 你喜欢买鞋吗？多久买一次？
items.answer: I don't buy shoes just for fun. I usually get a new pair when the old ones are worn out, so perhaps a couple of times a year.
items.ideaZh: 不为娱乐买鞋，旧鞋穿坏了才换，大概一年几次。
items.vocab: worn out — 穿坏、磨损的；a couple of times — 几次
items.provenance: 舒适运动鞋偏好、约三四百元预算、网购与频率为拟写，可按实际调整。

items.question: Have you ever bought shoes online?
items.questionZh: 你在网上买过鞋吗？
items.answer: Yes, I've bought casual shoes online. It's easy to compare prices, but choosing the right size can be tricky. For basketball shoes, I'd rather try them on first.
items.ideaZh: 买过休闲鞋，但尺码难选；篮球鞋更愿意先试穿。
items.vocab: casual shoes — 休闲鞋；try them on — 试穿它们
items.provenance: 舒适运动鞋偏好、约三四百元预算、网购与频率为拟写，可按实际调整。

items.question: Do you spend a lot of money on shoes?
items.questionZh: 你在鞋子上花很多钱吗？
items.answer: Not really. I usually spend a few hundred yuan on a pair and keep wearing them for quite a while. Comfort matters more to me than an expensive name.
items.ideaZh: 不算多，一双几百元、穿较久；重舒适而非品牌。金额为日常补充。

items.question: Do you prefer sports shoes or fashionable shoes?
items.questionZh: 你更喜欢运动鞋还是时尚鞋？
items.answer: I'd choose sports shoes. I play basketball, and I also like comfortable shoes for walking around. A fashionable pair is less useful to me if it hurts my feet.
items.ideaZh: 选运动鞋，联系真实篮球爱好和日常走路；时尚但磨脚就不实用。
items.vocab: comfortable — 舒适的；useful — 有用的

items.question: Would you choose to wear sneakers when you are not exercising?
items.questionZh: 不运动时你也会穿运动鞋吗？
items.answer: Yes, quite often. They go well with casual clothes and are comfortable for going to class or meeting friends. I don't save them only for playing basketball.
items.ideaZh: 平时上课、见朋友也穿；好搭配且舒服，不只打球时用。
items.vocab: comfortable — 舒适的

items.question: Did you learn to be polite when you were a child?
items.questionZh: 你小时候学过如何有礼貌吗？
items.answer: Yes, my parents taught me to greet people and say thank you. If I forgot, they reminded me. Those small habits gradually became part of how I treat others.
items.ideaZh: 父母教问候和道谢，忘了就提醒，逐渐形成习惯。
items.vocab: gradually — 逐渐地；people — 人们

items.question: When do you think people need to be polite?
items.questionZh: 你觉得哪些时候需要有礼貌？
items.answer: I think we should be polite in everyday situations, especially when asking for help or disagreeing with someone. Even a short, respectful reply can make a conversation go more smoothly.
items.ideaZh: 日常都需要，尤其求助和意见不同时；礼貌有助于交流顺畅。
items.vocab: respectful — 尊重他人的；smoothly — 顺利地
items.provenance: 礼貌教育与童年行为为常见日常补充。

items.question: Have you met anyone who was very polite recently?
items.questionZh: 你最近遇到过特别有礼貌的人吗？
items.answer: Yes, a shop assistant was very patient when I asked about headphones recently. He let me finish my questions and explained things clearly without making me feel rushed.
items.ideaZh: 用原耳机店故事：店员耐心听完、解释、不催促；为已有草稿的复用。
items.vocab: patient — 有耐心的
items.provenance: 基于已确认背景与旧素材拟写；其余日常偏好、人物及时间细节为可调整补充，见中文思路。

items.question: Is it important to be polite?
items.questionZh: 你认为有礼貌很重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, because it helps people feel respected. It doesn't mean agreeing with everything someone says. You can have a different opinion and still explain it without making the other person uncomfortable.
items.ideaZh: 重要，因为让人感到被尊重；不同意也可以温和表达。
items.vocab: respected — 受到尊重的；opinion — 观点
items.provenance: 礼貌教育与童年行为为常见日常补充。

items.question: Do you have any friends who are not very polite?
items.questionZh: 你有没有不太有礼貌的朋友？
items.answer: Occasionally a friend interrupts people when he gets excited. I don't think he means to be rude, but it can be frustrating when you haven't finished speaking.
items.ideaZh: 朋友兴奋时会插话，不一定有恶意，但听者会不舒服；人物习惯为拟写。
items.vocab: frustrating — 令人沮丧的；people — 人们
items.provenance: 基于已确认背景与旧素材拟写；其余日常偏好、人物及时间细节为可调整补充，见中文思路。

items.question: Would you tell a friend if you thought their behaviour wasn't polite?
items.questionZh: 如果朋友行为不礼貌，你会告诉他吗？
items.answer: Yes, if we're close, I'd mention it privately. I'd explain what sounded rude rather than embarrass them in front of everyone. That would make the conversation easier.
items.ideaZh: 亲近朋友会私下提醒，指出行为，不当众让对方难堪。
items.vocab: rather than — 而不是

items.question: When you were a child, how did you learn to be polite?
items.questionZh: 你小时候怎样学会有礼貌？
items.answer: Mostly by watching my parents and listening to their reminders. For example, they asked me to thank people who helped me. Those small habits gradually became part of everyday life.
items.ideaZh: 主要模仿父母并听提醒，比如感谢帮助自己的人，逐渐成为习惯。
items.vocab: reminders — 提醒；gradually — 逐渐地
items.provenance: 礼貌教育与童年行为为常见日常补充。

items.question: When do you think it's most important to be polite?
items.questionZh: 你觉得什么时候礼貌尤其重要？
items.answer: I'd say when meeting someone for the first time or asking for help. A polite greeting and a little patience can make the other person feel more comfortable.
items.ideaZh: 第一次见面或求助时尤其重要；问候和耐心帮助对方放松。

items.question: What kinds of things make you feel tired?
items.questionZh: 什么事情会让你疲惫？
items.answer: Long periods of studying at my computer can make me tired. It's especially noticeable when I've stayed up late, because concentrating the next day takes much more effort.
items.ideaZh: 电脑前学习过久、熬夜后注意力更费力；作息细节是补充。
items.vocab: because — 因为

items.question: How do you keep yourself awake when you feel very tired?
items.questionZh: 很累时你怎样保持清醒？
items.answer: If I still have something important to finish, I get up and walk around for a few minutes. Fresh air helps, but I try to rest properly afterwards.
items.ideaZh: 急需完成任务时起身走动、透气；之后仍安排休息，不把提神当作长期替代睡眠。
items.vocab: important — 重要的
items.provenance: 基于已确认背景与旧素材拟写；其余日常偏好、人物及时间细节为可调整补充，见中文思路。

items.question: Do you hang out with your friends when you are tired?
items.questionZh: 疲惫时你还会和朋友出去吗？
items.answer: It depends how tired I am. I might still meet a friend for a quiet meal, but I'd probably skip a long basketball game if I felt completely worn out.
items.ideaZh: 看疲劳程度：可以安静吃饭，太累就不打长时间篮球。
items.vocab: skip — 不参加或略过；worn out — 筋疲力尽的
items.provenance: 学习、篮球和游戏背景真实；具体疲劳频率与应对方式为日常补充。

items.question: Do you think people feel less tired as they get older?
items.questionZh: 你认为人越老越不容易累吗？
items.answer: Not necessarily. I think it depends on sleep, health and how busy someone is. An older person with a relaxed routine might feel better than an exhausted student.
items.ideaZh: 不一概而论，看睡眠、身体和忙碌程度；年长者轻松时可能比疲惫学生状态好。

items.question: When do you usually feel tired?
items.questionZh: 你通常什么时候感到疲惫？
items.answer: Usually after a long day of classes or a difficult study session. Basketball can make me physically tired too, but that's a more enjoyable kind of tiredness because I feel relaxed afterwards.
items.ideaZh: 上课或学习很久会累；打球也会身体疲劳，但之后心情放松。

items.provenance: 学习、篮球和游戏背景真实；具体疲劳频率与应对方式为日常补充。

items.question: What do street markets sell?
items.questionZh: 街头市场通常卖什么？
items.answer: The ones I've seen sell fresh vegetables, fruit, snacks and inexpensive everyday items. I like how you can walk past different stalls and see everything quite close up.
items.ideaZh: 根据见过的市场列蔬果、小吃、日用品；近距离逛摊位。
items.vocab: different — 不同的

items.question: Do you prefer to go shopping in the shopping mall or the street market?
items.questionZh: 你更喜欢商场还是街头市场购物？
items.answer: For electronics, I prefer a shopping mall because I can compare products and ask staff questions. For snacks or a casual walk, a street market is more interesting.
items.ideaZh: 按商品区分：电子产品选商场，小吃和闲逛选市场；呼应耳机素材。

items.question: When was the last time you went to a street market?
items.questionZh: 你最近一次去街头市场是什么时候？
items.answer: I went to one near home last weekend with a family member. We bought some vegetables and looked at the food stalls. It was a fairly ordinary shopping trip.
items.ideaZh: 上周末和家人去家附近买菜、看小吃；时间同行者和经历全部为新增草稿。
items.provenance: 基于已确认背景与旧素材拟写；其余日常偏好、人物及时间细节为可调整补充，见中文思路。

items.question: Are there many street markets in China?
items.questionZh: 中国有很多街头市场吗？
items.answer: I've seen quite a few, especially around residential areas. They seem useful for everyday shopping, although I wouldn't assume every city or neighbourhood has the same kind of market.
items.ideaZh: 只据个人观察说居民区见到不少，不编全国普及率。
items.vocab: useful — 有用的

items.question: Do you find it easy to remember people's names?
items.questionZh: 你觉得记住别人的名字容易吗？
items.answer: It's easier when I spend some time talking with the person. If it's just a quick introduction in a large group, I'm much more likely to forget.
items.ideaZh: 深入聊过就容易，群体中匆匆介绍则容易忘。
items.vocab: introduction — 介绍；likely — 可能的
items.provenance: 记名字习惯与感受为日常补充。

items.question: What do you do to remember a person's name?
items.questionZh: 你会用什么方法记住一个人的名字？
items.answer: I try to use the person's name naturally during the conversation and connect it with something we discussed. That works better for me than repeating the name silently once.
items.ideaZh: 聊天时自然使用名字，再与谈话内容关联起来。
items.vocab: connect — 联系起来；silently — 默默地
items.provenance: 记名字习惯与感受为日常补充。

items.question: Have you ever felt bad because you couldn't remember someone's name?
items.questionZh: 你有没有因为记不住名字而难过？
items.answer: Yes, once I recognised someone from class but couldn't remember his name. I felt a bit awkward and apologised. Luckily, he didn't seem bothered when I asked again.
items.ideaZh: 用同学名字想不起的小尴尬，礼貌道歉并再问；经历为补充草稿。
items.vocab: remember — 记住
items.provenance: 基于已确认背景与旧素材拟写；其余日常偏好、人物及时间细节为可调整补充，见中文思路。

items.question: How do you feel when people can't remember your name?
items.questionZh: 别人记不住你的名字时，你感觉如何？
items.answer: I don't mind very much, especially when we've only met once. I forget names too, so I usually just tell them again and try not to make it awkward.
items.ideaZh: 不太介意，尤其只见过一次时；再告诉对方，避免尴尬。
items.vocab: mind — 介意；awkward — 尴尬的
items.provenance: 记名字习惯与感受为日常补充。

items.question: Is it important to remember people's names?
items.questionZh: 记住别人的名字重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, especially when you meet someone regularly. Using their name shows that you paid attention and helps the conversation feel more personal. It doesn't have to be perfect, though.

items.question: Do you prefer sad or happy music?
items.questionZh: 你更喜欢悲伤还是欢快的音乐？
items.answer: Usually happy music, especially when I'm walking or taking a break. I sometimes enjoy a sad song too, but I wouldn't choose a whole playlist of sad music when I'm already tired.
items.ideaZh: 通常选欢快音乐；偶尔听伤感歌，但疲劳时不想整单都听伤感的。

items.question: Does happy music make you feel more excited?
items.questionZh: 欢快的音乐会让你更兴奋吗？
items.answer: Yes, it can lift my mood, particularly if it has a strong beat. I might listen to it before going out, but I prefer something calmer when I'm studying.
items.ideaZh: 会，强节奏能改善心情；学习时则选更平静的音乐。

items.question: Is it easy to learn music?
items.questionZh: 学音乐容易吗？
items.answer: Learning a simple song can be enjoyable, but performing well takes practice. I think keeping time and controlling your voice are harder than they look when you watch a confident musician.
items.ideaZh: 简单入门愉快，节奏和声音控制要练，不以欣赏经验冒充专业技能。

items.question: Do you take music lessons at school?
items.questionZh: 你现在在学校上音乐课吗？
items.answer: Not at the moment. My current courses are mainly connected with computer science. I had ordinary music lessons when I was younger, but now I mostly listen for enjoyment.
items.ideaZh: 现在计算机课程为主，不上音乐课；小时候普通课为补充。

items.question: Do you wear a watch?
items.questionZh: 你戴手表吗？
items.answer: Not usually. I normally check the time on my phone. I might wear a watch for a special occasion, but it's not something I feel I need every day.

items.answer: No, I haven't, as far as I remember. Most gifts I've received have been more practical things for studying or everyday life. A simple watch could still be a nice gift.

items.question: Why do some people wear expensive watches?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人戴昂贵的手表？
items.answer: Some people like the design or the way a watch is made. Others may see it as a sign of success. Personally, I'd care more about comfort and whether I liked it.

items.question: Do you think it is important to wear a watch? Why?
items.questionZh: 你认为戴手表重要吗？为什么？
items.answer: Not for everyone. It's useful if you want to check the time quickly without taking out your phone, but I manage quite well without wearing one regularly.
items.ideaZh: 不对所有人都重要；看时间快是优点，但自己不戴也方便生活。

items.question: What kind of parks and gardens did you like when you were a child?
items.questionZh: 你小时候喜欢什么样的公园花园？
items.answer: I liked parks with open areas where I could run around. Trees and places to sit were nice too, but having room to play mattered more to me than formal gardens.
items.ideaZh: 喜欢能跑玩的开阔公园，树荫座椅也好；童年偏好为补充。

items.questionZh: 你现在喜欢去公园和花园吗？
items.answer: Yes, although now I prefer walking and talking to someone rather than running around. A park is a good place to take a break from studying and computer screens.

items.questionZh: 你觉得城市应该有更多公园和花园吗？
items.answer: Yes, especially small parks close to where people live. I don't always have time for a long trip, so a nearby green space would be useful for a short evening walk.

items.topic: Parks and gardens 公园与花园
items.question: Is there a famous park or garden that you want to visit?
items.questionZh: 有没有你想去的著名公园或花园？
items.answer: I'd like to visit the Summer Palace in Beijing. I've seen pictures of its gardens and lake, and it seems like somewhere I could walk slowly and enjoy the surroundings.

items.questionZh: 你小时候是整洁的人吗？
items.answer: Not always. I often left books or toys out and needed reminders from my parents. I've become more careful now that I have study materials and computer equipment to look after.

items.question: Are you a tidy person now?
items.questionZh: 你现在是整洁的人吗？
items.answer: Yes, especially my desk, because I find it easier to study when I can find everything. I'm not perfectly tidy all the time, but I dislike a completely messy workspace.

items.question: What do you think of those who don't care about tidiness?
items.questionZh: 你怎么看待不在乎整洁的人？
items.answer: I'm fairly relaxed about a little mess, but shared spaces are different. If someone's things make it difficult for others to study or move around, they should tidy up.

items.question: What do you think of those who are overly concerned about tidiness?
items.questionZh: 你怎么看待过分在意整洁的人？
items.answer: I understand wanting a clean space, but it can become tiring if every small object has to be perfect. I'd rather keep things comfortable and usable without worrying all the time.

items.question: How often do you wear headphones?
items.questionZh: 你多久戴一次耳机？
items.answer: Most days, usually when I'm listening to English or playing games. I don't wear them continuously, though. Sometimes I prefer a quiet room and a proper break from any sound.

items.question: Do you think headphones are useful?
items.questionZh: 你觉得耳机有用吗？
items.answer: Definitely. I can listen to something without disturbing people nearby, and it's easier to hear the details. They're particularly useful when I'm practising English listening or watching a video.

items.questionZh: 什么场合人们不应该戴耳机？
items.answer: I wouldn't use them while crossing a road or when someone is talking to me. In those situations, I want to hear what's happening around me and pay attention.

items.question: What do you usually do when there is a traffic jam?
items.questionZh: 堵车时你通常做什么？
items.answer: As a passenger, I usually listen to music or talk with whoever I'm travelling with. If we're going to be late, I send a message so the person waiting knows.
items.ideaZh: 作为乘客听歌或聊天；预计迟到就发消息告知等候者。
items.vocab: traffic jam — 交通堵塞；whoever — 无论谁
items.provenance: 童年乘车、乘客偏好和未来购车意愿为日常草稿；不编造已有驾照。

items.question: Do you like shopping?
items.questionZh: 你喜欢购物吗？
items.answer: Sometimes, especially if I'm buying something I actually need, like headphones. I don't enjoy walking around shops for hours without a purpose, though. I usually prefer a fairly short trip.
items.ideaZh: 买确实需要的东西时喜欢，但不爱漫无目的逛很久。
items.vocab: purpose — 目的；headphones — 耳机

items.question: How often do you go shopping?
items.questionZh: 你多久购物一次？
items.answer: I buy small everyday things when I need them, but I only go on a longer shopping trip occasionally, perhaps once a month. I try to plan larger purchases.
items.ideaZh: 小物按需买，较长的购物行程偶尔一次；大额购买会先计划。
items.vocab: purchases — 购买的物品或购买行为；occasionally — 偶尔

items.question: Do you prefer online shopping or in-store shopping?
items.questionZh: 你更喜欢网购还是实体店购物？
items.answer: It depends on the item. Online shopping is convenient for simple things, but I prefer a shop for shoes or headphones because I can check the fit or comfort.
items.ideaZh: 看商品：普通小物网购方便，鞋和耳机更想现场试舒适度。
items.vocab: in-store shopping — 实体店购物；fit — 合身或合脚程度
items.provenance: 耳机购物沿用 P2 新增故事；频率、衣服退货属于日常补充。

items.question: Do you compare prices when you shop? Why?
items.questionZh: 购物时你会比价吗？为什么？
items.answer: Yes, especially for electronics. Comparing a few options helps me understand what I'm paying for. I don't spend hours checking a very cheap item, but bigger purchases deserve more thought.
items.ideaZh: 电子产品会比价看价值，小东西不耗太久，较大购买多考虑。

items.question: Is it difficult for you to make choices when you shop?
items.questionZh: 你购物时难以作选择吗？
items.answer: Sometimes, when several products look almost the same. I usually decide on a budget and the features I actually need. That narrows the choice and stops me comparing endlessly.
items.ideaZh: 相似选项多会难选，先预算和需求再筛，避免无限比较。
items.vocab: budget — 预算

items.question: Do you think expensive products are always better than cheaper ones?
items.questionZh: 你认为贵的产品总比便宜的好吗？
items.answer: No. Sometimes you pay extra for a name or an appearance rather than better performance. I prefer checking how well something meets my needs instead of judging it by price alone.
items.ideaZh: 不一定，可能为品牌外观付费；看是否满足需求。
items.vocab: rather than — 而不是

items.question: Have you ever returned anything you bought online?
items.questionZh: 你退过网购的东西吗？
items.answer: Yes, I once returned a T-shirt because the size wasn't right. The process was fairly straightforward, but it reminded me to check the size information more carefully next time.
items.ideaZh: 用T恤尺码不合的草稿，退货不难，也提醒以后认真查尺码。
items.vocab: returned — 退货；straightforward — 简单明了的

items.question: What kind of clothes do you like to wear?
items.questionZh: 你喜欢穿什么衣服？
items.answer: Mostly T-shirts, comfortable trousers and trainers. That works well for university life and makes it easy to move around. I dress a little more carefully for special occasions.
items.ideaZh: 平常穿T恤、舒适裤子和运动鞋，适合校园活动；特殊场合更讲究。
items.vocab: trainers — 运动鞋；occasions — 场合
items.provenance: 日常穿衣与颜色偏好为合理补充，按海口生活背景拟写。

items.question: Do you wear different clothes on the weekend?
items.questionZh: 你周末会穿不同的衣服吗？
items.answer: There isn't a huge difference. I wear casual clothes for classes and at weekends. The main change is that I put on sports clothes when I'm going to play basketball.
items.ideaZh: 差别不大，都穿休闲装；打篮球时会换运动服。
items.vocab: weekdays — 工作日；sports clothes — 运动服
items.provenance: 日常穿衣与颜色偏好为合理补充，按海口生活背景拟写。

items.question: Do you buy clothes because of the brand? What brands do you usually buy?
items.questionZh: 你因为品牌买衣服吗？通常买什么品牌？
items.answer: Not usually. I care more about comfort and fit, so I don't stick to one particular brand. If a basic T-shirt feels good and the price is reasonable, that's enough.
items.ideaZh: 不固定品牌，直接说明没偏好；舒适合身、价合理即可。

items.question: What colours of clothes do you dislike?
items.questionZh: 你不喜欢什么颜色的衣服？
items.answer: I don't really like very bright yellow or orange on myself. They draw more attention than I want. I usually feel more comfortable wearing simple, darker colours instead.
items.ideaZh: 明确回答不喜欢亮黄橙，原因是太抢眼；不能只说喜欢深色。

items.question: Have you learned about outer space and stars?
items.questionZh: 你了解过外太空和星星吗？
items.answer: Only the basics at school and through a few videos. I know a little about the planets, but I'm not an expert. Pictures of space often make me curious to learn more.
items.ideaZh: 只学过基础，也看过一些视频；不装专家，太空图片会激发好奇。

items.question: Do you like science fiction movies? Why?
items.questionZh: 你喜欢科幻电影吗？为什么？
items.answer: Yes, when they have an interesting story as well as good visual effects. I enjoy imagining a different world, but I still need characters I care about to stay interested.
items.ideaZh: 喜欢有好故事和视觉效果的，也需要让自己关心的人物才能看下去。
items.vocab: visual effects — 视觉特效；characters — 角色
items.provenance: 太空学习、科幻喜好与旅行意愿为补充；不声称看过特定影片。

items.question: Do you want to know more about outer space?
items.questionZh: 你想进一步了解太空吗？
items.answer: Yes, especially how people study places that are so far away. I'd prefer a simple explanation or documentary first, because a very technical book would probably be difficult for me.
items.ideaZh: 想知道人们如何研究遥远的地方，偏好简单讲解或纪录片入门。

items.question: Do you want to go into outer space in the future?
items.questionZh: 你将来想去太空吗？
items.answer: The idea is exciting, but I don't think I'd choose it myself. I'd worry about the training and the journey. For now, I'm happy learning about space from Earth.
items.ideaZh: 想法令人兴奋，但担心训练和旅程，更愿意在地球上了解它。

items.question: Do you like science?
items.questionZh: 你喜欢科学吗？
items.answer: Yes, especially when it explains how something works. Since I study computer science, I enjoy seeing a clear idea turn into something practical, rather than just memorising a definition.
items.ideaZh: 喜欢理解原理，尤其把计算机知识变成实际用途，而非只背定义。

items.question: When did you start to learn about science?
items.questionZh: 你什么时候开始学科学？
items.answer: I started with basic science lessons in primary school. Simple activities caught my attention more than reading alone, because I could actually see what happened when something changed.
items.ideaZh: 小学开始；能直接观察变化的小活动，比只阅读更吸引自己。

items.question: Which science subject is interesting to you?
items.questionZh: 你对哪个科学学科感兴趣？
items.answer: Computer science interests me most because it's my major. I like learning how a program follows instructions, and it's satisfying when I can use that knowledge to solve a problem.
items.ideaZh: 最喜欢本专业计算机科学，理解程序运行并用知识解决问题很有成就感。

items.question: What kinds of interesting things have you done with science?
items.questionZh: 你做过哪些与科学有关的有趣事情？
items.answer: I've made small programs for class tasks. They weren't complicated, but getting a program to work after fixing mistakes was enjoyable. It helped connect what I learned with something I could test.

items.question: Do you like watching science TV programmes?
items.questionZh: 你喜欢看科普电视节目吗？
items.answer: Sometimes, if they explain an idea clearly and use everyday examples. I lose interest when the language becomes too technical, so I prefer programmes aimed at ordinary viewers.

items.question: Do Chinese people often visit science museums?
items.questionZh: 中国人经常参观科技馆吗？
items.answer: I'm not sure how often people go overall. I know some families and schools arrange visits, but among my friends, watching a science video is a more common activity.

items.question: Describe a place you went to that was noisy.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你去过的很吵的地方。
cueCard: And explain how you felt about this place being so noisy.
cueCardZh: 说明你对那里如此吵闹的感受
items.answer:
A noisy place I've been to is a shopping mall in Haikou. I went there with my girlfriend on a weekend afternoon because I wanted to look for a pair of headphones.

The shops were having a sales event, so there were people everywhere. Some stores were playing loud music, and staff were speaking through microphones. Near the food area, I could also hear children calling to their parents and people moving chairs around.

We walked around a few electronics shops and compared different headphones. However, it was quite hard to talk. Sometimes my girlfriend had to repeat what she had said because I couldn't hear her clearly. I don't mind a bit of background noise, but several sounds together can be tiring. After buying the headphones, we found a quieter place to sit. I was glad to take a break. Next time, I'd probably go on a weekday morning instead.

We walked around a few electronics shops and compared different headphones. However, it was quite hard to talk. Sometimes my girlfriend had to repeat what she had said because I couldn't hear her clearly. I don't mind a bit of background noise, but several sounds together can be tiring. After buying the headphones, we found a quieter place to sit. I was glad to take a break. Next time, I'd probably go on a weekday morning instead.
cluesZh: 地点与目的：周末下午和女朋友去海口商场，想买一副耳机。
噪声来源：促销人多，店铺音乐和员工麦克风声，加上餐饮区孩子喊人、挪椅子的声音。
过程与感受：比较耳机时很难交谈，女朋友要重复说话；多种噪声叠加令人疲惫，买完去安静处休息，下次考虑工作日上午去。
translationsZh: 我们逛了几家电子产品店，比较不同的耳机。不过，当时说话很费劲。有时女朋友不得不重复刚说过的话，因为我听不清。我不介意一点背景噪声，但好几种声音混在一起会让人累。买完耳机后，我们找了个安静些的地方坐下。能休息一下，我很高兴。下次我可能会改在工作日早上去。
items.provenance: 海口商场购物、时间、同行者和噪声细节为拟写；不指定不存在的店名。
items.extension: The noise also made it difficult to test the headphones properly. I had to ask the shop assistant to help me find a quieter corner.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：噪声也妨碍试听耳机，只好请店员帮忙找较安静的角落。

items.question: What kinds of places are usually noisy in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家哪些地方通常很吵？
items.answer: Busy markets, stations and shopping centres can be noisy because many people are moving around and talking at once. Construction adds another kind of noise. I notice the difference most when I leave a crowded commercial area and walk into a quieter residential street.
items.ideaZh: 列市场车站商场及工地；解释人群与机器声音，再用离开商业区的体验展开。
items.vocab: because — 因为；people — 人们

items.question: In which places is noise generally not allowed or discouraged?
items.questionZh: 哪些地方通常不允许或不鼓励噪音？
items.answer: Libraries and hospital waiting areas usually encourage people to keep their voices down. Someone may be concentrating or feeling unwell, so a loud conversation can affect them quite directly. Clear signs help, but people also need to consider the purpose of the space.
items.ideaZh: 图书馆医院需安静，关系到专注和休息；标牌之外也要体谅空间用途。
items.vocab: clear — 清楚的；help — 帮助
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: How do people usually respond when they encounter noisy behaviour in public?
items.questionZh: 遇到公共场所吵闹行为时，人们通常怎样反应？
items.answer: Some people politely ask the person to lower their voice, while others move away because they want to avoid an argument. If the noise continues, asking a member of staff can be more effective. The response depends on how serious the disturbance is.
items.ideaZh: 礼貌提醒、挪开、找工作人员；选择取决于干扰程度，不鼓励直接冲突。
items.vocab: because — 因为；people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: What do people usually do when they feel noisy?
items.questionZh: 受到噪音干扰时，人们通常会怎么做？
items.answer: If you mean being bothered by noise, people often try to find a quieter spot or close a window. Headphones can help in some situations too. If another person is causing the problem, a polite request may work better than simply trying to ignore it.
items.ideaZh: 先自然澄清原题feel noisy的意思，再说换位置关窗耳机或礼貌提醒。
items.vocab: help — 帮助；people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Why do some people dislike noise, while others seem to enjoy it?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人讨厌噪音，有些人却喜欢？
items.answer: People connect the same sound with different experiences. Loud music might feel exciting at a party but annoying when someone is trying to sleep. Personality matters too, although I think the situation and whether people can control the sound often make a bigger difference.
items.ideaZh: 同样音乐在派对和睡觉时感受不同；性格、场景及控制权共同影响。
items.vocab: different — 不同的；people — 人们

items.question: Does a quiet environment help people concentrate more effectively? Why?
items.questionZh: 安静环境有助于专注吗？为什么？
items.answer: Usually, yes, because there are fewer sounds competing for attention. That's useful for reading or solving a difficult problem. However, some people prefer gentle background music. I'd distinguish a predictable, quiet sound from sudden conversations that interrupt a person's train of thought.
items.ideaZh: 减少注意力竞争有利阅读解题；稳定轻音乐可能有用，突然谈话更干扰。
items.vocab: attention — 注意力；useful — 有用的

items.question: Describe a place you enjoy its nature.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你喜欢其自然环境的地方。
cueCard: How you found out about this place
And explain why you enjoy going to this natural place.
cueCardZh: 说明你为什么喜欢去那里
items.answer:
A natural place I really enjoyed visiting was Dadonghai Beach in Sanya. I went there with my girlfriend, and it's a place I'd happily visit again when I have the chance.

Before the trip, I had seen some photos of the beach online. The clear water looked attractive, so we decided to include it in our visit. When we arrived, we could see the sea, the sand and people enjoying time by the water. I took lots of photos of my girlfriend, and then we walked slowly along the beach together.

What I enjoyed most was the sea breeze. It felt cool and comfortable, and being there helped me stop thinking about my usual study tasks. We didn't need an expensive activity or a busy schedule. Just walking, talking and looking at the water made the trip feel relaxing. That's why this natural place has stayed in my mind.

如何得知和看到什么：出发前看网上照片，抵达后看到海水、沙滩和人们。拍女朋友、慢慢散步是真实核心，信息来源和景物细节为补充。
原因和感受：保留the sea breeze，凉爽海风帮助放松；不需要复杂活动，一起散步聊天看海就很好。

items.extension: If I went back, I'd leave some time without taking pictures, so we could simply enjoy the place and each other's company.
items.extensionZh: 再去会留一些不拍照的时间，单纯欣赏环境、享受陪伴。

items.question: What kind of people like to visit natural places?
items.questionZh: 什么样的人喜欢去自然地点？
items.answer: All sorts of people can enjoy it, including families, photographers and people who want quiet time. Their activities may differ: some like a challenging walk, while others prefer sitting by the sea. I wouldn't connect enjoying nature with one age group or personality type.
items.ideaZh: 家庭、摄影者、想安静的人都可能喜欢，方式不同，不能限定一种年龄或性格。

items.question: What are the differences between a natural place and a city?
items.questionZh: 自然地点与城市有什么区别？
items.answer: Natural places usually offer more open space, plants and opportunities to slow down. Cities provide convenient transport, services and more activities, but can feel crowded. The difference isn't absolute, though. A well-designed park can give city residents some of the benefits of nature.
items.ideaZh: 比较环境节奏与服务便利，再补城市公园能缩小差异。

items.question: Do you think that going to the park is the only way to get close to nature?
items.questionZh: 去公园是亲近自然的唯一方式吗？
items.answer: No, people can walk by the sea, go hiking or look after plants at home. A park is convenient, especially in a city, but the important part is paying attention to the natural environment. Even a small garden can provide that connection.
items.ideaZh: 海边徒步家中种植都可；公园方便但并非唯一，关键在观察和接触。

items.question: What can people gain from going to natural places?
items.questionZh: 去自然地点能让人获得什么？
items.answer: People can get a break from screens and a chance to move around. They may also notice things they usually ignore, such as changing light or birdsong. For me, those simple experiences help make a busy day feel less rushed and more balanced.
items.ideaZh: 屏幕休息、活动身体、注意小细节；以个人放松体验展开，不给医学保证。

items.question: Are there any wild animals in the city?
items.questionZh: 城市里有野生动物吗？
items.answer: Yes, even a busy city can have wild birds and insects, particularly around trees or water. They may be less noticeable than animals in a forest, but they're still part of the environment. Keeping some green spaces helps people notice and protect that wildlife.
items.ideaZh: 鸟和昆虫也是野生动物，不把流浪猫狗等同野生物种；绿地提供接触机会。

items.question: Do you think it is a good idea to let animals stay in local parks for people to see?
items.questionZh: 让动物生活在本地公园供人观看好吗？
items.answer: If local wildlife is living there naturally, it can be a good learning opportunity. But I wouldn't support bringing animals into an unsuitable park just for visitors' entertainment. People should keep a respectful distance, and the animals' needs should matter more than getting close photographs.
items.ideaZh: 区分自然栖息和为娱乐而关养；保持距离，照顾动物需求。

items.question: Describe a time when you had to wait for something special to happen.
items.questionZh: 描述一次等待特别事情发生的经历。
cueCard: Why you had to wait for it
What you did while you were waiting
And explain how you felt about waiting for this special thing to happen.
items.answer:
A time I waited for something special was before a short trip to Sanya with my girlfriend. We were going to visit Dadonghai Beach, and I was really looking forward to spending time together.

We had decided to go at the weekend because we both had things to finish during the week. That meant I couldn't simply leave as soon as I felt excited about the idea. While waiting, I finished my coursework, looked at what we might need and packed a small bag. I also checked that my phone had enough space for pictures.

The wait felt longer than it really was because I kept imagining the beach. I wanted a break from my normal routine, but I tried not to spend the whole week thinking about it. When we finally went, I took photos of my girlfriend and we walked along the sand. I felt that the anticipation had made the simple trip even more enjoyable.

cluesZh: 点题：等待和女朋友去三亚大东海。旅行背景真实，“出发前等待”事件为新草稿。
为什么等、等时做什么：工作日各有任务，只能周末去；完成作业、准备小包、检查照片空间，全部为合理拟写。
感受：因期待而觉得时间慢，仍把任务做完；到海边拍照散步后，期待让旅行更有乐趣。
items.provenance: 沿用真实三亚旅行背景；考试结束后等待周末出行、提前整理物品和期待情绪均为新拟。不是已确认的等待经历。
items.extension: Having something pleasant ahead also gave me a reason to finish my work on time instead of leaving it until the last moment.
items.extensionZh: 等待的期待也推动自己及时完成作业。

items.question: What are some everyday situations when people have to wait?
items.questionZh: 生活中哪些时候人们必须等待？
items.answer: People wait for buses, appointments, food and replies to messages. Some waiting is unavoidable because a service can only help a certain number of people at once. A clear estimate of the waiting time makes these situations easier to manage than an unexplained delay.
items.ideaZh: 列交通预约餐食消息；服务容量导致等待，明确时长比不确定更易接受。
items.vocab: manage — 管理应对；clear — 清楚的

items.question: Why do many people really dislike waiting?
items.questionZh: 为什么很多人不喜欢等待？
items.answer: Waiting can make people feel that their time is being controlled by someone else. It's particularly frustrating when they don't know what's happening or have another commitment. I think uncertainty is often the real problem, rather than a short delay by itself.
items.ideaZh: 核心是不确定和失去时间控制，尤其后面有安排；不只是不愿等几分钟。
items.vocab: rather than — 而不是；frustrating — 令人沮丧的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Do you think adults are better at waiting than children?
items.questionZh: 成年人比儿童更善于等待吗？
items.answer: Generally, adults have more experience of unavoidable delays and more ways to occupy themselves. Children may find an unexplained wait harder to understand. Still, adults can become impatient too, especially when stressed. A meaningful activity and a clear explanation can help both groups.
items.ideaZh: 成人经验策略更多，儿童难理解；压力下成人也急，两者都受益于解释和活动。

items.question: Describe a time when you received very good service from a shop, a store or a company.
items.questionZh: 描述一次在商店或公司得到优质服务的经历。
cueCard: Which shop/store or company it was
Why you thought this service was so good
And explain how you felt after receiving such good service.
cueCardZh: 说明接受服务后的感受
items.answer:
I received really good service at an electronics shop in a shopping mall in Haikou. I went there with my girlfriend a few months ago to buy some headphones.

I had saved up for them, so I wanted to choose carefully. The shop assistant asked what I would use them for and how much I wanted to spend. I explained that I needed them for studying English and playing games. He showed me a few options within my budget and explained the differences in simple language.

What impressed me was that he didn't push me towards the most expensive pair. He let me try them on and gave me time to decide. Before I paid, he also explained what to do if there was a problem. I left feeling satisfied and comfortable with my choice. Good service, to me, means helping someone find what suits them, rather than making them feel under pressure.

I had saved up for them, so I wanted to choose carefully. The shop assistant asked what I would use them for and how much I wanted to spend. I explained that I needed them for studying English and playing games. He showed me a few options within my budget and explained the differences in simple language.

What impressed me was that he didn't push me towards the most expensive pair. He let me try them on and gave me time to decide. Before I paid, he also explained what to do if there was a problem. I left feeling satisfied and comfortable with my choice. Good service, to me, means helping someone find what suits them, rather than making them feel under pressure.
cluesZh: 地点与时间：几个月前，和女朋友去海口商场的电子产品店买耳机。
服务过程：我攒钱后想慎重挑选；店员询问用途和预算，用简单语言比较适合听英语、打游戏的几款耳机。
好在哪里：不强推最贵款，允许试戴、留出决定时间并解释售后；尊重需求，让我满意且没有压力。
translationsZh: 让我印象深刻的是，他没有催我买最贵的那副。他让我试戴，也给我时间作决定。付款前，他还解释了如果出现问题该怎么办。离开时我很满意，也对自己的选择感到踏实。对我来说，好服务意味着帮助顾客找到适合自己的东西，而不是让他们感到压力。
items.provenance: 与 N08 同一次耳机购买；店员说明、耐心试用及售后告知为新增情节。
items.extension: I would consider going back to that shop because I felt respected. That kind of patient explanation is especially helpful when you are buying technology.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：感到被尊重，所以会考虑再去；购买科技产品时，耐心解释尤其有帮助。

items.question: Do you think the most expensive shops or stores usually provide the best service?
items.questionZh: 最贵的商店通常服务最好吗？
items.answer: Not necessarily. An expensive shop may have more staff and provide personal attention, but price doesn't guarantee a helpful attitude. A small shop can offer excellent service if the owner listens carefully and explains things honestly. Training and management matter as much as the price range.
items.ideaZh: 贵店资源可能多，但态度不由价格保证；小店倾听诚实也可好服务。
items.vocab: attention — 注意力
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Why is it that service in shops or stores is sometimes not good?
items.questionZh: 为什么有时商店服务不好？
items.answer: Staff may be serving too many customers, or they may not have received enough training. Poor communication can also create problems, such as promising something the shop can't deliver. I wouldn't always blame one employee; the way a business organises its work matters too.
items.ideaZh: 人手培训承诺沟通都有影响；不能把系统问题全归咎某员工。
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: How important do you think good service is to most customers?
items.questionZh: 好服务对顾客有多重要？
items.answer: It's especially important when customers need advice or have a problem after buying something. A patient explanation can make them feel confident about their choice. Good service also gives people a reason to return, even if another shop offers a slightly lower price.
items.ideaZh: 咨询售后最重要，解释帮助作决定，信任带来回头客。
items.vocab: patient — 有耐心的；confident — 自信的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: How is dealing with customers face-to-face different from dealing with them on the phone?
items.questionZh: 面对面服务和电话服务有什么不同？
items.answer: Face-to-face communication allows staff to see expressions and demonstrate a product. On the phone, they have to depend more on clear questions and careful listening. However, a phone call is convenient when the customer can't travel, so each method can suit a different situation.
items.ideaZh: 当面可看表情演示；电话靠清楚提问倾听，方便远程处理。

items.question: What personal qualities do customer service staff need in order to handle complaints well?
items.questionZh: 处理投诉的客服需要什么个人品质？
items.answer: They need patience, clear communication and the ability to stay calm. An upset customer wants to feel understood before hearing a solution. Staff also need to be honest about what they can change, because making an unrealistic promise usually creates another complaint later.
items.ideaZh: 耐心冷静清楚表达，先理解再解决，承诺必须实际。
items.vocab: patience — 耐心；clear — 清楚的

items.question: Do you think working in customer service would be an enjoyable job?
items.questionZh: 客服工作会令人愉快吗？
items.answer: It could be satisfying for someone who enjoys helping people and solving practical problems. However, repeated complaints can be tiring, especially without support from management. I think the working environment makes a big difference; reasonable staffing and clear procedures can make the job much more enjoyable.
items.ideaZh: 助人解决问题有成就感，但持续投诉累；管理支持和合理人手影响体验。
items.vocab: practical — 实用的；clear — 清楚的

items.question: Describe an exciting book that you enjoy reading.
items.questionZh: 描述一本你喜欢读的令人兴奋的书。
cueCard: What type of book it was
And explain why the book was so exciting.
cueCardZh: 说明它为什么令人兴奋
items.answer:
An exciting book I enjoyed was a collection of short stories called Aesop's Fables. I borrowed it from a library because I wanted something easy to read after a busy period of studying.

The stories use animals to explore human behaviour. One I remember is The Tortoise and the Hare. They have a race, and the hare seems certain to win because it moves much faster. But it becomes overconfident and stops to rest, while the tortoise continues moving towards the finish.

What made the book exciting for me was waiting to see how each small problem would end. Even a short story could surprise me, and I often wanted to read just one more. The race was especially interesting because the expected winner didn't win. I liked having both a clear story and something to think about afterwards. It reminded me that steady effort can matter more than a strong start.

内容：龟兔赛跑，快的兔子自信停下，慢的乌龟继续前进。
兴奋点：想知道结局、短篇也有反转、忍不住再读一篇；龟兔结果出乎预期，关联持续努力。

items.extension: I sometimes remember that message when I practise English. Making a little progress each day seems more useful than relying only on an early advantage.
items.extensionZh: 延伸至练英语时持续练习，而非只靠起步优势。

items.question: What kinds of books do people in your country like reading?
items.questionZh: 你们国家人们喜欢读什么书？
items.answer: I'm not sure about national rankings, but people around me read novels, study materials and books related to personal interests. The preferred format varies too: some enjoy paper books, while others read on a phone. A student's choices may reflect current courses as much as general trends.
items.ideaZh: 不猜全国排名，谈身边小说、学习资料与兴趣书，纸书电子书和课程需求也不同。
items.vocab: rankings — 排名；format — 形式
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: What kinds of books do young people and old people enjoy?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与年长者喜欢什么书？
items.answer: Some younger readers enjoy fantasy or books connected with new interests, while some older readers prefer history or familiar authors. But I'd avoid treating age as a rule. A person's background, interests and available reading time can explain their choices better than age alone.
items.ideaZh: 可以举年龄偏好例子，但不刻板；背景兴趣时间往往更能解释。
items.vocab: enjoy — 享受喜欢
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Do boys and girls like the same kinds of books?
items.questionZh: 男孩女孩喜欢相同类型的书吗？
items.answer: There's plenty of overlap. A good adventure or an interesting character can appeal to anyone. Some choices may be shaped by what friends recommend or what publishers promote, but I don't think gender reliably tells us what an individual reader will enjoy.
items.ideaZh: 兴趣有重叠，不用性别定规则；朋友推荐和接触渠道也影响。
items.vocab: enjoy — 享受喜欢
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Do you think it is very important to read the book before watching the movie version of it?
items.questionZh: 看改编电影前读原著很重要吗？
items.answer: They don't have to. Reading first can give more detail and leave room to imagine the characters, while a film may make someone interested in the book. I'd treat them as different versions of a story. Enjoying one doesn't require following a fixed order or judging every difference as a mistake.
items.ideaZh: 不必固定顺序，先读有想象和细节，先看也能激发阅读兴趣，版本差异不等于错误。
items.vocab: versions — 版本；characters — 人物
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: Are movies usually not as good as the books they are based on?
items.questionZh: 改编电影通常不如原著吗？
items.answer: Not always. A book can explore a character's thoughts in detail, while a film uses acting, sound and images to create its own effect. Some adaptations lose important parts, but others tell the story very well. I'd judge whether the film works on its own.
items.ideaZh: 书擅心理细节，电影用表演声音画面；改编可好可坏，单看表现。
items.vocab: important — 重要的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Can movies which are based on novels encourage people to read more?
items.questionZh: 小说改编电影能鼓励人读书吗？
items.answer: Yes, a film can introduce people to a story they wouldn't otherwise notice. If they enjoy the characters, they may read the book for more detail. However, some viewers feel satisfied with the film alone, so it creates an opportunity rather than guaranteeing more reading.
items.ideaZh: 电影打开故事入口，感兴趣就读细节；也有人只看电影，因此不是保证。

items.question: Describe a person who makes special objects (by hands or a technology).
items.questionZh: 描述一个用手或技术制作特别物件的人。
cueCard: And explain how you felt about this person.
cueCardZh: 说明你对这个人的感受
items.answer:
My grandfather, whom I have known all my life, is good at making small things by hand. He enjoys working with wood, and he often makes useful objects instead of buying new ones.

For example, he once made a simple phone stand for me. It was made from a small piece of wood left over from another job. He used basic hand tools and sandpaper to make the edges smooth. The design wasn't fancy, but it held my phone at a comfortable angle while I watched videos.

I think he is good at this because he is patient and pays attention to small details. Before making anything, he measures carefully and thinks about how it will be used. If something doesn't fit, he adjusts it instead of giving up. I enjoy watching him work because I can see an ordinary piece of material become something useful. The things he makes also feel personal, especially when he has made them for someone in the family.

If something doesn't fit, he adjusts it instead of giving up. I enjoy watching him work because I can see an ordinary piece of material become something useful. The things he makes also feel personal, especially when he has made them for someone in the family.
cluesZh: 人物与相识：爷爷，从小认识，喜欢木工并制作小物件；人物设定为旧草稿。
具体作品：用剩余木料、简单手工工具和砂纸做手机支架，边缘光滑、角度舒服，虽不花哨但实用。
能力与意义：耐心、注意细节，先测量和考虑用途，不合适就调整；普通材料变成用品，也承载对家人的心意。
translationsZh: 我觉得他擅长手工，是因为他有耐心，而且留意小细节。制作任何东西前，他都会仔细测量，想好它会怎样被使用。如果哪里不合适，他会调整，而不是放弃。我喜欢看他做东西，因为能看到一块普通材料变成有用的物品。他做的东西也很有个人心意，尤其是专门给家人做的时候。
items.provenance: 爷爷擅长做小木制品、给你做手机支架及制作细节为拟写。
items.extension: I still use the phone stand on my desk. It reminds me of him, and it is a small example of making good use of materials.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：现在桌上仍用这个支架，它让我想起爷爷，也体现了充分利用材料。

items.question: What kinds of handicrafts do young children usually enjoy making?
items.questionZh: 小孩子通常喜欢制作什么手工？
items.answer: Simple paper crafts, drawings and models are good examples. Children often enjoy tasks where they can choose colours and see a result fairly quickly. A complicated project may need adult help, but letting children make some decisions gives them a stronger sense of ownership.
items.ideaZh: 纸艺画画模型，颜色自由且快见成果；适当指导同时保留自主选择。

items.question: Do you think all children should learn about art at school?
items.questionZh: 所有儿童都应该在学校学艺术吗？
items.answer: Yes, they give children a chance to explore ideas and practise looking carefully. Art can also provide a different way to express feelings. The classes shouldn't only reward the neatest picture. If children feel free to experiment and improve, more of them can benefit from taking part.
items.ideaZh: 提供探索、观察与表达的机会，不应只奖励画得整齐，而应允许尝试和进步。
items.vocab: experiment — 尝试；express feelings — 表达情感

items.question: Why do some people prefer to stay quiet while making things?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人做东西时喜欢安静？
items.answer: Making something can require close attention, especially when a small mistake affects the whole result. Quiet helps some people follow the steps without interruption. Others simply find the activity relaxing. It doesn't necessarily mean they dislike company; they may prefer talking when the task is finished.
items.ideaZh: 精细工作需要专注，安静也有放松作用；不等于不喜欢人际交流。

items.question: How does the development of arts and culture affect society? Why?
items.questionZh: 艺术文化发展如何影响社会？为什么？
items.answer: It gives people ways to express ideas and understand experiences different from their own. Local music, stories and buildings can also connect a community with its past. These activities matter because a society needs shared experiences as well as practical services and economic activity.
items.ideaZh: 表达交流不同经验，连接社区历史；社会也需要共同体验，不只经济服务。

items.question: Describe a time you helped someone solve problems.
items.questionZh: 描述一次你帮助别人解决问题的经历。
cueCard: And explain how you felt about this experience.
items.answer:
A time I helped someone was when my girlfriend had trouble saving new photos on her phone. We were at home after a trip, and her phone kept showing a message saying there wasn't enough space.

She didn't want to delete the photos because many of them were memories of places we had visited together, including Dadonghai Beach. I study computer science, so I offered to help her organise them.

We connected the phone to my laptop and copied the photos into folders. Before removing anything from the phone, we checked that the copies opened properly and kept another backup. We also deleted some repeated pictures that she didn't want. It took a little time, but afterwards she could use her phone more comfortably. I felt useful and happy to help. It was a small problem, but it mattered to her, and I enjoyed using something I knew to make her day easier.

items.question: When do people usually ask others for help?
items.questionZh: 人们通常何时向别人求助？
items.answer: Usually when a problem is beyond their skills, time or resources. Someone might ask a friend about a computer issue or need support with a difficult decision. Asking early can prevent a small problem becoming larger, provided people explain clearly what kind of help they need.
items.ideaZh: 能力时间资源不足时求助，电脑问题或决定；尽早清楚说明需求。

items.question: Is it important for parents to teach their children to help others?
items.questionZh: 父母教孩子帮助别人重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, because children learn a lot from ordinary family behaviour. Parents can show them how to notice another person's needs and offer something useful. Small actions, like helping carry things, are a manageable starting point. The lesson should include respect, rather than forcing help on someone.
items.ideaZh: 从日常示范、搬小物等行动起步；帮助也尊重他人，不强加。

items.question: Is it enough for children to learn about helping others only from their parents?
items.questionZh: 只从父母那里学帮助别人够吗？
items.answer: No, children also need opportunities at school and in their community. Different situations teach them that people need different kinds of support. A teacher can organise a group task where everyone contributes, while classmates help children learn cooperation between people of a similar age.
items.ideaZh: 家庭之外学校社区也要实践；任务分工学合作，同龄人也有作用。

items.question: What kinds of skills are needed when people want to help others?
items.questionZh: 帮助别人需要什么技能？
items.answer: Listening is a good starting point, because guessing the problem can lead to unhelpful advice. People also need relevant knowledge and clear communication. For a complicated issue, recognising the limits of their skills matters too. Sometimes the most useful help is finding someone better qualified.
items.ideaZh: 先听清需求，相关知识与沟通；知道能力边界，必要时转给更合适的人。

items.question: Should people solve their own problems before helping others?
items.questionZh: 人们应该先解决自己的问题再帮别人吗？
items.answer: They should consider their own capacity, but they don't need a perfect life before being helpful. A small favour might be quite manageable during a busy week. If helping would create serious problems for them, it's reasonable to set a limit or offer another kind of support.
items.ideaZh: 量力而行但不必等一切完美；小帮忙可做，负担过重时设界限。

items.question: Describe a person who taught you a skill when you were young.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你年幼时教过你技能的人。
cueCard: And explain whether it is easy to learn it.
cueCardZh: 说明这项技能是否容易学
items.answer:
A person who taught me a skill when I was young was my father. He showed me how to control a basketball while moving when I was about twelve, on a court near our home.

I wanted to learn because other children were playing together, and I didn't want to stand at the side without knowing what to do. At first, I kept looking down, and the ball often bounced away. My father showed me how to use my fingers and asked me to practise slowly before trying to run.

The basic idea was easy to understand, but doing it smoothly wasn't easy at all. I needed several weeks of practice before I stopped losing the ball so often. Sometimes I felt impatient, but he stayed calm. Eventually I could join games more confidently and make friends through them. I still enjoy basketball, so I feel grateful that he helped me get started and taught me to be patient with a new skill.

items.question: What kinds of skills do you think children should learn before they start school?
items.questionZh: 孩子上学前应学会哪些技能？
items.answer: Basic independence is useful, such as using the toilet, putting belongings away and asking an adult for help. Children also benefit from taking turns and expressing simple needs. I wouldn't expect them to master school subjects in advance; feeling safe and being able to join activities matters more.
items.ideaZh: 重点是如厕、收物、求助、轮流参与和表达需要，不要求提前精通学科。

items.question: What's the best age for children to begin school?
items.questionZh: 孩子开始上学最合适的年龄是多少？
items.answer: I wouldn't choose one exact age for every child. Readiness includes being able to communicate, follow simple routines and spend time away from home. Schools also differ in what they expect. A gradual introduction and support from adults may matter more than a small difference in starting age.
items.ideaZh: 不定单一年龄；看沟通作息独立准备和学校要求，过渡支持很重要。

items.question: Is it better for a child to learn a skill on their own, or with a teacher?
items.questionZh: 孩子自学技能还是跟老师学更好？
items.answer: A teacher is useful when correct technique matters, because mistakes can be noticed early. Learning independently also gives children room to explore and solve problems. I'd combine the two: demonstrate the basics, let the child practise, and offer help when it is actually needed.
items.ideaZh: 老师保证基础和纠错，自学给探索空间；示范后独立练，卡住再帮助。

items.question: Do you think the internet is a good way to learn a new skill?
items.questionZh: 互联网是学习新技能的好途径吗？
items.answer: Yes, people can find demonstrations and replay difficult parts at their own pace. That's useful for something like learning a software tool. The main difficulty is judging the quality of advice and sticking with practice. Watching several tutorials isn't the same as being able to do the skill.
items.ideaZh: 演示可重复、按自己节奏；筛选内容并动手练，不把观看数量当能力。

items.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of learning a skill from other people?
items.questionZh: 跟别人学技能有什么优缺点？
items.answer: Another person can explain mistakes and adapt the lesson when something isn't clear. That feedback can save time. However, the learner may become dependent on guidance, or the teacher's pace may not suit them. Independent practice between lessons helps turn the advice into a usable skill.

items.question: Do young people learn things faster than older people?
items.questionZh: 年轻人比年长者学得快吗？
items.answer: It depends on the skill and the learner's experience. Younger people may feel comfortable experimenting with an unfamiliar app, while older learners can connect new information with knowledge they already have. Motivation and regular practice matter a lot, so I wouldn't assume age alone decides learning speed.
items.ideaZh: 看技能与经历，年轻者敢试，年长者可用经验；动力练习也重要。

items.topic: 经常做但浪费时间的活动
items.question: Describe an activity you usually do that wastes your time.
items.questionZh: 描述一项你经常做但浪费时间的活动。
cueCard: How long you have been doing it
When do you usually do it
And explain why you are still doing it knowing it is a waste of time.
cueCardZh: 说明明知浪费时间为什么仍在做
items.answer:
An activity I do regularly that can waste my time is playing extra rounds of a game after I have already planned to stop. I've had this habit for a few years, usually in the evening after studying.

I enjoy games because they help me relax, and I can play with friends online. The problem is that one more round rarely feels like a big decision. If I lose, I want to try again. If I win, I want to keep going. Before I notice it, a short break can become a much longer session.

I don't think all gaming is a waste of time, but these extra rounds often are. They can push back my bedtime or leave less time for something I wanted to finish. I sometimes feel more tired afterwards instead of relaxed. I'm trying to set a clear stopping time and tell my friends in advance, so it's easier to leave the game.

I enjoy games because they help me relax, and I can play with friends online. The problem is that one more round rarely feels like a big decision. If I lose, I want to try again. If I win, I want to keep going. Before I notice it, a short break can become a much longer session.

cluesZh: 经常做的活动：原计划结束后仍多玩几局；补已经这样几年，通常晚上学习后，时长为补充。
形成原因：游戏能放松并与朋友联机；输了想再试、赢了想继续，不知不觉休息变长。
为什么浪费与改进：并非所有游戏都浪费时间，但多余局数推迟睡觉、挤占任务时间，甚至更累；设定停玩时间并提前告知朋友。
translationsZh: 我喜欢游戏，因为它能帮我放松，也能和朋友一起联机玩。问题在于，再打一局往往感觉不是什么大决定。如果输了，我想再试一次；如果赢了，我又想继续。在我意识到之前，一次短暂的休息就可能变成很长一段游戏时间。
我不认为玩游戏全都是浪费时间，但这些额外的局数常常是。它们可能推迟我的睡觉时间，或者让原本想完成的事情所剩时间更少。有时玩完我反而更累，而不是更放松。我正在尝试设定明确的停止时间，并提前告诉朋友，这样退出游戏就更容易。

items.extensionZh: 延伸：仍想享受游戏，只是更好地控制时间；保持平衡比完全放弃更现实。

items.topic: 经常做但浪费时间的活动
items.question: What kinds of activities do people have to do every day?
items.questionZh: 人们每天必须做哪些活动？
items.answer: Eating, washing, travelling to work or study, and looking after a home are common examples. These tasks may not always feel interesting, but they support everything else people want to do. Organising them into a simple routine can reduce the number of small decisions each day.
items.ideaZh: 吃饭清洁通勤家务支持日常；简单作息减少反复决定。

items.topic: 经常做但浪费时间的活动
items.question: Is it important to have a daily routine?
items.questionZh: 有固定日常安排重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, a simple routine reduces the number of small decisions people have to make. It can help them begin work without waiting to feel motivated. But the routine should allow some flexibility. If one unexpected event ruins the entire schedule, the plan is probably too strict to be useful.
items.ideaZh: 能减少小决定、帮助开始行动，但要有弹性，不能一点意外就毁掉整天计划。

items.topic: 经常做但浪费时间的活动
items.question: How can people make routine activities less boring?
items.questionZh: 怎样让日常重复活动不那么无聊？
items.answer: People can change a small part of the activity or connect it with a clear goal. For example, cooking a familiar meal with a different ingredient can make it interesting again. Sharing a task with someone also helps, as long as the conversation doesn't interfere with doing it properly.
items.ideaZh: 小变化、明确目的、一起做；举熟菜换食材，仍保证事情做好。

items.topic: 经常做但浪费时间的活动
items.question: What kinds of things make people feel pressured?
items.questionZh: 什么事情让人感到压力？
items.answer: Deadlines, money worries and other people's expectations can create pressure. Even enjoyable activities become stressful if someone feels they must perform perfectly. Students, for example, may worry about several tasks at once. Having clear priorities and someone to discuss the problem with can make the workload feel more manageable.
items.ideaZh: 期限、钱和他人期望，追求完美也会添压；明确优先事项并讨论有助于应对。
items.vocab: expectations — 期望；manageable — 能应对的
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.topic: 经常做但浪费时间的活动
items.question: Is it beneficial to have a certain amount of stress?
items.questionZh: 一定程度的压力有益吗？
items.answer: A manageable deadline can encourage people to start and focus on what matters. However, pressure stops being useful when it feels constant or impossible to control. I'd distinguish a short challenge with enough support from a situation where someone never has time to recover.
items.ideaZh: 可控截止日期有推动力，持续失控压力则不同；区分短挑战和无恢复空间。
items.vocab: useful — 有用的；people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 经常做但浪费时间的活动
items.question: What would make people feel less stressed - having more time or more money?
items.questionZh: 更多时间还是更多钱更能减压？
items.answer: It depends on the source of the pressure. Someone struggling with essential bills may benefit more from money, while an overloaded student may need time and fewer commitments. Often the two are connected, but neither automatically solves problems such as unclear expectations or poor communication.
items.ideaZh: 经济困境需钱，任务过载需时间；也有期望不清、沟通差的问题不能自动解决。
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Describe a crowded place you have been to.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你去过的拥挤地点。
cueCard: Where you have been that was crowded
How often you go to this place
Who did you go there with
And explain how you feel about going to this place.
cueCardZh: 说明你对去那里的感受
items.answer:
A crowded place I went to was a shopping mall in Haikou. I go there about once a month. On this visit, I went with my girlfriend on a weekend afternoon during a sales event.

We went there mainly because I wanted to buy some headphones. As soon as we walked in, we noticed how busy it was. People were standing outside popular shops, and we had to wait before using the lifts. Near the food area, it was difficult to find a free table.

We visited an electronics shop, tried several pairs of headphones and eventually chose one. Then we walked around for a little longer, but moving through the crowd was tiring. We decided to leave and get something to eat somewhere quieter. I was pleased with what I bought, but I didn't enjoy the crowds very much. Since then, I've tried to choose less busy times when I need to shop.

We went there mainly because I wanted to buy some headphones. As soon as we walked in, we noticed how busy it was. People were standing outside popular shops, and we had to wait before using the lifts. Near the food area, it was difficult to find a free table.

We decided to leave and get something to eat somewhere quieter. I was pleased with what I bought, but I didn't enjoy the crowds very much. Since then, I've tried to choose less busy times when I need to shop.
cluesZh: 地点、频率、同行者：海口商场大约每月去一次，这次周末和女朋友去，频率和事件为旧草稿补充。
目的与拥挤细节：买耳机；热门店外有人、电梯需等、餐饮区难找空桌。
活动和后续：试戴后买到耳机，但在人群中走很累，便离开去安静处吃东西；以后避开购物高峰。
translationsZh: 我们进了一家电子产品店，试了几副耳机，最后选定了一副。接着又逛了一会儿，但穿过人群很累。我们决定离开，到安静些的地方吃点东西。我对买到的东西很满意，但不太喜欢拥挤的人群。从那以后，需要购物时，我会尽量选择人少的时段。
items.provenance: 沿用耳机购物故事；人流、排队及离开商场的安排为拟写。
items.extension: Being there with my girlfriend made the wait less boring. We could talk to each other, although we sometimes had to raise our voices.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：有女朋友一起，等待不那么无聊；可以聊天，不过有时要提高音量。

items.question: Why do people go to crowded places?
items.questionZh: 人们为什么去拥挤的地方？
items.answer: Often because a place offers something they want, such as a popular restaurant or a special event. Sometimes crowds are unavoidable, as on public transport at busy times. So people aren't always choosing the crowd itself; they may simply accept it as part of getting somewhere or doing something enjoyable.
items.ideaZh: 通常为餐厅、活动或交通需求，未必喜欢人群本身，而是接受必要代价。
items.vocab: unavoidable — 无法避免的；public transport — 公共交通
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: Do people enjoy going to crowded places?
items.questionZh: 人们喜欢去拥挤的地方吗？
items.answer: Some enjoy the energy of a busy concert or market, while others find it tiring. Choice matters too. A crowd at an event you wanted to attend feels different from being squeezed into transport when you're already late. I think context explains a lot of the difference.
items.ideaZh: 看主动选择与场景：演出人群有活力，迟到通勤挤车难受。
items.vocab: enjoy — 享受喜欢；different — 不同的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Which parts of a city tend to be the most crowded?
items.questionZh: 城市哪些地方最容易拥挤？
items.answer: Transport hubs, popular shopping areas and major attractions often attract large numbers of people. The busiest time can change throughout the day. For example, a station may be packed during commuting hours, while a restaurant area becomes busier in the evening or at weekends.
items.ideaZh: 枢纽商圈景点随时段变化；用通勤与晚间餐饮作比较。
items.vocab: people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Does a city need to have quiet places?
items.questionZh: 城市需要安静的地方吗？
items.answer: Yes, residents need somewhere to rest or concentrate without constant activity around them. Libraries and small green spaces can provide that option even in a busy city. They don't have to be completely silent, but people should be able to take a break from the busiest streets.
items.ideaZh: 图书馆绿地提供休息专注空间，不必绝对无声但应能离开喧闹。
items.vocab: concentrate — 专注；people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: If a city is very crowded, what kind of facilities should it have?
items.questionZh: 拥挤城市应有哪些设施？
items.answer: Reliable public transport and safe walking routes are important so people can move without everything depending on cars. Cities also need enough public toilets, seating and clear signs in busy areas. Good facilities help spread people out and make necessary waiting less uncomfortable.
items.ideaZh: 交通步道、厕所座椅标识，帮助分散人流和改善等待。
items.vocab: reliable — 可靠的；clear — 清楚的
