items.topic: 经常进行但不喜欢的短途旅行
items.question: Describe a short trip you often take but do not like.
items.questionZh: 描述一段你经常进行却不喜欢的短途旅程。
cueCard: And explain why you do not like the trip.
items.answer:
A short trip I often take but don't really enjoy is the bus journey from my home to school in Haikou. I usually make this trip on weekday mornings when I have classes.

It takes about half an hour on a normal day, but it can take longer when the roads are busy. I need to arrive on time, so I often leave earlier than I would like. The bus can also be crowded, and sometimes I have to stand for most of the journey.

The part I dislike most is the waiting. If I just miss a bus, I keep checking the time and worrying about being late. I sometimes listen to music to make the trip more pleasant, but I still find it tiring before an early class. The journey is necessary, and taking the bus is affordable. However, I would enjoy it more if the waiting time were more predictable.
paragraphs: A short trip I often take but don't really enjoy is the bus journey from my home to school in Haikou. I usually make this trip on weekday mornings when I have classes.

It takes about half an hour on a normal day, but it can take longer when the roads are busy. I need to arrive on time, so I often leave earlier than I would like. The bus can also be crowded, and sometimes I have to stand for most of the journey.

The part I dislike most is the waiting. If I just miss a bus, I keep checking the time and worrying about being late. I sometimes listen to music to make the trip more pleasant, but I still find it tiring before an early class. The journey is necessary, and taking the bus is affordable. However, I would enjoy it more if the waiting time were more predictable.
cluesZh: 路线和时间：海口家到学校的公交路程，工作日早上有课时乘坐。
实际不便：平常约半小时，堵车会延长；为了准时得早出门，车上拥挤时还要站着。
最不喜欢的部分：等车时间难预测、担心迟到；听音乐稍有缓解，虽便宜且必要，但上早课前已感疲惫。
translationsZh: 我最不喜欢的是等待。如果刚好错过一班车，我就会不停看时间，担心迟到。有时我听音乐，让路程愉快些，但早课前这样出行还是让我觉得累。这段路是必须走的，坐公交也负担得起。不过，如果等车时间更容易预估，我会更喜欢这段行程。
items.provenance: 拟定住在海口家中、上学常乘公交、路程约半小时；具体交通与居住信息均可替换。
items.extension: On quieter days, the same journey feels much easier. Having a seat and a little extra time can make a surprisingly big difference.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：人少时同一段路会轻松很多；有座位、时间宽裕一点，体验就明显不同。

items.topic: 经常进行但不喜欢的短途旅行
items.question: What forms of transport do people in your country use more often?
items.questionZh: 你们国家人们经常使用什么交通方式？
items.answer: From what I see, people choose buses, cars, trains or smaller forms of transport depending on the distance. A city trip is different from travelling between provinces. Cost, convenience and the transport available near home usually matter more than having one favourite method for every journey.
items.ideaZh: 距离决定城市和跨省方式，看费用便利及当地设施；不编全国排名。
items.vocab: different — 不同的；people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 经常进行但不喜欢的短途旅行
items.question: Why do people choose to travel abroad during their holidays?
items.questionZh: 为什么人们假期选择出国旅行？
items.answer: They may want to see a different environment, try unfamiliar food or experience another culture directly. A holiday also gives people a chance to step away from everyday routines. However, travelling abroad isn't the only way to do that; it depends on a person's interests and budget.
items.ideaZh: 新环境食物文化、离开日常；承认国内也能实现，随兴趣预算而定。
items.vocab: budget — 预算；experience — 经历经验
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 经常进行但不喜欢的短途旅行
items.question: What are the benefits of travelling abroad?
items.questionZh: 出国旅行有什么好处？
items.answer: People can experience different daily routines, try unfamiliar food and practise communicating outside their usual environment. It may also challenge assumptions about another place. The benefit depends on how someone travels, though. Paying attention and talking respectfully with people can teach more than rushing through a list of sights.
items.ideaZh: 体验不同生活饮食和沟通环境，也能反思成见；认真观察交流比赶景点更有收获。
items.vocab: assumptions — 先入为主的看法；respectfully — 尊重地
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.topic: 经常进行但不喜欢的短途旅行
items.question: How does travelling with large crowds affect people's experience?
items.questionZh: 和大批人群一起旅行如何影响体验？
items.answer: It can make transport, restaurants and attractions harder to use, especially when people spend a lot of time queuing. On the other hand, a lively crowd can add atmosphere to an event. Planning quieter times and leaving some flexibility can make the same destination feel much more enjoyable.
items.ideaZh: 排队资源紧张降低体验，活动氛围可能加分；错峰留弹性。
items.vocab: people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 经常进行但不喜欢的短途旅行
items.question: What are the main purposes people have for travelling?
items.questionZh: 人们旅行的主要目的有哪些？
items.answer: Some travel to relax, while others want to learn, visit relatives or do something adventurous. The purpose affects the kind of trip they plan. Someone wanting rest may choose one comfortable base, whereas someone exploring a new area might prefer moving between several places.
items.ideaZh: 放松学习探亲冒险等目的改变行程：休息固定落脚，探索多地点。
items.vocab: comfortable — 舒适的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Describe a movie you dislike.
items.questionZh: 描述一部你不喜欢的电影。
cueCard: When and where you watched it
And explain why you dislike it.
items.answer:
A film I didn't enjoy was a horror film I watched online at home last year. I can't remember its English title, but it was about a family who moved into an old house and began hearing strange sounds.

I watched it with a friend who had suggested it. At first, I was curious because I wanted to find out what was happening in the house. However, the film kept using sudden loud noises to make the audience jump. After a while, that became tiring rather than exciting.

My main problem was that I didn't care much about the characters. They made choices that seemed unlikely, and the ending didn't answer several questions. I usually prefer comedies, such as King of Comedy, because I enjoy humour and a story I can connect with. This film didn't give me that feeling. I was glad when it finished, although we had a laugh about it afterwards.
paragraphs: A film I didn't enjoy was a horror film I watched online at home last year. I can't remember its English title, but it was about a family who moved into an old house and began hearing strange sounds.

I watched it with a friend who had suggested it. At first, I was curious because I wanted to find out what was happening in the house. However, the film kept using sudden loud noises to make the audience jump. After a while, that became tiring rather than exciting.

My main problem was that I didn't care much about the characters. They made choices that seemed unlikely, and the ending didn't answer several questions. I usually prefer comedies, such as King of Comedy, because I enjoy humour and a story I can connect with. This film didn't give me that feeling. I was glad when it finished, although we had a laugh about it afterwards.
cluesZh: 电影与背景：去年在家网上看的一部恐怖片，记不清英文名；一家人搬进老房子后听到怪声。
观看过程：朋友推荐并一起看，开始好奇，后来反复用突然巨响吓人，让人疲惫。
核心不满与对比：不关心角色，不合理选择与未解答的结尾；更喜欢《喜剧之王》那样有幽默、能产生共鸣的故事。
translationsZh: 我最不满意的是，我不太关心这些角色。他们作出的选择似乎不太合理，结尾也没有回答好几个问题。我通常更喜欢喜剧，比如《喜剧之王》，因为我喜欢幽默，也喜欢能让我产生共鸣的故事。这部电影没有给我那种感觉。结束时我很高兴，虽然之后我们还拿它开玩笑、笑了一阵。
items.provenance: 拟写一部不记得片名的网络恐怖片及观看经历；不把喜欢的《喜剧之王》改成不喜欢。
items.extension: I would not say that all horror films are bad. This particular one just relied too much on sudden shocks and too little on a good story.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：不是认为所有恐怖片都不好，只是这一部过度依赖突然惊吓，故事却不够好。

items.question: What kinds of films are popular in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家流行什么类型的电影？
items.answer: I can't give an exact ranking, but comedies and action films seem popular among people I know. A familiar actor or an interesting story can attract viewers across different genres. Preferences vary, so a film that works well for a family outing may not be someone's first choice when watching alone.
items.ideaZh: 不编排名，从熟人看喜剧动作片较受欢迎，演员故事和观看场合也影响选择。
items.vocab: genres — 类型；ranking — 排名
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: What are the differences between watching a film at home and watching it in a cinema?
items.questionZh: 在家和在影院看电影有什么区别？
items.answer: At home, people can choose the time, pause the film and spend less. A cinema offers a larger screen and a shared atmosphere, and there are usually fewer household distractions. I'd choose according to the film and the company. A family comedy can be just as enjoyable at home.
items.ideaZh: 家里自由、省钱、能暂停，影院屏幕大氛围集中；依电影和同伴选择。
items.vocab: household distractions — 家中的干扰；company — 陪伴的人
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: Do you think films are more effective than books in helping people become more creative?
items.questionZh: 电影比书更能帮助人变得有创造力吗？
items.answer: Not necessarily. Films provide images, sound and examples of visual storytelling, which can inspire ideas. Books leave more of the scene for the reader to imagine. Both can support creativity; what matters is whether people think about what they experience and use it to create something of their own.
items.ideaZh: 不一定，电影提供视听示范，书留想象空间，关键是看后如何思考和创造。
items.vocab: inspire — 启发；creativity — 创造力
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: Can films help people understand the culture of other countries?
items.questionZh: 电影能帮助人们理解其他国家的文化吗？
items.answer: Yes, films can introduce daily habits, language and social issues in a memorable way. But one story can't represent a whole country. A viewer should avoid assuming that every person lives like the characters. Films are a useful starting point for curiosity, especially when followed by other sources or conversations.
items.ideaZh: 能展示习惯、语言和社会问题，但一部片不能代表全国，应结合其他资料。
items.vocab: represent — 代表；social issues — 社会问题
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: Describe a popular person you know.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你认识的受欢迎的人。
cueCard: Where and when you usually see this person
What type of person he/she is
And explain why you think this person is very popular.
items.answer:
A popular person I know is my friend Leo, whom I met through basketball at school. I usually see him at school, either in class or on the basketball court after lessons.

He is friendly and easy to talk to, but I think the main reason people like him is that he makes them feel included. If a new person joins our game, he explains the rules and passes the ball to them instead of ignoring them. He also listens when people talk about their problems.

Once, I made a mistake during a basketball game and felt embarrassed. He encouraged me to keep going, which helped me relax. I've noticed him doing similar things for other people too. He doesn't make a big show of being helpful; it feels natural. That's why I think he is popular. People know they can spend time with him without being judged for every small mistake. I feel lucky to have a friend like that.
paragraphs: A popular person I know is my friend Leo, whom I met through basketball at school. I usually see him at school, either in class or on the basketball court after lessons.

He is friendly and easy to talk to, but I think the main reason people like him is that he makes them feel included. If a new person joins our game, he explains the rules and passes the ball to them instead of ignoring them. He also listens when people talk about their problems.

Once, I made a mistake during a basketball game and felt embarrassed. He encouraged me to keep going, which helped me relax. I've noticed him doing similar things for other people too. He doesn't make a big show of being helpful; it feels natural. That's why I think he is popular. People know they can spend time with him without being judged for every small mistake. I feel lucky to have a friend like that.
cluesZh: 人物和相识：通过学校篮球认识Leo，平时课堂或课后球场见；Leo是练习代称，相识细节为补充。
受欢迎的原因：友好、让人有参与感；新球友来会讲规则和传球，也愿意听别人烦恼。
例子与评价：我失误时被他鼓励，他也同样帮助别人；举止自然，不挑别人小错，让人安心相处。
translationsZh: 有一次，我打篮球时犯了错，觉得很尴尬。他鼓励我继续，这让我放松下来。我也注意到他会对其他人做类似的事。他不会刻意炫耀自己多热心，而是表现得很自然。这就是我觉得他受欢迎的原因。大家知道，和他相处时，不会因为每一个小失误都受到评判。我觉得有这样的朋友很幸运。
items.provenance: 真实：球友鼓励过你。补充：Leo 代称、在班级受欢迎、照顾新队员和帮助同学等特征。
items.extension: He also has a good sense of humour, which helps when everyone is tired. Even a difficult day can feel lighter after talking with him.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：他也很幽默，大家累时尤其有帮助；困难的一天也会因聊天而轻松些。

items.question: What kind of children tend to be popular at school?
items.questionZh: 什么样的孩子在学校容易受欢迎？
items.answer: Some are friendly, funny or good at bringing people into a group. Others become known through sport or school activities. I think kindness helps popularity last: classmates are more likely to enjoy being with someone who listens and includes them than someone who only wants attention.
items.ideaZh: 友善、有趣、善于带人融入或擅长活动都能吸引人，善意让受欢迎持续更久。
items.vocab: includes them — 让他们融入；kindness — 友善
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: Is it important for children to be popular at school?
items.questionZh: 孩子在学校受欢迎重要吗？
items.answer: Feeling accepted matters because children need friends and a sense of security. However, being the most popular person isn't necessary. I'd rather a child had a few trustworthy friends than felt pressure to please everyone. Schools should help all students feel included, not reward only the most visible ones.
items.ideaZh: 重被接纳和可靠朋友，不重人气排名；学校应照顾所有学生。
items.vocab: because — 因为；help — 帮助
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Should popular children help others who are less popular?
items.questionZh: 受欢迎的孩子应帮助不太受欢迎的孩子吗？
items.answer: They can make a useful difference by inviting someone into a game or group conversation. But inclusion shouldn't depend on a few popular children acting kindly. Teachers and other students also share responsibility, and the help should feel friendly rather than making someone seem like a charity project.
items.ideaZh: 邀请参与有用，但不能全靠人气学生；老师同学共同负责，方式不居高临下。

items.question: Do you agree that unpopular children are more likely to succeed later in life?
items.questionZh: 不受欢迎的孩子更容易在以后成功吗？
items.answer: I don't think school popularity predicts success reliably. An unpopular child might develop independence, but they might also feel discouraged. Later success depends on skills, support and opportunities. It's more useful to help children build confidence than to suggest that being excluded is somehow an advantage.
items.ideaZh: 不认为人气可靠预测成功；技能支持机会更重要，不美化被排斥。
items.vocab: opportunities — 机会；confidence — 信心

items.question: Is being popular important in the workplace? What are the advantages and disadvantages?
items.questionZh: 职场受欢迎重要吗？有哪些优缺点？
items.answer: Being approachable can make cooperation easier, because colleagues feel comfortable asking questions or sharing problems. The disadvantage comes when someone avoids difficult conversations just to remain liked. I think being respected and dependable is more useful than being popular at the cost of honest feedback.
items.ideaZh: 亲近便于合作，但讨好会回避难谈；可靠被尊重比牺牲真实反馈的人气更有用。
items.vocab: comfortable — 舒适的；useful — 有用的

items.question: Is it a good thing if your boss is popular?
items.questionZh: 老板受欢迎是好事吗？
items.answer: Usually it helps if employees feel comfortable speaking to their boss. Problems can be discussed earlier, and the workplace may feel less tense. However, a well-liked boss still needs to make fair decisions. Personal friendliness shouldn't replace clear expectations or equal treatment of different employees.
items.ideaZh: 好沟通能早发现问题，但公平标准不能被私人好感替代。

items.question: Describe a time when you saved money to buy something you wanted.
items.questionZh: 描述一次攒钱买想要的物品的经历。
cueCard: How you saved money for it
How long it took you to save enough money
And explain how you felt after you bought it.
items.answer:
Something special I saved up for was a pair of headphones. I wanted them for listening to English and playing games without disturbing other people.

They cost around four hundred yuan, which felt like quite a lot to me as a student. Instead of asking my parents to buy them straight away, I decided to save part of my spending money. For about six weeks, I bought fewer snacks and stopped paying for extra items in games. I kept a note of how much I had saved on my phone.

When I finally had enough, I went to a shopping mall with my girlfriend and tried a few pairs before choosing one. I felt excited, but I also felt proud because I had worked towards something I wanted. The headphones became more meaningful to me because of that effort. I still use them regularly, and I try to take good care of them.

cluesZh: 物品与目的：一副耳机，用来听英语和打游戏，避免打扰别人。
攒钱过程：约四百元；六周里少买零食、不买游戏额外物品，用手机记下存款，而不是马上请父母买。
购买与意义：和女朋友到商场试了几副再挑选；既兴奋又为自己的努力骄傲，因此更珍惜并经常使用。
translationsZh: 耳机大约四百元，对作为学生的我来说，这笔钱不算少。我没有立刻让父母给我买，而是决定存下一部分零花钱。大约六周里，我少买零食，也不再花钱买游戏里的额外物品。我在手机上记录自己存了多少钱。
钱终于够了的时候，我和女朋友去了商场，试了几副耳机才选定一副。我很兴奋，也很自豪，因为我为自己想要的东西付出了努力。正因为这份努力，这副耳机对我更有意义。我现在仍经常用，也尽量好好爱惜它。
items.provenance: 耳机、约四百元、六周攒钱、减少零食与游戏消费等均为补拟经历；后续购物题沿用同一物品。
items.extension: The experience also taught me to wait before buying things. Sometimes I realise I don't really want an item after thinking about it for a while.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：这教会我购买前先等一等；有些东西想一阵后会发现其实并不想要。

items.question: Should schools teach children how to manage money?
items.questionZh: 学校应该教儿童管理金钱吗？
items.answer: Yes, using simple, practical activities. Younger children could compare prices or plan how to use a small pretend budget. Older students could discuss needs, wants and saving goals. Lessons should fit their age, because complicated financial language is less useful than habits they can apply in everyday life.
items.ideaZh: 应该，用适龄的比价、模拟预算和区分需要与想要等实际活动。
items.vocab: pretend budget — 模拟预算；saving goals — 储蓄目标
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: Should parents encourage their children to spend money freely or to be careful with it?
items.questionZh: 父母应鼓励孩子自由花钱还是谨慎花钱？
items.answer: They should teach a balance. Children need to understand saving for future needs, but also how to spend sensibly on things they value. If spending always feels wrong, money becomes a source of unnecessary worry. A small allowance can help them practise choosing instead of buying everything immediately.
items.ideaZh: 教平衡，既为未来储蓄，也合理花在重视的东西上，小额零花钱可用来练习。
items.vocab: sensibly — 明智合理地；allowance — 零花钱
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: Is it easier to teach teenagers how to manage money when they are 16 or 17 years old?
items.questionZh: 在十六七岁教青少年理财更容易吗？
items.answer: In some ways, yes. Teenagers at that age can understand prices and plan purchases that matter to them. Giving them a small budget lets them practise. However, basic ideas can be introduced earlier, and age alone doesn't make learning easy; they still need clear examples and room to make small mistakes.
items.ideaZh: 某些方面会，这时懂价格、可练预算；更早也能启蒙，年龄不是唯一因素。
items.vocab: budget — 预算；room to make small mistakes — 允许犯小错的空间
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: Do you think which one is easier, saving money or spending money?
items.questionZh: 存钱和花钱哪个更容易？
items.answer: For many people, spending is easier because the reward is immediate. Saving means saying no to something now for a later benefit. But income matters too; someone with very little left after basic expenses may find saving difficult even if they are careful and have good habits.
items.ideaZh: 花钱常有即时满足，存钱需要等待；收入和必要开支也会限制储蓄。
items.vocab: immediate — 即时的；basic expenses — 基本开支

items.question: Describe a person who you think is very happy.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你觉得很快乐的人。
cueCard: Why you think this person is happy
And explain how you feel about this person.
items.answer:
A happy person I know is my friend Leo. We often see each other at school and play basketball together when we have some free time.

He is easy to talk to and usually has a smile on his face. He enjoys simple things, like having a good meal or making a difficult shot. When something funny happens, he laughs openly, and that often puts the rest of us in a good mood too.

I remember making a mistake during a basketball game once. I felt awkward, but he encouraged me and told me to keep trying. He didn't make a big deal out of it. I think he is happy because he doesn't expect everything to be perfect. He focuses on what he can enjoy or improve. Of course, he has bad days like everyone else, but he usually finds a way to move on. I feel more relaxed around him.

I think he is happy because he doesn't expect everything to be perfect. He focuses on what he can enjoy or improve. cluesZh: 人物与关系：朋友 Leo，在学校常见面，有空一起打篮球。
日常表现：好相处、常微笑，吃顿好饭或投进难球就开心；笑声也感染朋友。
具体例子与原因：我失误时他鼓励我、不小题大做；不要求凡事完美，关注能享受和改进的部分。
translationsZh: 我记得有次打篮球时犯了一个错误。我觉得很尴尬，但他鼓励我，让我继续尝试。他没有把这当成什么大事。我觉得他快乐，是因为他不期待一切都完美。他关注的是自己能享受什么、能改进什么。当然，他也和其他人一样会有心情不好的时候，但通常都能想办法继续向前。和他在一起，我会更放松。
items.provenance: 真实：球友在你失误后鼓励你。补充：Leo 代称、开朗性格、笑话与日常习惯。
items.extension: His attitude makes our games more enjoyable. Even when we lose, we can still laugh together and look forward to playing again another day.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：他的态度让比赛更有趣，输了也能一起笑，并期待下次打球。

items.question: What do people enjoy most about their secondary school years?
items.questionZh: 人们最喜欢中学时代的什么？
items.answer: Many people remember spending time with classmates and sharing ordinary experiences, such as games or school events. Those memories may feel special because everyone was learning and growing together. However, not everyone enjoyed school, so I wouldn't assume the same period was happy for every person.
items.ideaZh: 同学游戏活动共同成长常令人怀念；也承认并非人人中学都快乐。
items.vocab: remember — 记住；because — 因为

items.question: Can teachers tell when a child is unhappy?
items.questionZh: 老师能看出孩子不开心吗？
items.answer: Sometimes, especially if they know a child's usual behaviour. A student who suddenly stops joining activities may need attention. But teachers can't know everything from appearances, because some children hide their feelings. A calm, private conversation is likely to tell them more than simply assuming what is wrong.
items.ideaZh: 熟悉孩子时可能看出变化，但不能只凭外表，私下平静交谈更有帮助。
items.vocab: behaviour — 行为；appearances — 外在表现

items.question: Should teachers always know what their students are doing?
items.questionZh: 老师应该始终知道学生在做什么吗？
items.answer: No, constant checking would be unrealistic and could make children uncomfortable. Teachers should know enough to keep students safe and support learning, while allowing some independence. Clear rules and regular conversations can help. The amount of supervision should also depend on the child's age and the situation.
items.ideaZh: 不用时时监控；兼顾安全与独立，靠规则和沟通，监督程度按年龄情境调整。
items.vocab: supervision — 监督；independence — 独立性

items.question: How can the arts help spread positive emotions in society?
items.questionZh: 艺术如何帮助社会传播积极情绪？
items.answer: Music, films and performances can give people an experience to share. A comedy might help a family laugh together after a difficult day, while a song can express a feeling that is hard to explain. The effect depends on the audience, though; people don't all enjoy the same kind of art.
items.ideaZh: 电影音乐提供共享体验，也能表达难说的感受；效果因观众喜好而异。
items.vocab: audience — 观众；express — 表达
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: Describe someone who is older than you that you admire.
items.questionZh: 描述一个比你年长而且你敬佩的人。
cueCard: And explain how you feel about this person.
items.answer:
Someone older than me whom I admire is my grandfather. I've known him all my life, of course, but I appreciate him more as I get older.

He is a patient person who enjoys growing plants and making small things by hand. When I visit him, we often water the plants together or sit outside and talk. He sometimes shows me how to fix something simple around the house. He explains each step slowly and doesn't get annoyed when I ask questions.

What I admire most is the way he treats people. He listens carefully and rarely makes me feel embarrassed about a mistake. If I have a problem with my studies, he may not understand the technical details, but he still helps me feel calmer. Spending time with him reminds me that being useful and kind can matter more than showing off. I feel comfortable around him, and I value our time together.

cluesZh: 人物：爷爷，从小就认识，越长大越能体会他的好。
相处活动：浇花、在外面聊天、学习简单维修；他耐心解释，不因我提问而恼火。
敬佩原因：认真倾听，不让人因犯错难堪；即使不懂专业细节也能安慰我，提醒我善良和帮助别人比炫耀更重要。
translationsZh: 我最敬佩的是他待人的方式。他认真听别人说话，很少让我因为犯错而难堪。如果我的学习出了问题，他或许不懂其中的技术细节，但仍能让我平静下来。和他相处提醒我，能帮上忙、待人善良，可能比炫耀自己更重要。和他在一起我很自在，也很珍惜我们共处的时间。
items.provenance: 爷爷的性格、花园、相处活动及鼓励方式均为新设定；不当作用户已确认家庭事实。
items.extension: I would like to visit him more often when I am less busy. Even a short conversation with him usually improves my mood.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：不忙时想多去看他；即使简短聊天也通常能改善心情。

items.question: What can young and old people learn from each other?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与老人能互相学什么？
items.answer: Young people can learn practical experience and patience from older people. Older people may appreciate help with newer technology or a different view of current life. It should go both ways. For example, a grandparent could teach a useful cooking skill while a grandchild explains how to organise photos on a phone.
items.ideaZh: 年轻人学经验耐心，老人学新技术；用教做饭与整理手机照片举例，强调双向学习。
items.vocab: go both ways — 是双向的；patience — 耐心

items.question: Has old people's life quality improved when compared to the past?
items.questionZh: 与过去相比，老年人的生活质量提高了吗？
items.answer: In some ways it may have, with more tools and services that make daily life convenient. But the improvement is not equal for everyone. Someone who feels isolated or struggles with digital services may still face difficulties. I'd consider independence, relationships and access to help, rather than just material comfort.
items.ideaZh: 便利工具服务可能改善生活，但并不均等；还应看孤独感、独立性和求助渠道。
items.vocab: isolated — 孤立、缺少联系的；access to help — 获得帮助的途径
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: Why is there a generation gap between the young and the old?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与老人为什么有代沟？
items.answer: Different generations grow up with different technology, expectations and experiences. That can affect how they see work, relationships or spending money. Problems grow when each side assumes its own experience is the only normal one. Listening to the reasons behind an opinion can make the gap easier to understand.
items.ideaZh: 成长时的技术、期望与经历不同；双方只认自己的经验会加剧问题，倾听有帮助。
items.vocab: generation gap — 代沟；assumes — 想当然地认为
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: What do old people usually do in their daily life?
items.questionZh: 老年人日常通常做什么？
items.answer: It varies with their health, interests and responsibilities. Some still work, some care for family, and others spend time on hobbies or meeting friends. A retired person might enjoy gardening or walking, but retirement doesn't mean everyone has the same routine or unlimited free time.
items.ideaZh: 视健康、责任和兴趣，有人工作、照顾家人或发展爱好，退休不等于都有很多空闲。
items.vocab: retirement — 退休；responsibilities — 责任
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.topic: 与朋友度过的愉快夜晚
items.question: Describe an enjoyable evening with your friends.
items.questionZh: 描述一个和朋友度过的愉快夜晚。
cueCard: Who you spent the evening with
And explain why you think it was an enjoyable evening.
items.answer:
An evening I really enjoyed was a Friday last term when I played basketball with some friends at school. My friend Leo and two other classmates were there.

We had finished our classes and wanted to do something active before the weekend. We played a few short games on the school court. During one game, I made a mistake and felt a bit embarrassed. Leo encouraged me and told me to keep going. That helped me relax and enjoy the game again.

Afterwards, we went to a small restaurant nearby and had dinner together. We talked about classes, games and some funny things that had happened that week. Nothing particularly unusual happened, but the whole evening felt easy and enjoyable. I liked having a break from my computer and spending time with people who made me feel comfortable. I went home physically tired but in a much better mood than before.

cluesZh: 时间人物：上学期某个周五晚上，在学校和 Leo、另外两位同学打篮球。
球场经历：下课后打几场短比赛；我失误尴尬时 Leo 鼓励我，让我重新放松享受比赛。
后续与感受：附近餐馆聚餐，聊课程、游戏和趣事；普通活动也很轻松，离开电脑、和自在相处的朋友在一起，身体累但心情好。
translationsZh: 之后，我们去了附近一家小餐馆一起吃晚饭。我们聊了课程、游戏，以及那周发生的一些有趣的事。没有发生什么特别不寻常的事情，但整个晚上都很轻松愉快。我喜欢暂时离开电脑，和让我感到自在的人一起度过时间。回家时身体虽然累，但心情比之前好多了。
items.provenance: 真实：校篮球场、朋友鼓励。补充：上学期周五晚上、Leo 代称、三位朋友及打球后吃饭。
items.extension: It reminded me that a good evening does not have to cost much. A simple activity and the right people can be enough.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：愉快夜晚不一定花很多钱，简单活动加上合适的朋友就足够。

items.topic: 与朋友度过的愉快夜晚
items.question: What kinds of activities do people usually do with their friends?
items.questionZh: 人们通常和朋友做哪些活动？
items.answer: They might eat together, play sports, watch something or simply talk. The choice depends on shared interests and available time. I think a regular, simple activity can be more valuable than an elaborate plan, because it makes meeting easier when everyone has different commitments.
items.ideaZh: 吃饭运动观看聊天随兴趣时间；简单固定活动更易在忙碌中维持。
items.vocab: different — 不同的；because — 因为
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 与朋友度过的愉快夜晚
items.question: What are the differences between the evening activities of young people and older people?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与年长者的晚间活动有什么不同？
items.answer: Younger people may choose activities connected with school friends or newer forms of entertainment. Older people may have more established routines and interests. However, there is plenty of overlap, such as walking, films and sport. Differences in available time and physical ability can be more useful to consider than age by itself.
items.ideaZh: 可能有娱乐形式和习惯差异，也有散步、电影、运动等共同点，要看时间与体力。
items.vocab: overlap — 重合之处；physical ability — 体能

items.topic: 与朋友度过的愉快夜晚
items.question: Do people enjoy spending time with their cousins? Why?
items.questionZh: 人们喜欢和堂表兄弟姐妹相处吗？为什么？
items.answer: Often, especially if they grew up together. Cousins can share family memories while also feeling like friends of a similar age. But closeness depends on contact and personality. Someone who rarely meets their cousins may feel more comfortable with friends they see every day.
items.ideaZh: 一起长大可兼朋友和家庭记忆；关系也看接触频率个性。

items.topic: 与朋友度过的愉快夜晚
items.question: Is it important to maintain relationships with extended family members?
items.questionZh: 保持与大家庭成员的关系重要吗？
items.answer: It can give people a wider network of support and a connection with family history. A quick call or an occasional visit may be enough to keep that link. Still, the relationship should be respectful; being related doesn't mean people have to agree on everything.
items.ideaZh: 支持网络与家族记忆，电话偶尔探访维系；亲属也要相互尊重。

items.topic: 与朋友度过的愉快夜晚
items.question: How can families strengthen their relationships and become closer?
items.questionZh: 家庭怎样加强关系、变得更亲密？
items.answer: Regular time together helps, especially when people are paying attention instead of looking at separate screens. A shared meal or short walk gives everyone a chance to talk. It also helps to choose activities that different family members enjoy, so being together feels pleasant rather than like another obligation.
items.ideaZh: 定期专心共处，吃饭散步交流，选择大家喜欢的活动，避免相处成为负担。

items.question: How do people get along in a big family?
items.questionZh: 大家庭成员怎样和睦相处？
items.answer: They need clear communication and some respect for personal space. Sharing chores fairly can prevent small frustrations from building up. In a large family, people won't agree on everything, so being able to discuss a problem calmly matters. Spending time together is easier when nobody feels ignored or given too much work.
items.ideaZh: 清楚沟通、尊重个人空间、公平分担家务，平静解决分歧，避免忽视或压任务。

items.question: What are the differences between young people's leisure time activities and those of old people?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与老人的休闲活动有什么不同？
items.answer: Younger people may choose activities connected with school friends or newer forms of entertainment. Older people may have more established routines and interests. However, there is plenty of overlap, such as walking, films and sport. Differences in available time and physical ability can be more useful to consider than age by itself.

items.question: Do young people prefer spending time with family or with friends?
items.questionZh: 年轻人更喜欢陪家人还是朋友？
items.answer: Many young people enjoy being with friends because they share interests and want more independence. That doesn't mean family becomes unimportant. Someone might prefer friends for a basketball game and family for a relaxed meal. The situation and the quality of the relationships matter more than age alone.

items.question: Do older people prefer spending time with family or with friends?
items.questionZh: 老人更喜欢和家人还是朋友相处？
items.answer: It depends on their relationships and daily routine. Some older people enjoy being with children and grandchildren, while others value friends who share their interests. items.question: Why do people need friends?
items.questionZh: 人们为什么需要朋友？
items.answer: Friends give people company, support and someone to share experiences with. A friend may understand a worry differently from a family member because they are at a similar stage of life. Friendship is also about enjoying ordinary things together, such as a meal or a game, rather than only asking for help.
items.ideaZh: 朋友带来陪伴、支持和共同经历，也能理解同阶段的烦恼，友谊不只是求助。

items.topic: 看过的名人采访（原文提示冲突）
items.question: Describe an interviewed a famous person that you have seen.
items.questionZh: 描述你看过的一次名人采访（原题有语病）。
cueCard: And explain how you felt about the experience.
cueCardZh: 你采访了谁（与观看标题冲突）
你问了什么（与观看标题冲突）
items.answer:
I'd like to describe an old interview with Michael Jordan that I watched online. It was from a programme called 60 Minutes, and it covered basketball and life after retirement.

I watched it on my laptop at home one evening a few months ago. My friend Leo had sent me a link because he knew I liked basketball. I used subtitles, and I paused a few times when I couldn't follow the English.

What interested me was seeing a famous player sitting down and having a conversation. Usually, I only watch short clips of people playing, so this felt more personal. It made me curious about what someone's life is like away from their job. I also thought about my own interests. Basketball is important to me, but so are my studies and family. I enjoyed the interview and talked about it with Leo the next time we played together.

I watched it on my laptop at home one evening a few months ago. My friend Leo had sent me a link because he knew I liked basketball. I used subtitles, and I paused a few times when I couldn't follow the English.

What interested me was seeing a famous player sitting down and having a conversation. Usually, I only watch short clips of people playing, so this felt more personal. It made me curious about what someone's life is like away from their job. I also thought about my own interests. Basketball is important to me, but so are my studies and family. I enjoyed the interview and talked about it with Leo the next time we played together.

观看情境：几个月前某晚在家用电脑看，Leo 发来链接；借字幕和暂停帮助理解。
感受与联系：从球场片段转向人物对话，感到更贴近个人生活；思考篮球之外，学业和家人也重要。

items.question: What kinds of people are usually interviewed?

items.answer: Job applicants are a common example. Journalists also interview public figures, experts and ordinary people who have experienced an event. items.question: Why do some people dislike being interviewed?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人不喜欢接受面试或采访？
items.answer: They may feel nervous about being judged or struggle to explain themselves under pressure. Someone can be good at a job without being a confident speaker. Unclear questions make this worse. A friendly introduction and a little thinking time can help people give a more accurate picture of their abilities.
items.ideaZh: 被评判和压力下表达令人紧张，提问含糊更难；友好开场和思考时间有帮助。

items.question: Why do some people think interviews are a waste of time?

items.answer: Some interviews repeat information already written in an application or ask questions that have little connection with the work. items.question: What should people do to prepare for a job interview?

items.answer: They should understand the role and prepare a few clear examples of relevant experience. Practising answers can help, but memorising every sentence may sound unnatural. items.question: Describe a person in your life who really likes taking photos.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你生活中很喜欢拍照的人。
cueCard: When and where he/she takes photos
Why you think he/she likes taking photos
And explain how you feel about him/her.
items.answer:
Someone I know who really enjoys taking photos is my girlfriend. We met through friends at university, and we gradually got to know each other better.

She takes photos in lots of ordinary places, such as parks, cafes and streets with interesting buildings. She usually uses her phone, so she doesn't need to carry much equipment. Sometimes she notices a small detail, like sunlight on a wall, that I would walk straight past.

We once went to Dadonghai Beach in Sanya together. I took lots of photos of her there, and she also took pictures of the sea and things we saw on our walk. I like this habit because the photos help us remember time we have spent together. I do sometimes ask her to put the phone away for a while, but mostly I enjoy taking part. She has taught me to pay more attention to the things around me.

She has taught me to pay more attention to the things around me.
cluesZh: 人物与相识：女朋友，大学时通过朋友认识，逐渐熟悉。

大东海例子与评价：我给她拍照，她拍海和沿途景物；照片留住相处时光，也让我更留意身边事物。

items.extension: When we look through the photos later, we often remember small moments we had forgotten. That is what makes the pictures valuable to us.

items.question: Do you think it's okay to take photos everywhere?
items.questionZh: 你认为任何地方都可以拍照吗？
items.answer: No, people should consider privacy, safety and the rules of the place. Taking a view of a beach is different from photographing a stranger closely without asking. items.question: Why do tourists like taking photos while they are travelling?

items.question: Describe a person who is well-organized.
items.questionZh: 描述一个有条理的人。
cueCard: Why you think he/she is well-organized
And explain how you feel about him/her.
items.answer:
The most organised person I know is my friend Leo. We became friends through basketball at school and study together, and I've noticed this quality whenever we have a group project.

He doesn't use a complicated system. At the start of each week, he writes a short list of things he needs to finish. He also keeps his computer files in clearly named folders, so he rarely wastes time looking for something.

Last term, we worked on a small website together. Before we started, he wrote down our tasks and made sure everyone knew what to do. When we had a problem, we could check the list and see what needed attention. This helped us finish without rushing at the last minute. I think being organised matters to him because he wants time for both studying and basketball. It helps him feel less stressed. I've started copying his habit of making a short daily list, and it really helps.

具体事例—意义—影响：网站项目先分工、遇事查清单，避免最后赶工；兼顾学习和篮球、减压，我也开始列每日清单。
translationsZh: 上学期，我们一起做了一个小网站。开始前，他写下各项任务，确保每个人都知道该做什么。遇到问题时，我们就能查清单，看看哪里需要处理。这让我们不用到最后一刻才匆忙赶工。我认为有条理对他很重要，因为他想同时留出学习和打篮球的时间。这也让他压力更小。我已经开始学习他列简短每日清单的习惯，确实很有帮助。

items.extension: He is flexible when plans change, though. If a task takes longer than expected, he adjusts the list instead of getting angry with everyone.

items.question: Why is it important for people to be organized?
items.questionZh: 有条理为什么重要？
items.answer: It reduces the time people spend searching for things or worrying about forgotten tasks. That leaves more attention for the work itself. For example, clear folders can make a group project easier to manage. Organisation should support daily life, rather than become another task that takes too much time.
items.ideaZh: 减少找东西和担心漏事的耗时，让人专注任务；整理应服务生活，不额外添负担。

items.question: Do you think children should learn to be organized from a young age?
items.questionZh: 孩子应该从小学习有条理吗？
items.answer: Yes, as long as the expectations match their age. A young child can learn to put toys back, while an older child can plan homework. These habits develop gradually. Expecting a child to manage a full adult-style schedule would probably create frustration rather than useful independence.
items.ideaZh: 应该但符合年龄，从收玩具到安排作业逐步来，不强加成人式日程。
items.vocab: expectations — 期望；gradually — 逐渐地
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: Are organized people more likely to be successful at work or in their studies?
items.questionZh: 有条理的人更容易在工作或学习中成功吗？
items.answer: Organisation can improve their chances because they are less likely to forget tasks or leave everything until the deadline. However, they still need relevant skills and effort. A beautifully arranged timetable won't help much if the person never actually starts the work or asks for help when they are stuck.
items.ideaZh: 能减少遗忘和拖延，但仍需技能与努力，漂亮时间表不能代替行动。
items.vocab: timetable — 时间表；relevant skills — 相关技能
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: What can people do to become more organized?
items.questionZh: 人们怎样变得更有条理？
items.answer: They can begin with a short list of priorities and a regular place for important things. Keeping the system simple matters, because a complicated plan is easy to abandon. For students, checking tomorrow's tasks at the end of the day can prevent a rushed start the next morning.
items.ideaZh: 列简短优先清单，重要物品固定位置，晚上看次日任务，系统应简单易坚持。
items.vocab: abandon — 放弃；rushed — 匆忙的
items.provenance: 观点示范：例子用于说明，不表示用户亲历；涉及群体时避免绝对化。

items.question: Should parents teach their children to be organized?
items.questionZh: 父母应该教孩子做事有条理吗？
items.answer: Yes, but they should teach it through simple routines rather than constant criticism. A parent could help a child choose a place for school things and prepare a bag the night before. As the habit becomes familiar, the child can take more responsibility without needing reminders every time.
items.ideaZh: 应该，通过简单习惯而非持续批评；先帮助整理书包，再逐步让孩子负责。
items.vocab: routines — 日常习惯；responsibility — 责任

items.question: Do you think it is important for managers to be well organized?
items.questionZh: 管理者做事有条理重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, because a manager's organisation affects other people's work. If tasks or deadlines are unclear, a whole team may waste time. Being organised doesn't mean planning every minute. It means making priorities clear, sharing information and adjusting the plan when something important changes.
items.ideaZh: 重要，任务和期限影响团队；有条理是明确重点、共享信息并适时调整。
items.vocab: deadlines — 截止日期；adjusting — 调整

items.question: Describe a person you know who likes to learn about history.
items.questionZh: 描述一个喜欢学历史的人。
cueCard: Why you think he/she likes to learn about history
What kinds of history he/she learns
And explain how you feel about him/her.
cueCardZh: 为什么觉得他喜欢历史
items.answer:
A person I know who enjoys learning history is my grandfather. He is especially interested in how ordinary people lived in the past, rather than just the names of famous rulers.

He watches history programmes and reads books with pictures and short explanations. When he finds an interesting story, he sometimes writes down a few notes or tells someone in the family about it. He also likes comparing what he has learned with things he remembers from his own childhood.

I think he loves history because it helps him understand how everyday life has changed. For example, he is curious about how people travelled, worked and communicated before modern technology. I don't share all of his interests, and sometimes I lose track of the names he mentions. However, I respect his curiosity. He shows me that learning doesn't have to stop when you leave school. I enjoy it most when we talk about a simple, real-life example.

学习方法：看历史节目和图文书，记笔记、与家人分享，并联系自己的童年回忆。
原因与评价：想了解日常生活如何改变；我不全懂他的兴趣，但尊重好奇心，体会离校后仍可持续学习。
translationsZh: 我觉得他热爱历史，是因为历史帮助他理解日常生活发生了怎样的变化。例如，他好奇现代科技出现以前，人们怎样出行、工作和交流。我并不对他喜欢的所有内容都感兴趣，有时也记不清他提到的人名。不过，我尊重他的好奇心。他让我看到，学习不必在离开学校时结束。我最喜欢的是，我们讨论简单、贴近实际生活的例子的时候。

items.extensionZh: 延伸：他的兴趣鼓励我多问过去的事；联系普通生活后，历史更容易理解。

items.question: Should people start learning history from a young age?
items.questionZh: 人们应该从小开始学历史吗？
items.answer: Yes, if it is presented in a way they can enjoy and understand. Old objects, pictures and family memories can make them curious about change. The aim should be interest and basic understanding. A long list of facts to memorise might make history feel difficult before they have a reason to care.
items.ideaZh: 可以，用物件图片和家人回忆激发好奇，先兴趣理解，别只要求背一堆事实。
items.vocab: curious — 好奇的；memorise — 记忆、背诵

items.question: At what age is it best for people to start learning history?
items.questionZh: 从什么年龄开始学历史最好？
items.answer: They can begin quite young through simple stories about family and local places. Formal study can become more detailed once they can understand time and compare accounts. I wouldn't choose one exact age for everyone. The approach matters more than starting early just to memorise names and dates.
items.ideaZh: 幼年可听家庭本地故事，理解时间后再深入；方式比统一规定年龄更重要。
items.vocab: formal study — 正式学习；compare accounts — 比较不同叙述

items.question: When people travel to a place, are they mainly interested in its local history?
items.questionZh: 旅行时人们主要对当地历史感兴趣吗？
items.answer: Some are, especially when visiting an old town or museum, but others are more interested in food, scenery or meeting people. The same visitor may enjoy several of these things. I think a little historical context can add meaning without becoming the only purpose of the trip.
items.ideaZh: 兴趣包括历史美食风景人际，可同时喜欢；历史背景增添意义但非唯一目的。
items.vocab: enjoy — 享受喜欢；people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Is it important to learn about how people lived in the past?
items.questionZh: 了解过去人们怎样生活重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, because it helps explain how daily habits and institutions developed. It can also make us question things we now take for granted. Learning how ordinary families lived gives history a human side, instead of making the past seem like a list of rulers, dates and battles.
items.ideaZh: 帮助理解习惯制度的形成，也反思习以为常之事，让历史有人情而非只有帝王战役。
items.vocab: take for granted — 认为理所当然；institutions — 制度
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.question: Should people learn about ancient history before they study modern history?
items.questionZh: 应该先学古代历史再学近代历史吗？
items.answer: Learning in time order can help people understand connections, but I don't think it must always start with ancient history. A familiar modern event may first make someone interested. A teacher can then explain the earlier background. The main thing is giving learners a clear sense of when things happened.
items.ideaZh: 时间顺序有帮助但不必强制，熟悉的近代事件也能激发兴趣，再追溯背景。
items.vocab: ancient history — 古代史；background — 背景

items.topic: 听不感兴趣的话但坚持听
items.question: Describe a time when someone talked about something you were not interested in but you kept listening.
items.questionZh: 描述一次别人讲你不感兴趣的事情但你坚持听的经历。
cueCard: And explain how you felt about the experience.
items.answer:
I remember a time when my grandfather talked about a history programme he had watched. It happened after lunch during a visit to his home.

He was explaining a long story about an old ruler and the people around him. There were lots of names, and I found it difficult to keep track of them. To be honest, I wasn't very interested at first. I had been hoping to talk about something closer to everyday life.

However, I kept listening because he clearly enjoyed sharing the story with me. I didn't want to make him feel that his interests were unimportant. Instead of checking my phone, I asked why he found that person interesting. His answer helped me understand the story a little better. I still wouldn't choose the programme myself, but I was glad I had stayed polite. The conversation mattered because it was time we were spending together.
paragraphs: I remember a time when my grandfather talked about a history programme he had watched. It happened after lunch during a visit to his home.

He was explaining a long story about an old ruler and the people around him. There were lots of names, and I found it difficult to keep track of them. To be honest, I wasn't very interested at first. I had been hoping to talk about something closer to everyday life.

However, I kept listening because he clearly enjoyed sharing the story with me. I didn't want to make him feel that his interests were unimportant. Instead of checking my phone, I asked why he found that person interesting. His answer helped me understand the story a little better. I still wouldn't choose the programme myself, but I was glad I had stayed polite. The conversation mattered because it was time we were spending together.
cluesZh: 场景：去爷爷家做客，午饭后听他讲看过的历史节目。
不感兴趣的原因：古代统治者和身边人物的长故事，名字太多、难跟上；原本更想聊日常生活。
继续倾听的理由与做法：尊重爷爷分享的热情，不看手机、主动问兴趣点；虽没爱上节目，但珍惜相处且庆幸保持礼貌。
translationsZh: 不过，我继续听了下去，因为他显然很享受和我分享这个故事。我不想让他觉得自己的兴趣无关紧要。我没有看手机，而是问他为什么觉得那个人有意思。他的回答让我稍微更理解了这个故事。我自己还是不会选择看那个节目，但很高兴自己一直保持礼貌。这次谈话重要，是因为我们正在一起度过一段时光。
items.provenance: 爷爷喜欢历史、一次午饭后的长谈和你的反应为拟写；同一人物设定可用于 N18。
items.extension: Afterwards, we moved on to another topic that we both enjoyed. I think taking turns like that makes a conversation more pleasant for everyone.

items.topic: 听不感兴趣的话但坚持听
items.question: What kind of topics do young people like to talk about today?
items.questionZh: 现在年轻人喜欢聊哪些话题？
items.answer: Among people I know, common topics include study, games, films and plans for the future. Friends also talk about everyday problems and funny things they've seen online. Interests vary, of course. A group of basketball fans may spend much more time discussing a match than another group would.
items.ideaZh: 从身边人说学习、游戏、电影和未来，也聊日常与网络趣事，兴趣不同话题不同。

items.topic: 听不感兴趣的话但坚持听
items.question: What would happen if the listener didn't listen carefully?
items.questionZh: 听众不认真听会怎样？
items.answer: They might miss an important detail or misunderstand what they are expected to do. In a group project, that could mean completing the wrong task and wasting time. It can also make the speaker feel ignored. Asking for clarification early is usually easier than fixing the result of a misunderstanding.
items.ideaZh: 可能漏掉细节、做错任务并让说者感到被忽略，早问清比事后补救容易。
items.vocab: clarification — 澄清；misunderstanding — 误解

items.topic: 听不感兴趣的话但坚持听
items.question: How can we tell if a listener is listening carefully?
items.questionZh: 怎样判断听众是否认真听？
items.answer: A careful listener usually responds to the actual point and asks relevant questions. They may briefly explain what they understood to check it. Eye contact can help, but it isn't proof on its own. Someone could look interested while thinking about something else, so the response matters more.
items.ideaZh: 看回应是否切题、是否提出相关问题和确认理解，眼神接触本身不是充分证明。

items.question: Describe a sportsperson that you know.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你知道的运动员。
cueCard: How well he/she plays this sport
And explain how you feel about him/her.
items.answer:
A successful sportsperson I admire is Michael Jordan. He played basketball and won six NBA championships with the Chicago Bulls. I first became interested in him through short videos of old games.

What catches my attention is how confident he looks on the court. I enjoy watching the way he moves with the ball and makes decisions quickly. As someone who plays basketball for fun, I know even simple actions can become difficult when other people are trying to stop you.

I don't know him personally, so I can't say exactly what he is like in private. From his public interviews, he seems very competitive and serious about what he does. I admire the level he reached, although I don't expect to become a professional player myself. Watching him makes me want to practise the basics and keep trying after mistakes. For me, his success is a reason to enjoy improving at my own level.

cluesZh: 人物与成就：迈克尔·乔丹，随芝加哥公牛队赢得六次 NBA 总冠军；通过旧比赛短视频开始关注。
吸引我的地方：场上自信，持球移动与快速决策出色；自己打球知道有防守时简单动作也不易。
谨慎评价与个人影响：不认识本人，只从公开采访看出好胜和认真；欣赏成就，激励自己练基础、失误后坚持，不必当职业球员。
translationsZh: 我并不认识他本人，所以无法确切说出他私下是什么样的人。从公开采访看，他似乎非常好胜，也认真对待自己做的事情。我敬佩他达到的水平，尽管我并不期望自己成为职业球员。看他打球让我想练好基本功，并在失误后继续尝试。对我来说，他的成功是一个动力，让我享受在自己的水平上不断进步。

items.question: What are the most popular sports in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家最流行哪些运动？
items.answer: I'd hesitate to name just one. Basketball is very visible around my school, and table tennis is another sport people commonly associate with China. The answer may also change depending on whether we mean playing or watching. My own interest in basketball probably makes me notice it more.
items.ideaZh: 不武断只选一个，可谈身边篮球和常被联想到的乒乓球，也区分参与与观看。

items.question: Do you agree that all students are willing to play sports?
items.questionZh: 所有学生都愿意参加运动吗？
items.answer: No, students differ in their interests and confidence. Someone may dislike competitive team games but enjoy swimming or walking. Offering several choices can help more students take part. I'd focus on finding an activity they feel comfortable trying rather than assuming reluctance means they are lazy.
items.ideaZh: 兴趣自信不同，给竞赛外选择，别把不愿参加某项等于懒。

items.question: What qualities make a top athlete?
items.questionZh: 顶尖运动员需要什么品质？
items.answer: An athlete needs discipline, patience and the ability to respond to setbacks. In team sports, listening and cooperating are important too. Losing a match or making a mistake shouldn't mean giving up. Being willing to review what happened and practise a specific weakness helps turn effort into improvement.
items.ideaZh: 自律、耐心、应对挫折和合作能力，愿意复盘并练具体弱点才能进步。

items.question: Describe a public building you enjoy spending time in (e.g. library, sports hall).
items.questionZh: 描述一个你喜欢待着的公共建筑。
cueCard: And explain why you enjoy spending time in it.
cueCardZh: 说明为什么喜欢待在那里
items.answer:
A public building I enjoy visiting is a library in Haikou, not too far from my home. I first heard about it from a friend who liked studying there.

The building looks quite simple from the outside, with large windows near the entrance. Inside, there are rows of bookshelves and plenty of desks. The reading area feels bright, and the seats are comfortable enough for a few hours of study. There are also clear signs, so it isn't difficult to find your way around.

I mainly go there when I need to concentrate on my university work or practise English. At home, I can easily get distracted by games or other things on my computer. In the library, seeing people quietly working helps me stay focused. I also like taking a short break to look at the books. It gives me a useful change of environment without making the day complicated or expensive.

items.question: Do people generally prefer to live in apartments rather than houses?
items.questionZh: 人们通常更喜欢公寓而不是独栋房屋吗？
items.answer: It depends on location, budget and daily needs. Apartments can be convenient near work or public transport, while a house may offer more space and privacy. Many people make a compromise rather than choose their ideal home, so what they live in doesn't always show what they prefer.
items.ideaZh: 看地点预算需求；实际住处可能是折中，不等于理想偏好。
items.vocab: rather than — 而不是；budget — 预算

items.question: Is it important to protect historical buildings? What are the benefits?
items.questionZh: 保护历史建筑重要吗？有什么益处？
items.answer: Yes, important buildings can help people understand a place's history in a way photographs alone can't. They also give an area a distinctive character. Preservation should make the building safe and useful where possible, rather than simply keeping an empty structure that nobody can maintain.
items.ideaZh: 实物历史和地方特色；保护兼顾安全用途维护，不只空壳保留。
items.vocab: rather than — 而不是；useful — 有用的

items.question: Which is more important - preserving historical buildings or building new ones?
items.questionZh: 保护历史建筑和建新建筑哪个更重要？
items.answer: I'd decide case by case. A historically valuable building deserves careful protection, while a city also needs safe homes and modern services. The best solution may combine an old building with a new use. Planning should consider real historical value and community needs, not simply age.
items.ideaZh: 逐案评估，兼顾历史价值与住房服务；旧建筑新用途可能兼顾双方。

items.question: Describe a person who you help to improve health and fitness.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你帮助改善健康和体能的人。
cueCard: And how you felt about him/her.
items.answer:
Someone I helped become more active was my cousin Ben. He spent a lot of his free time sitting at a computer and often said he felt tired after a short walk.

I suggested doing something together because I knew it would be easier than telling him to exercise on his own. We started with short walks and some relaxed basketball practice. We didn't keep score at first. We just passed the ball, took a few shots and stopped for a break when we needed one.

The difficult part was making it a regular habit. Sometimes he wanted to stay home, so we agreed on a simple plan that didn't take too much time. After a few weeks, he could stay active for longer and seemed to enjoy it more. I felt pleased because we were also spending good time together. I think having company helped him more than being told what he should do.
paragraphs: Someone I helped become more active was my cousin Ben. He spent a lot of his free time sitting at a computer and often said he felt tired after a short walk.

I suggested doing something together because I knew it would be easier than telling him to exercise on his own. We started with short walks and some relaxed basketball practice. We didn't keep score at first. We just passed the ball, took a few shots and stopped for a break when we needed one.

The difficult part was making it a regular habit. Sometimes he wanted to stay home, so we agreed on a simple plan that didn't take too much time. After a few weeks, he could stay active for longer and seemed to enjoy it more. I felt pleased because we were also spending good time together. I think having company helped him more than being told what he should do.
cluesZh: 人物与起因：表亲 Ben 久坐电脑前，常说走一会儿就累，我帮助他增加活动。
方法：陪他做，比叫他独自锻炼更容易；从短距离散步、轻松传球投篮开始，不计分，需要时就休息。
难点与结果：规律坚持最难，所以约定短小可行的计划；几周后活动时间变长、更加享受，陪伴比说教有效。
translationsZh: 困难之处在于把它变成固定习惯。有时他想待在家里，所以我们商量了一个不太占时间的简单计划。几周后，他能持续活动更久，看起来也更享受运动了。我很高兴，因为我们也一起度过了愉快的时光。我觉得，有人陪着，比别人告诉他应该做什么，更能帮助他。
items.provenance: 表弟 Ben 为拟写人物；散步、轻松投篮与体能改善是练习设定，不涉及疾病治疗或医疗建议。
items.extension: I also enjoyed the extra exercise myself. Helping him gave both of us a reason to leave our screens and spend some time outside.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：我自己也享受增加的运动；帮助他也让我们都有理由离开屏幕、走到户外。

items.question: Is it important to have a healthy community?
items.questionZh: 拥有健康的社区重要吗？
items.answer: Yes, a neighbourhood with clean public spaces and places to walk makes everyday life more comfortable. It also gives residents practical opportunities to be active or meet others. I'd think of a healthy community as one that supports useful habits, rather than expecting every resident to live in exactly the same way.
items.ideaZh: 清洁步道活动交往条件支持好习惯；不是要求人人相同生活方式。
items.vocab: practical — 实用的；comfortable — 舒适的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Does living in a healthy community give people a sense of belonging?
items.questionZh: 健康社区能给人归属感吗？
items.answer: It can, especially when residents use shared spaces and gradually recognise each other. A walking group or a small community activity gives people a reason to interact. However, attractive facilities alone aren't enough. People also need to feel welcome and able to participate without being judged.
items.ideaZh: 共享活动形成熟面孔，但设施之外还需接纳和参与机会。
items.vocab: gradually — 逐渐地；people — 人们

items.question: Does the government have a responsibility or role to play in building healthy communities?
items.questionZh: 政府有责任建设健康社区吗？
items.answer: I think it has a role in providing clean public spaces, safe routes and accessible facilities. Individual residents can't organise all of that themselves. At the same time, residents should help by respecting shared areas and taking part in decisions. Cooperation makes the facilities more useful.
items.ideaZh: 公共空间安全和可及设施需公共组织；居民爱护并参与决策，双方合作。

items.topic: 为特殊事件举办的派对
items.question: Describe a party which was held for a special event.
items.questionZh: 描述一个为特殊事件举办的派对。
cueCard: What people were doing at the party
And explain how you felt about it.
items.answer:
A party that impressed me was a birthday gathering for my grandfather. We held it at his home on a weekend last year, and about eight family members came.

It wasn't a large or expensive party. My mother cooked noodles, and everyone brought something to share. We helped put the food on the table and moved a few chairs so we could all sit together. After eating, we took some family photos and listened to my grandfather tell stories.

What impressed me most was how pleased he looked to have everyone there. He didn't seem particularly interested in presents. He wanted to know how we were doing and whether we were enjoying ourselves. I usually spend a lot of my free time on a computer, so it felt good to have an evening like that. The party reminded me that being present and paying attention can mean a lot to someone you care about.
paragraphs: A party that impressed me was a birthday gathering for my grandfather. We held it at his home on a weekend last year, and about eight family members came.

It wasn't a large or expensive party. My mother cooked noodles, and everyone brought something to share. We helped put the food on the table and moved a few chairs so we could all sit together. After eating, we took some family photos and listened to my grandfather tell stories.

What impressed me most was how pleased he looked to have everyone there. He didn't seem particularly interested in presents. He wanted to know how we were doing and whether we were enjoying ourselves. I usually spend a lot of my free time on a computer, so it felt good to have an evening like that. The party reminded me that being present and paying attention can mean a lot to someone you care about.
cluesZh: 背景：去年某个周末在爷爷家为他过生日，约八位家人参加。
活动：规模不大、花费不高；母亲煮面，大家带吃的、摆桌搬椅，饭后合照并听爷爷讲故事。
印象深的原因：爷爷更在意家人到场和近况，而非礼物；离开电脑认真陪伴，让我感受到在场和关注的重要。
translationsZh: 最让我印象深刻的是，看到大家都来了，他显得特别高兴。他似乎并不特别在意礼物。他想知道我们最近怎么样、是否玩得开心。我平时很多空闲时间都花在电脑上，所以能这样度过一个晚上，感觉很好。这次聚会提醒我，对自己在乎的人来说，亲自陪伴并认真关注他们，可能意义很大。
items.provenance: 拟写爷爷生日、周末在家、约八位家人、母亲做面条和合照，不当作已确认往事。
items.extension: I still like looking at the photos from that evening. They remind me of a relaxed moment when nobody was in a hurry to leave.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：现在仍喜欢看当晚照片，想起那段谁都不急着离开的轻松时光。

items.topic: 为特殊事件举办的派对
items.question: When do people usually hold parties in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家人们通常什么时候办派对？
items.answer: People often hold parties to mark a birthday, achievement or major life change. They also need a time when guests are available, so weekends can be convenient. A party doesn't need a big reason, though; sometimes friends simply want a chance to get together after being busy for a while.
items.ideaZh: 生日、成就或人生变化时常办，也要大家有空；有时只是忙后想团聚。
items.vocab: mark — 纪念；get together — 相聚
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.topic: 为特殊事件举办的派对
items.question: Do people prefer to hold parties in public places or in their own homes?
items.questionZh: 人们更喜欢在公共场所还是家里办派对？
items.answer: It depends on the size and purpose of the party. A private home feels personal and gives people more control, but preparation and cleaning take work. A public venue may be easier for a large group. I'd think about the guests' comfort and the practical effort before choosing.
items.ideaZh: 看规模目的，家里亲切可控但需准备清洁，公共场所可能更适合大群体。
items.vocab: venue — 场地；preparation — 准备
items.provenance: 观点示范：群体判断为个人看法，举例不表示用户亲历。

items.topic: 为特殊事件举办的派对
items.question: Is it important to provide food at a party?
items.questionZh: 派对提供食物重要吗？
items.answer: Usually, because sharing food helps people relax and gives guests something to do while talking. It doesn't have to be a costly meal. A few suitable snacks can work well, especially if the host considers different preferences and how long the gathering is expected to last.
items.ideaZh: 食物帮助放松聊天，不必昂贵，考虑偏好与聚会时长。

items.question: Describe a course that impressed you a lot.
items.questionZh: 描述一门令你印象深刻的课程。
cueCard: What you did during the course
And explain why it impressed you a lot.
items.answer:
A course that impressed me was an introductory programming course at university. I study computer science, so it was closely related to my major, but it changed how I thought about using a computer.

During the course, we made a simple program for keeping a list of tasks. At first, I thought writing the code would be straightforward. However, small mistakes kept stopping it from working. Our teacher encouraged us to test one part at a time instead of changing everything together. I tried that method and gradually found the problems.

When the program finally worked, it felt different from simply finishing an exercise on paper. I could enter something and see a useful result. The course impressed me because it connected an abstract idea with something practical. It also taught me that being stuck doesn't always mean I'm bad at a subject. Sometimes I just need a clearer method and enough patience to follow it.

课堂做什么：任务清单小程序出错，老师指导分步测试，逐渐找到问题；细节为拟写。
印象深刻的原因：程序能实际使用带来成就感，抽象知识有结果；卡住可能是方法问题。

items.extension: I still have plenty to learn, but that small success made me more willing to try difficult tasks rather than avoid them immediately.
items.extensionZh: 小成功增强尝试困难任务的意愿，不意味着已经熟练。

items.question: What do people need to remember in their daily lives?
items.questionZh: 人们日常需要记住什么？
items.answer: Appointments, deadlines, names and practical details such as where they left their keys are common examples. Forgetting them can affect other people as well as the individual. I think people should focus their memory on important information and use a reliable system for routine reminders.
items.ideaZh: 预约截止名字钥匙都重要；重要信息记住，重复提醒可借系统。
items.vocab: practical — 实用的；routine — 日常安排
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: What can we learn from history?
items.questionZh: 我们能从历史学到什么？
items.answer: We can learn how earlier choices affected people's lives and why certain traditions or institutions developed. History also shows that a situation can have several causes. I wouldn't treat the past as a simple instruction book, but it can help us ask better questions about decisions today.
items.ideaZh: 理解选择后果、传统制度成因和多重原因；历史帮助提问，不是简单照搬。
items.vocab: help — 帮助；people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Why do some people have a better memory than others?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人记忆力比别人好？
items.answer: Some people pay closer attention or connect new information with something meaningful. They may also use effective habits, such as reviewing instead of trying to remember everything at once. The task matters too; someone can remember sports results easily but struggle with names they rarely use.
items.ideaZh: 专注、意义关联、复习和领域兴趣共同作用；不同任务表现可不同。
items.vocab: attention — 注意力；remember — 记住
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Do people like things of memorial significance?
items.questionZh: 人们喜欢有纪念意义的东西吗？
items.answer: Many do, because an ordinary object can bring back a person or an experience. A photograph or a small gift may mean more than something expensive with no connection to their life. Not everyone keeps physical objects, though; some people prefer digital photos or simply remembering the event.
items.ideaZh: 纪念价值来自经历人际，不在价格；也有人以数字照片替代实物。
items.vocab: experience — 经历经验；because — 因为
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Which can help people remember things better, words or photos?
items.questionZh: 文字还是照片更能帮助人记忆？
items.answer: Photos are useful for recalling a scene or a face, while words can record details that aren't visible, such as what someone said. I'd often use both. A short note beside a photograph can explain why the moment mattered when the image alone no longer tells the whole story.
items.ideaZh: 照片提醒场景面孔，文字补对话意义；照片旁短注释结合最好。
items.vocab: useful — 有用的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Can technology help people remember things better? How?
items.questionZh: 科技能帮助记忆吗？怎样帮助？
items.answer: Yes, calendars, reminders and searchable notes help people keep track of information. They are especially useful for repeated tasks or dates. However, the system needs to be organised and checked. Saving something in a place you never look at doesn't necessarily make it easier to remember or use.
items.ideaZh: 日历提醒笔记有用，但要整理查看；存了不等于会想起。
items.vocab: useful — 有用的；remember — 记住
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 节约大量时间的方法或改变
items.question: Describe a way/change that helps you save a lot of time.
items.questionZh: 描述一个帮助你节省很多时间的方法或改变。
cueCard: And explain how you feel about the way/change.
items.answer:
A change that helps me save time is organising my study files into clear folders. Before doing this, I often saved documents wherever was easiest and then struggled to find the right version later.

Now I keep a folder for each course and use simple file names that include the task and date. When I download something, I put it in the correct place straight away. Once a week, I spend a few minutes removing repeated copies and checking that important work is easy to find.

The change wasn't technically difficult, but keeping the habit took some effort. At first I still wanted to leave things on the desktop. What helped was making the system simple enough to use every day. I feel less frustrated now because I can start working instead of searching through a long list. It doesn't make every task faster, but it removes small delays that used to happen repeatedly.

Now I keep a folder for each course and use simple file names that include the task and date. When I download something, I put it in the correct place straight away. Once a week, I spend a few minutes removing repeated copies and checking that important work is easy to find.

cluesZh: 方法和问题：整理学习文件夹，过去随手存放导致找不到版本；整个习惯为新增草稿。
怎样执行：一科一文件夹，任务加日期命名，下载时归位，每周整理重复文件。
难易和感受：技术不难，难在坚持；系统简化后减少反复查找，不夸大所有任务都提速。

items.extension: I would recommend starting with just a few useful folders. A very complicated system could take more time to maintain than it actually saves.
items.extensionZh: 建议少量清晰文件夹，复杂系统可能维护成本更高。

items.topic: 节约大量时间的方法或改变
items.question: Is it necessary for children to learn time management?
items.questionZh: 儿童有必要学习时间管理吗？
items.answer: Yes, at an age-appropriate level. Learning to leave time for homework, play and sleep can make a day feel less rushed. Children don't need a complicated schedule, though. A simple routine and a chance to make small choices can teach the idea gradually.
items.ideaZh: 按年龄教，协调作业玩耍睡眠，用简单作息和小选择而非复杂表格。
items.vocab: routine — 日常安排；gradually — 逐渐地
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 节约大量时间的方法或改变
items.question: What can schools do to help students learn time management?
items.questionZh: 学校怎样帮助学生学习时间管理？
items.answer: Teachers can show how to break an assignment into smaller stages and discuss how long each stage might take. Giving students some choice in planning is useful too. The goal should be realistic judgement, rather than filling every minute or punishing someone whenever an estimate is wrong.
items.ideaZh: 作业拆步估时并允许学生安排；学合理判断，不把每分钟填满或惩罚估错。

items.topic: 节约大量时间的方法或改变
items.question: What can people do to save time?
items.questionZh: 人们怎样节约时间？
items.answer: They can prepare frequently used things in advance, group similar tasks and avoid unnecessary interruptions. For example, keeping study files in clear folders saves repeated searching. It's also worth checking priorities, because doing an unimportant task faster doesn't always make the whole day more useful.
items.ideaZh: 准备归类减少打断，文件夹例子；先看优先级，再追速度。
items.vocab: clear — 清楚的；useful — 有用的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 节约大量时间的方法或改变
items.question: Does technology help people save time? How and why?
items.questionZh: 科技帮助人们省时间吗？怎样以及为什么？
items.answer: It can make searching, communication and routine work much quicker. A shared document, for example, avoids sending several versions back and forth. But technology also creates distractions. It saves time when people use a suitable tool for a clear purpose, rather than switching between apps without a plan.
items.ideaZh: 共享文档节约往返，但工具也分心；明确用途选择合适工具才省时。
items.vocab: routine — 日常安排；rather than — 而不是
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.topic: 节约大量时间的方法或改变
items.question: Do you think parents should be responsible for teaching children to save time?
items.questionZh: 父母应负责教孩子节约时间吗？
items.answer: Yes, they can model simple habits, such as preparing a schoolbag the night before. But the responsibility shouldn't fall on parents alone; schools can reinforce the same ideas. Adults also need to leave room for rest and play, so saving time doesn't become constant pressure to be productive.
items.ideaZh: 父母示范前晚备包，学校巩固；也要留休息娱乐空间，避免效率压力。

items.topic: 节约大量时间的方法或改变
items.question: Do people who can manage time well become successful more easily?
items.questionZh: 善于时间管理的人更容易成功吗？
items.answer: It can help them practise regularly and finish important work without leaving everything until the last moment. However, time management can't replace skill, resources or help from other people. I'd describe it as a useful advantage, not a guarantee that every carefully planned effort will succeed.
items.ideaZh: 能稳定练习按时完成是优势，但不能取代技能资源支持，不保证成功。

items.question: Describe a gift you would like to buy for your friend.
items.questionZh: 描述一件你想买给朋友的礼物。
cueCard: How long you have known him/her
How you would choose a gift for him/her
And explain why you would choose that gift for him/her.
items.answer:
A gift I'd like to buy for a friend is a basketball. The friend is Leo, whom I got to know through playing at school. We've known each other for several years and often play together.

I'd choose the gift by thinking about what he actually uses, rather than buying something simply because it looks expensive. I'd look for a ball that's comfortable to handle and suitable for the courts we normally use. I'd compare a few options and keep the price within a budget I could manage as a student.

The reason I'd choose it is that basketball is part of our friendship. I remember making a mistake during a game and receiving encouragement from him. A practical gift connected with something we enjoy would feel more personal than an unrelated item. I haven't bought it yet, but I like the idea of giving him something we could use together instead of leaving it on a shelf.

如何选择：看是否常用、手感和场地适配，比较选项并控制学生预算。
原因：联系真实鼓励经历，礼物与共同爱好和友谊有关；明确尚未购买，不把设想写成已发生。

items.extension: I'd probably ask a casual question about what kind of ball he likes first, so the surprise wouldn't come at the cost of choosing something unsuitable.
items.extensionZh: 先随意了解偏好，避免为了惊喜而送错。

items.question: When do people normally send gifts to others?
items.questionZh: 人们通常什么时候送礼？
items.answer: Birthdays, weddings and festivals are common occasions, but a gift can also express thanks or encouragement. The meaning depends on the relationship and situation. I think an unexpected small gift can be particularly memorable when it shows that someone has paid attention to what another person needs.
items.ideaZh: 生日婚礼节日及感谢鼓励；小而用心的意外礼物也令人难忘。

items.question: Is it hard to choose a gift?
items.questionZh: 挑选礼物难吗？
items.answer: It can be difficult if you don't know the person's interests or what they already own. A close friend is often easier to buy for because you notice their habits. I'd rather ask a simple question than spend a lot on something impressive but completely unsuitable.
items.ideaZh: 不了解偏好和已有物品会难；熟朋友较易，不确定就问而非盲目求贵。
items.vocab: because — 因为

items.question: Will people feel happy when receiving an expensive gift?
items.questionZh: 收到昂贵礼物一定会高兴吗？
items.answer: Not necessarily. They may appreciate the generosity, but an expensive gift can also make someone feel uncomfortable or obliged to return the favour. A thoughtful present at a comfortable price may feel better. I think the relationship and the intention matter more than the amount spent.
items.ideaZh: 昂贵可能带来回礼压力，合适价格更自在；关系心意比金额重要。
items.vocab: comfortable — 舒适的；thoughtful — 考虑周到的

items.question: Which do people give on traditional festivals, red envelopes or other kinds of gifts?
items.questionZh: 传统节日人们送红包还是其他礼物？
items.answer: Both can be appropriate, depending on the festival and relationship. In my experience, red envelopes are familiar at family celebrations, while food or something useful may suit other visits. I wouldn't assume every family follows the same custom, so I'd consider what the recipient is comfortable receiving.
items.ideaZh: 红包礼物都可能，随节日关系和家庭习惯选择，不说全国统一规则。
items.vocab: comfortable — 舒适的；experience — 经历经验

items.question: What do people usually consider when buying gifts?
items.questionZh: 买礼物时人们通常考虑什么？
items.answer: They think about the recipient's interests, the occasion and their own budget. Practical details matter too, such as whether the person has space for the item. I think the best starting point is what would be useful or meaningful to them, rather than what makes the giver look generous.
items.ideaZh: 兴趣场合预算空间，优先接受者的意义用途，不是赠送者显得阔绰。

items.question: Are there any unlucky things that people should not buy as gifts in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家有没有不宜作为礼物的不吉利物品？
items.answer: Yes, clocks are a familiar example because their Chinese name has an unlucky association. However, people differ in how seriously they take that tradition. I'd ask about a recipient's preferences rather than assume a rule applies to every family. A gift should make the person feel comfortable.

items.question: Describe an occasion that you lost something in public.
items.questionZh: 描述一次你在公共场所丢东西的经历。
cueCard: When and where you lost it
What you did to find it
And explain how you felt about it.
items.answer:
An occasion when I lost something in public was during a visit to a shopping mall in Haikou with my girlfriend. We'd been looking at headphones, and I realised my wallet wasn't in my pocket.

At first, I checked my bag and all my pockets because I thought I'd simply put it somewhere unusual. Then we went back to the places we'd just visited. I remembered taking it out near a seat, but it wasn't there when we returned. We asked at the service desk and described the wallet without giving out more personal details than necessary.

Fortunately, someone had handed it in. I checked that it was mine and thanked the staff. I felt very relieved, because replacing the things inside would have taken time and spoiled the rest of the day. I was also annoyed with myself for not checking the seat before leaving. Since then, I've tried to keep important items in the same place and do a quick check whenever I move on.

At first, I checked my bag and all my pockets because I thought I'd simply put it somewhere unusual. Then we went back to the places we'd just visited. Fortunately, someone had handed it in. I checked that it was mine and thanked the staff. I felt very relieved, because replacing the things inside would have taken time and spoiled the rest of the day. I was also annoyed with myself for not checking the seat before leaving. Since then, I've tried to keep important items in the same place and do a quick check whenever I move on.
cluesZh: 物品、何时何地：与女朋友去海口商场看耳机时发现钱包不见；新增草稿。
寻找步骤：先包和口袋，再原路找，最后服务台说明外观；不把不必要个人信息公开。
结果感受：被交到服务台，核对取回，松口气也自责；之后固定位置、离开前检查。
