items.extension: The experience also made me appreciate the person who returned it. A small honest action can save someone else a great deal of worry.
items.extensionZh: 感谢归还者，小行动减少别人的担忧。

items.question: What kinds of things do people usually lose?
items.questionZh: 人们通常会丢什么东西？
items.answer: Small things people carry around, such as keys, wallets, phones and umbrellas, are easy to leave behind. It often happens when someone puts an item down temporarily and moves on. A change of routine can also make familiar habits less reliable, especially during a busy journey.
items.ideaZh: 钥匙钱包手机伞等随身小物，临时放下与匆忙换作息易忘。
items.vocab: routine — 日常安排；reliable — 可靠的

items.question: What will people do when losing things?
items.questionZh: 丢了东西人们会怎么做？
items.answer: They usually check where they last remember using it and retrace their steps. Asking staff about a lost-property desk can help in a public place. If the item contains important personal information, they may also need to protect that information while continuing to look for the object.
items.ideaZh: 回想最后位置沿路找，问失物处；重要信息物品还需注意保护信息。

items.question: Is it effective to offer rewards to find lost things?
items.questionZh: 提供酬谢寻找失物有效吗？
items.answer: It may encourage someone to make an extra effort to return an item, particularly if doing so takes time. But many people return things without expecting payment. Clear contact information and a practical way to arrange the return may be more helpful than a large reward alone.
items.ideaZh: 酬谢可补付出，但很多人不求钱；联系方式和归还安排可能更有用。
items.vocab: practical — 实用的；clear — 清楚的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: What kinds of people may lose things often?
items.questionZh: 哪些人可能经常丢东西？
items.answer: People who are distracted or rushing between several tasks may forget where they put things. Someone in an unfamiliar place may also lack their usual routine. I wouldn't attach it to one personality type; even a careful person can lose something when their attention is elsewhere.
items.ideaZh: 分心忙碌陌生环境增加风险，不用固定人群标签；细心者也会分神。
items.vocab: routine — 日常安排；attention — 注意力

items.question: What can we do to reduce the possibility of losing things?
items.questionZh: 怎样减少丢东西的可能？
items.answer: Keeping important objects in the same place is useful, along with a quick check before leaving a seat or vehicle. People can also carry fewer unnecessary things. I prefer a simple habit that works every day rather than relying on remembering a long checklist when I'm already rushing.
items.ideaZh: 固定位置、离开前检查、少带杂物；简单日常习惯优于忙时长清单。

items.question: What do people often feel after losing things?
items.questionZh: 丢东西后人们通常什么感受？
items.answer: They may feel worried, frustrated or annoyed with themselves, especially if the object is expensive or contains personal memories. Uncertainty about getting it back can make the feeling worse. Even losing a cheap item can be upsetting if replacing it creates a lot of extra work.
items.ideaZh: 担心沮丧自责，不确定加重；便宜东西若有记忆或补办麻烦也会难受。

items.topic: 印象深刻的特殊活动聚会
items.question: Describe a party for a special event that impressed you a lot.
items.questionZh: 描述一个令你印象深刻的特殊事件聚会。
cueCard: When and where it was held
What the party was held for
And explain why it impressed you a lot.
items.answer:
A party that impressed me was a birthday gathering for my grandfather. We held it at his home on a weekend last year, and about eight family members came.

It wasn't a large or expensive party. My mother cooked noodles, and everyone brought something to share. We helped put the food on the table and moved a few chairs so we could all sit together. After eating, we took some family photos and listened to my grandfather tell stories.

What impressed me most was how pleased he looked to have everyone there. He didn't seem particularly interested in presents. He wanted to know how we were doing and whether we were enjoying ourselves. I usually spend a lot of my free time on a computer, so it felt good to have an evening like that. The party reminded me that being present and paying attention can mean a lot to someone you care about.

It wasn't a large or expensive party. My mother cooked noodles, and everyone brought something to share. We helped put the food on the table and moved a few chairs so we could all sit together. After eating, we took some family photos and listened to my grandfather tell stories.

What impressed me most was how pleased he looked to have everyone there. He didn't seem particularly interested in presents. He wanted to know how we were doing and whether we were enjoying ourselves. I usually spend a lot of my free time on a computer, so it felt good to have an evening like that. The party reminded me that being present and paying attention can mean a lot to someone you care about.
cluesZh: 背景：去年某个周末在爷爷家为他过生日，约八位家人参加。
活动：规模不大、花费不高；母亲煮面，大家带吃的、摆桌搬椅，饭后合照并听爷爷讲故事。
印象深的原因：爷爷更在意家人到场和近况，而非礼物；离开电脑认真陪伴，让我感受到在场和关注的重要。
translationsZh: 最让我印象深刻的是，看到大家都来了，他显得特别高兴。他似乎并不特别在意礼物。他想知道我们最近怎么样、是否玩得开心。我平时很多空闲时间都花在电脑上，所以能这样度过一个晚上，感觉很好。这次聚会提醒我，对自己在乎的人来说，亲自陪伴并认真关注他们，可能意义很大。
items.provenance: 拟写爷爷生日、周末在家、约八位家人、母亲做面条和合照，不当作已确认往事。
items.extension: I still like looking at the photos from that evening. They remind me of a relaxed moment when nobody was in a hurry to leave.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：现在仍喜欢看当晚照片，想起那段谁都不急着离开的轻松时光。

items.topic: 印象深刻的特殊活动聚会
items.question: When do people like to hold a party?
items.questionZh: 人们什么时候喜欢办聚会？
items.answer: People often hold parties to mark a birthday, achievement or major life change. They also need a time when guests are available, so weekends can be convenient. A party doesn't need a big reason, though; sometimes friends simply want a chance to get together after being busy for a while.
items.ideaZh: 生日、成就或人生变化时常办，也要大家有空；有时只是忙后想团聚。

items.topic: 印象深刻的特殊活动聚会
items.question: Do you think people nowadays prefer attending big parties or small gatherings with close friends? Why?
items.questionZh: 现在人们更喜欢大派对还是亲友小聚？为什么？
items.answer: Both appeal to different people, but a small gathering often makes conversation easier. Guests can spend proper time together without planning a large event. A big party can suit a major celebration, though. I'd choose based on the purpose rather than assume one size is fashionable for everyone.
items.ideaZh: 小聚好交谈易安排，大活动适合重大庆祝；看目的而不假设流行偏好。

items.question: Are there any differences between how young people and older people celebrate events with parties?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与年长者用派对庆祝有什么不同？
items.answer: Some younger people prefer active games or louder music, while older guests may value a comfortable meal and time to talk. Those are only tendencies, though. A family gathering works better when the host considers the actual guests instead of planning entirely around assumptions about their ages.
items.ideaZh: 活动音乐与舒适聊天可能有差异，但按实际客人需求，避免年龄刻板。

items.question: What special events are celebrated in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家庆祝哪些特殊活动？
items.answer: People celebrate festivals such as Chinese New Year, as well as personal occasions like birthdays, weddings and graduations. Different events bring different groups together. A festival may involve wider family traditions, while a graduation party is often a chance to recognise someone's effort and enjoy the moment with friends.
items.ideaZh: 春节等节日，以及生日婚礼毕业，分别联系家庭传统或个人成就。

items.topic: 印象深刻的特殊活动聚会
items.question: Do you think it's a waste of money for governments to celebrate national events?
items.questionZh: 政府花钱庆祝全国性事件是浪费吗？
items.answer: Not automatically. A well-planned celebration can give people a shared experience and recognise something meaningful. But the cost should be reasonable, and essential services still matter. I'd question an expensive display that offers little lasting value, rather than dismiss every public celebration as a waste.
items.ideaZh: 共同意义可值得，成本须合理且兼顾基本服务；不一概浪费。

items.topic: 印象深刻的特殊活动聚会
items.question: What festivals are the most important for people in your country?
items.questionZh: 你们国家哪些节日最重要？
items.answer: Spring Festival is especially meaningful to many families because people try to come together and share meals. Other festivals can matter for different reasons, such as remembering relatives or spending time outdoors. I'd say importance is partly cultural and partly connected with a family's own memories.
items.ideaZh: 春节团聚很重要，其他节日有各自意义；重视程度也看家庭记忆。

items.topic: 特殊节日的食物（版本一）
items.question: Describe a kind of food that you ate at special occasions.
items.questionZh: 描述一种你在特殊场合吃过的食物。
cueCard: What occasion or event it was
How it is cooked or made
Why you would like to eat it
And explain why people eat it on that special occasion or event.
cueCardZh: 说明人们为什么在那个场合吃它
items.answer:
A food people eat on special occasions is noodles, especially for birthdays. In the version I know from family meals, the noodles are fairly simple, but the occasion gives them meaning.

My mother usually cooks the noodles in water and serves them with vegetables, an egg and a light soup. The important thing is to keep the noodles long rather than cut them into tiny pieces. Long noodles are associated with wishes for a long life, so they fit a birthday celebration well.

We had them at a small gathering for my grandfather's birthday. Everyone sat around the table, shared food and talked, which made the meal feel warm and personal. I like this kind of food because it doesn't need to be expensive or difficult to prepare. The meaning comes from the care behind it. For me, eating it is a way to celebrate someone and enjoy time together as a family.

做法与寓意：水煮后配菜、鸡蛋和清汤，保持面条长而不切碎，象征长寿祝福。
何时何地与意义：在爷爷家生日聚餐吃面，温暖团圆；聚会细节为旧草稿。
items.provenance: 拟写你家生日吃面条的习惯和母亲做法；面条表达长寿祝愿为常见文化解释，不要求用户背具体地方菜工艺。
items.extension: The taste is familiar, which makes it comforting too. Even a simple bowl of noodles feels special when someone has prepared it for your birthday.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：熟悉的味道令人安心；专为生日准备时，普通一碗面也特别。

items.topic: 特殊节日的食物（版本一）
items.question: Why are there special foods on special occasions or events?
items.questionZh: 为什么特殊场合会有特别的食物？
items.answer: Special food helps people recognise an occasion and connect it with shared memories. Preparing and eating it together can become part of the celebration. The meaning may be more important than the cost. Birthday noodles, for example, can express a wish for a long life through a familiar family meal.
items.ideaZh: 食物标记节日、连接共同回忆，准备和分享也是庆祝的一部分；如长寿面表达祝愿，意义不在价格。
items.vocab: occasion — 场合；express a wish — 表达祝愿

items.topic: 特殊节日的食物（版本一）
items.question: Are there any differences between the food people eat today and the food people ate in the past?
items.questionZh: 现在和过去人们吃的东西有什么不同？
items.answer: People in some places now have more choices and easier access to food from other regions. Ordering a prepared meal may also fit a busy schedule. Still, traditional home cooking remains important to many families. The differences depend on location and lifestyle, so there isn't one experience shared by everyone.
items.ideaZh: 部分地区选择更多、外地食物更容易获得，忙碌时也会点餐；家常传统饮食仍重要，差异取决于地区和生活方式。

items.question: Describe a problem with technology you have encountered, like a computer or a cell phone.
items.questionZh: 描述一次遇到的电脑手机等科技故障。
cueCard: When and where you had this problem
And explain how you felt when you had this problem.
items.answer:
A challenging technology problem I faced was when my computer suddenly showed a blue screen while I was playing a game. It happened at home one evening last term.

At first, I thought restarting it would solve everything, but I was still worried. I use the same computer for my university work, so I didn't want a problem with a game to affect my files or studies. The difficult part was not knowing whether the issue came from the software or the hardware.

I decided to check simple things first. I turned the computer off, disconnected the power and carefully cleaned the dust from it. After that, it worked normally again. I can't say that dust was definitely the only cause, but cleaning it solved the problem that time. I felt relieved and quite pleased that I had managed to deal with it. The experience reminded me to look after the equipment I depend on.
paragraphs: A challenging technology problem I faced was when my computer suddenly showed a blue screen while I was playing a game. It happened at home one evening last term.

At first, I thought restarting it would solve everything, but I was still worried. I use the same computer for my university work, so I didn't want a problem with a game to affect my files or studies. The difficult part was not knowing whether the issue came from the software or the hardware.

I decided to check simple things first. I turned the computer off, disconnected the power and carefully cleaned the dust from it. After that, it worked normally again. I can't say that dust was definitely the only cause, but cleaning it solved the problem that time. I felt relieved and quite pleased that I had managed to deal with it. The experience reminded me to look after the equipment I depend on.
cluesZh: 问题场景：上学期某晚在家打游戏，电脑突然蓝屏。
担忧与难点：起初以为重启即可，但同一电脑还用于功课，担心文件和学习受影响，难确定软硬件原因。
解决与限定：先关机断电清灰，之后恢复正常；不认定灰尘必然是唯一原因，只说明当次清灰后解决，感到放心并提醒自己维护设备。
translationsZh: 我决定先检查简单的地方。我关闭电脑、断开电源，然后仔细清理里面的灰尘。之后，它又能正常工作了。我不能说灰尘肯定是唯一原因，但那次清理确实解决了问题。我松了口气，也挺高兴自己处理好了。这次经历提醒我，要照顾好自己依赖的设备。
items.provenance: 真实：电脑打游戏时蓝屏，清灰后解决。补充：上学期在家、重启、担心资料、排查感受和断电清理过程。未确诊故障成因。
items.extension: I also became more careful about keeping copies of important files. That way, an unexpected computer problem would be less stressful in the future.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：之后也更注意备份重要文件，减少未来突发故障带来的压力。

items.question: What tech products do you use at home?
items.questionZh: 你在家用什么科技产品？
items.answer: I mainly use a computer and a phone for studying, communication and entertainment. Other household devices support ordinary tasks like cooking or washing. I think the useful question is what each device actually makes easier, because having more technology doesn't necessarily mean a more comfortable home.
items.ideaZh: 电脑手机加日常家电，按用途看价值，不把设备数量等于生活质量。
items.vocab: comfortable — 舒适的；useful — 有用的

items.question: What are the advantages and disadvantages of tech products for students?
items.questionZh: 科技产品对学生有什么优缺点？
items.answer: They make research, practice and sharing work more convenient. A student can revisit a lesson or get feedback without waiting for the next class. The drawbacks include distraction and depending on a tool without understanding the task. Clear study goals help separate useful support from aimless screen time.
items.ideaZh: 资源反馈便利，对应分心和不理解就依赖；目标区分有效学习和刷屏。
items.vocab: clear — 清楚的；useful — 有用的

items.question: Do children rely on AI?
items.questionZh: 儿童依赖人工智能吗？
items.answer: Some may turn to it quickly when a task feels difficult, but access and habits vary. I'd be concerned if a child copied an answer without checking it or trying independently. Adults can encourage children to explain the reasoning and compare suggestions with what they have learned.
items.ideaZh: 部分孩子会迅速求助，但不说全部；要求解释思路和核对，防止照抄。
items.vocab: independently — 独立地；compare — 比较

items.question: Do you think relying on AI is a bad thing?
items.questionZh: 依赖人工智能是坏事吗？
items.answer: Using it for support isn't automatically a problem. It can help organise ideas or explain something in another way. The risk comes when people stop checking accuracy or practising the skill themselves. I'd want it to help me think, while leaving me able to work without it.
items.ideaZh: 辅助解释整理可以；不核查不练习才危险，目标是离开工具仍能做。
items.vocab: help — 帮助；people — 人们
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: What technology do family members generally use?
items.questionZh: 家庭成员通常使用什么科技？
items.answer: Phones are useful for keeping in touch, while televisions and household appliances support entertainment and daily routines. Different relatives may prefer different devices. I think a clear, simple design often matters more than advanced features when several family members need to use the same product.
items.ideaZh: 手机电视家电各有用途，家庭共同使用更重简单清楚而非堆功能。
items.vocab: clear — 清楚的；useful — 有用的

items.question: Why do people want to buy the latest technology?
items.questionZh: 为什么人们想买最新科技？
items.answer: Some need a genuine improvement, such as replacing a slow device or getting a useful feature. Others enjoy trying something new or feel influenced by advertising. I'd compare the benefit with what I already own, because a newer model isn't always a worthwhile upgrade for every user.
items.ideaZh: 性能需求与尝鲜广告影响并存，先比较现有产品和实际收益。
items.vocab: compare — 比较；useful — 有用的

items.topic: 去过且适合居住的地方
items.question: Describe a place you have visited that you think it is a good place to live.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你去过且认为适合居住的地方。
cueCard: What you know about this place
And explain why you would recommend this place as a good place to live.
cueCardZh: 说明为什么推荐为宜居地
items.answer:
A place I've visited that I think could be good to live in is Sanya. I went there with my girlfriend, and we spent time at Dadonghai Beach, taking photos and walking along the sand.

What I know most directly is the seaside environment. The clear water and the sea breeze made a strong impression on me. People can walk outdoors, meet friends and enjoy time near the water. I also saw places to eat and ordinary shops, so the area didn't feel completely separate from everyday life.

I'd recommend considering it because I like the idea of balancing daily responsibilities with an easy way to relax outdoors. However, enjoying a visit isn't the same as living there. Before moving, I'd check the cost, transport and whether the location suited my studies or work. For someone whose routine fits those practical conditions, I think having the sea nearby could make ordinary days more enjoyable.

What I know most directly is the seaside environment. The clear water and the sea breeze made a strong impression on me. People can walk outdoors, meet friends and enjoy time near the water. I also saw places to eat and ordinary shops, so the area didn't feel completely separate from everyday life.

I'd recommend considering it because I like the idea of balancing daily responsibilities with an easy way to relax outdoors. However, enjoying a visit isn't the same as living there. For someone whose routine fits those practical conditions, I think having the sea nearby could make ordinary days more enjoyable.
cluesZh: 地点与到访：三亚，真实的大东海旅行；回答的是适合居住，不只推荐旅游。
了解什么、可以做什么：直接认识是海边环境，散步交友；餐饮商店细节为补充，不虚构全面城市研究。
宜居理由和条件：日常责任与户外放松平衡；明确先查费用交通学习工作，不将旅游好感当长期居住经验。
items.provenance: 真实：去过三亚大东海。把三亚视为未来宜居地是答题判断；生活便利、交通和学习空间为设想与补充，不声称长期住过三亚，不改变现居海口。
items.extension: I wouldn't choose only because a place looks beautiful in holiday photos. A comfortable home and a workable daily routine would still come first.
items.extensionZh: 美景之外，实际住处与可执行的日常安排更重要。

items.topic: 去过且适合居住的地方
items.question: What type of places do people like to live in?
items.questionZh: 人们喜欢住在什么样的地方？
items.answer: Preferences vary, but convenience, comfort and affordability are common concerns. Someone working in a city may choose an apartment near transport, while another person values a quieter place with more space. Family needs can change the choice too. A suitable home is one that works for the people actually living there.
items.ideaZh: 常考虑便利、舒适和负担得起；有人重交通便利，有人重安静宽敞，还要符合家庭实际需要。
items.vocab: affordability — 负担得起的程度；preferences — 偏好
items.provenance: 观点示范；个人习惯未由用户确认的部分为合理补充。R26 法律例子沿用已核实海南规定。

items.topic: 去过且适合居住的地方
items.question: Why do some people like to go abroad?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人喜欢出国？
items.answer: They may be looking for a different lifestyle, education, work or simply a new experience. A short visit can satisfy curiosity, while moving abroad requires much more planning. I think expectations matter; someone may enjoy the idea of a place before understanding the practical challenges of living there.
items.ideaZh: 生活教育工作体验，旅游与移居不同；理想印象还需现实了解。
items.vocab: practical — 实用的；experience — 经历经验

items.question: What are the differences in living arrangements between your country and other countries?
items.questionZh: 你们国家与其他国家的居住安排有什么差异？
items.answer: I wouldn't generalise about every country, but factors such as housing costs, family habits and city design can lead to different arrangements. Some people live with relatives, while others share with friends or live alone. Even within one country, a large city can differ greatly from a smaller town.
items.ideaZh: 费用家庭习惯城市形态影响同住选择；国内也有差异，避免整国概括。
items.vocab: different — 不同的；people — 人们

items.topic: 去过且适合居住的地方
items.question: What are the differences between the places preferred by the elderly and young people to live in?
items.questionZh: 年轻人与老年人偏好的住所有什么不同？
items.answer: Younger people may put more weight on access to work, study and social activities. Older residents might value a quieter setting and convenient everyday services. However, needs vary greatly. A safe neighbourhood and reliable transport can matter to both groups, even if their daily schedules differ.
items.ideaZh: 青年可能重通勤社交，长者重安静服务；安全交通两者都重要。

items.question: What preparations should be made before moving to a new place?
items.questionZh: 搬到新地方前应做哪些准备？
items.answer: People should check the cost, transport and everyday services, then think about how the location fits their routine. Visiting at different times can reveal things a photograph misses, such as traffic or noise. It's also helpful to plan the move itself rather than focus only on choosing the property.
items.ideaZh: 查费用交通设施，分时实地看噪音，另安排搬运过程。

items.topic: 去过且适合居住的地方
items.question: Is choosing a place to live one of the most important decisions in life?
items.questionZh: 选择住处是人生最重要的决定之一吗？
items.answer: For many people, yes, because it affects daily travel, expenses and who they can easily spend time with. It can shape ordinary life for years. Still, the decision isn't always permanent, and people have different degrees of choice. A practical, suitable home can be more valuable than an ideal image.
items.ideaZh: 影响通勤支出关系且持续久，但选择程度不同，也可变；合适实用重于理想形象。
items.vocab: practical — 实用的；suitable — 合适的

items.question: Describe a high-rise building you like or dislike.
items.questionZh: 描述一座你喜欢或不喜欢的高楼。
cueCard: And explain why you like or dislike it.
cueCardZh: 说明喜欢或不喜欢的原因
items.answer:
A tall building I don't particularly like is an apartment block near my home in Haikou. It has around thirty floors and is mainly used for housing.

From the outside, it looks quite plain, with grey walls and rows of similar windows. There are shops on the ground floor, which is convenient for the people living there. However, the building feels very large compared with the smaller streets around it.

I pass it quite often on my way to school. What I dislike is the feeling of being surrounded by so much concrete, especially when the area is busy. I'd prefer more space for trees and places where people can sit outside. I understand why tall buildings are useful in cities, since they provide homes for many people. Still, this particular one doesn't appeal to me. A few more green areas and a more welcoming entrance would make it look much better in my opinion.
paragraphs: A tall building I don't particularly like is an apartment block near my home in Haikou. It has around thirty floors and is mainly used for housing.

From the outside, it looks quite plain, with grey walls and rows of similar windows. There are shops on the ground floor, which is convenient for the people living there. However, the building feels very large compared with the smaller streets around it.

I pass it quite often on my way to school. What I dislike is the feeling of being surrounded by so much concrete, especially when the area is busy. I'd prefer more space for trees and places where people can sit outside. I understand why tall buildings are useful in cities, since they provide homes for many people. Still, this particular one doesn't appeal to me. A few more green areas and a more welcoming entrance would make it look much better in my opinion.
cluesZh: 点题：海口家附近一栋不太喜欢的公寓楼，约三十层，主要用于住宅。
外观：灰墙、重复排列的窗户，底层商店方便住户，但相对周围小街显得庞大。
理由与改进：混凝土包围感较强，希望多些树和户外座位；理解高楼容纳人口的用途，但这一栋缺少亲切感。

items.provenance: 海口住宅楼的具体位置、约三十层、外观与个人喜好为拟写；不冒用实际建筑名称。
items.extension: I don't think a building has to be unusual to look good. Even a simple design can work if it feels comfortable for the people nearby.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：建筑不一定要奇特才好看，简单设计只要让周围的人觉得舒适也很好。

items.question: Have you ever lived in a high-rise building?
items.questionZh: 你住过高层建筑吗？
items.answer: Yes, I've lived in an apartment in a building of around fifteen floors. The convenience is useful, but lifts and shared areas matter a lot. I think the quality of daily life depends more on those details than on the number of floors alone.
items.ideaZh: 备用草稿沿用旧公寓设定，“约十五层”是补充，具体高层经历未确认；说明便利与电梯公共区的重要性。

items.question: What impact do you think climate has on architectural design?
items.questionZh: 气候对建筑设计有什么影响？
items.answer: It can affect how a building deals with sunlight, rain and temperature. A hot place may need more shade and airflow, while a colder place needs to retain warmth. Good design should respond to local conditions, rather than copying an attractive building from somewhere with very different weather.
items.ideaZh: 气候影响遮阳通风挡雨保暖；本地适应比照搬外观重要。

items.question: Why do you think many Chinese people now live in high-rise buildings?
items.questionZh: 为什么现在很多中国人住在高层？
items.answer: In a crowded city, building upwards allows more people to live near jobs and services within a limited area. Apartments may also be the most available option at a particular budget. I wouldn't assume everyone actively prefers height; many people are choosing among the homes they can realistically afford.
items.ideaZh: 土地交通服务与预算影响供给；住高层不必然代表偏爱高度。

items.question: In the future, will Chinese people prefer high-rise buildings or houses?
items.questionZh: 未来中国人会更喜欢高层还是独栋？
items.answer: I expect both preferences to remain. Some people will value the space of a house, while others will choose an apartment for location and convenience. Affordability and transport will probably shape the decision as much as personal taste, so I wouldn't predict one choice for the whole country.
items.ideaZh: 两种偏好共存，空间与便利取舍；预算交通也决定，不做全国单一预测。

items.question: Why do you think some people design their own homes?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人自己设计家？
items.answer: They want the space to suit their habits, rather than adjust their lives to a standard layout. Someone who works from home may need a quiet room, for example. Personal involvement can be satisfying, but it also requires time and good advice to avoid impractical decisions.
items.ideaZh: 适合个人习惯如安静书房，参与有成就感但耗时且需专业意见。

items.topic: 看过的现场体育比赛（版本一）
items.question: Describe a live sports match you have ever watched.
items.questionZh: 描述一场你现场看过的体育比赛。
cueCard: And explain how you felt about it.
items.answer:
A live sports event I enjoyed watching was a basketball match at my school last term. I went with my friend Leo, and we stood beside the court with other students.

The match was between two student teams, so it wasn't a professional event, but the atmosphere was lively. People cheered when someone made a good shot, and we could hear the players calling to each other. The score stayed close for most of the game, which made it exciting to watch.

I liked being there in person because I could see things that are easy to miss in a short online clip. I watched how players moved when they didn't have the ball and how they helped each other. Since I play basketball myself, I found that interesting. We talked about the game afterwards and tried to remember a few useful ideas. It was an enjoyable afternoon that combined learning, excitement and time with a friend.

items.answer: Basketball and table tennis are examples that come to mind. Around my school, basketball is especially noticeable because students can play together after class. items.question: What are the advantages of watching sports events on site?
items.questionZh: 现场看体育比赛有什么好处？
items.answer: The atmosphere is the main attraction. You can hear the crowd and see how players move beyond what a camera chooses to show. Watching with friends also makes it a shared experience. The trade-off is that tickets, travel and crowds may make it less convenient than watching at home.
items.ideaZh: 现场气氛、全场视野、朋友共享，对应票交通人群成本；与线上优势分开回答。

items.question: What are the benefits of watching sports events on TV?
items.questionZh: 在电视上看体育赛事有什么好处？
items.answer: It saves travel time and can make events accessible to people who live far away. Depending on the service, viewers may also be able to review key moments. However, the quality depends on the connection and coverage. It is convenient, but it doesn't fully reproduce the atmosphere of being there.

items.question: What sports competitions in China are suitable for children?

items.answer: Local or school matches can be suitable because they are often shorter and easier to understand. The venue should be safe, and adults should consider noise, crowds and the child's interest. An expensive ticket doesn't guarantee a good experience if the child is tired or doesn't enjoy the sport.
items.ideaZh: 当地或学校比赛通常较短、较好理解；还要看安全、噪声、人群和兴趣，贵票不保证好体验。

items.question: Do children nowadays face a lot of competition?
items.questionZh: 现在儿童面临很多竞争吗？
items.answer: Some face competition in exams, sports or other activities, especially when adults compare results frequently. A little competition can provide a goal, but constant comparison may make ordinary learning feel like a test. I think children also need activities where cooperation and enjoyment matter more than rankings.
items.ideaZh: 考试体育比较可能多；竞争可给目标，持续排名有压力，也要合作娱乐。

items.topic: 看过的现场体育比赛（版本一）
items.question: Is this kind of competition good for children?
items.questionZh: 这种竞争对儿童好吗？
items.answer: It can be helpful if the challenge is fair and children learn to handle both winning and losing. It becomes less useful when results affect their sense of worth. Adults should recognise effort and improvement, so competition is one part of learning rather than the whole purpose.
items.ideaZh: 公平竞争学胜败，不能用输赢定义价值；重努力进步。

items.question: Describe a person you know who runs a successful business.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你知道的拥有成功生意的人。
cueCard: How you know about this person
What kind of business he or she runs
How long the business has been running
And explain why you think his or her business is successful.
items.answer:
A person I know who has a successful business is Ms Lin, the owner of a small restaurant near my school in Haikou. I got to know her because my friends and I sometimes eat there after playing basketball.

She told us she opened it about five years ago because she enjoyed cooking and wanted more control over her working life. She began with a small menu and used money she had saved, instead of opening a large place straight away.

The restaurant serves simple meals at prices students can afford. I think it does well because the food is reliable and the staff treat people warmly. Ms Lin remembers regular customers and listens when someone has a suggestion. The place isn't famous, but people keep coming back, which seems like a good sign. I admire the way she pays attention to ordinary details. Her business shows me that success can come from doing a useful job consistently.

Ms Lin remembers regular customers and listens when someone has a suggestion. The place isn't famous, but people keep coming back, which seems like a good sign. I admire the way she pays attention to ordinary details. Her business shows me that success can come from doing a useful job consistently.

经营时长与动机：约五年前开店，喜欢做饭并希望掌握工作节奏；时长和人物均为草稿。

items.extensionZh: 延伸：忙时亲自帮员工，而非只下命令，让员工和顾客都更舒服。

items.question: Why do you think one can achieve success?
items.questionZh: 人为什么能取得成功？
items.answer: Usually a combination of useful skills, steady effort and opportunities helps. People also benefit from advice and support, even when success looks individual from the outside. I think being willing to adjust after a mistake matters, because repeating the same approach doesn't always produce a better result.
items.ideaZh: 技能努力机遇支持相结合，出错后调整而非盲目重复。

items.question: Why do people fail in starting a business?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人创业失败？
items.answer: They may misunderstand what customers want, run out of money or take on costs they can't sustain. Sometimes the idea is promising but the timing is poor. Starting small and testing demand can help, although preparation cannot remove every uncertainty or make every business successful.
items.ideaZh: 需求资金成本时机可导致失败，小规模验证有用但不能消除不确定。

items.question: Is it difficult to start a business?
items.questionZh: 创业困难吗？
items.answer: I wouldn't call it easy just because a small business can begin online or from a modest space. Owners still need to understand the relevant requirements, find customers and manage costs. I haven't started one myself, but I think maintaining a steady business is a bigger challenge than simply getting started.
items.ideaZh: 小型线上业务可能较容易开始，但还要处理要求、成本和客户问题；没有亲身创业经验，持续经营比开张难。
items.vocab: online — 在线的

items.question: Should the government support anyone who wants to start a business?
items.questionZh: 政府应支持所有想创业的人吗？
items.answer: Basic information and training could be widely available, but financial support needs clear criteria. Not every idea is practical, and public money is limited. I'd favour fair opportunities to apply and careful assessment, rather than either automatically funding everyone or helping only people with useful connections.
items.ideaZh: 信息培训可普惠，资金要标准评估；不自动全给，也不靠关系。

items.question: Should enterprises give back to society after making profits?
items.questionZh: 企业盈利后应该回馈社会吗？
items.answer: Yes, a business benefits from customers, workers and public services, so contributing to the community is reasonable. That doesn't only mean donations. Treating staff fairly, providing reliable products and reducing unnecessary waste are everyday ways to act responsibly, alongside supporting a useful local project.
items.ideaZh: 企业受益社会，应以公平用工可靠产品减少浪费等日常责任回馈，不只捐钱。

items.question: Many people think consumers have excessive demands. What is your opinion?
items.questionZh: 有人认为消费者要求过多，你怎么看？
items.answer: Sometimes a request may be unrealistic, but customers are reasonable to expect what was promised. Clear information about a product or service prevents many disagreements. I would judge the actual request rather than label all consumers as demanding, because businesses and customers can both communicate badly.
items.ideaZh: 兑现承诺是合理要求，也有不现实诉求；看具体内容，双方沟通都可能出问题。
items.vocab: rather than — 而不是；clear — 清楚的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Do you think companies should prioritize profits or consumers' needs?
items.questionZh: 企业应优先利润还是消费者需求？
items.answer: They need enough profit to continue operating, but ignoring customers' real needs can damage the business over time. I'd look for a sustainable balance: offer something useful at a fair price and manage costs sensibly. A short-term gain from misleading people is unlikely to build lasting trust.
items.ideaZh: 生存需利润，长远靠满足需求；公道价格成本管理，欺骗短利损信任。

items.topic: 喜欢种植物的人（版本一）
items.question: Describe a person who likes growing plants.
items.questionZh: 描述一个喜欢种植物的人。
cueCard: And explain why he/she likes growing plants.
items.answer:
Someone I know who loves growing plants is my grandfather. I've known him all my life. He has a small garden at his home in Hainan, where he grows some vegetables and a few kinds of flowers.

The plants I notice most are the chillies and leafy vegetables, because he sometimes uses them in meals. He doesn't have any complicated equipment. He grows some things in the ground and others in reused containers. He checks the soil regularly and waters the plants when they need it.

When I visit, I sometimes help him carry water or remove dry leaves. He enjoys explaining which plants are doing well. I think he loves gardening because it gives him a calm routine and something to look forward to. Seeing a new leaf or picking something he has grown seems to make him happy. I find that attitude quite appealing. It shows how an ordinary daily activity can give someone a strong sense of satisfaction.

种类与方法：辣椒、叶菜能做饭；不用复杂设备，地里和旧容器都种，定期检查土壤、按需浇水。
相处与原因：我帮提水、清枯叶，他分享长势；种植提供平静日常和期待，新叶与收获带来满足。

items.provenance: 爷爷种辣椒、绿叶菜和花，院子及浇水习惯为拟写；符合英文 plants，不限于蔬菜。
items.extension: I would like to try growing one easy plant myself. Starting small would help me learn the habit without making it feel like another big task.

items.question: What preparations do you need for planting?

items.answer: People need to think about the available space, sunlight and how often they can look after a plant. Then they can choose suitable soil and a container. I'd find out the basic needs first, because buying an attractive plant without checking the conditions can lead to disappointment.

items.question: Do you think planting is easy or difficult?

items.answer: Keeping one suitable plant can be manageable, but growing things well takes attention and experience. items.question: What do you gain after solving problems in planting?
items.questionZh: 解决种植问题后能得到什么？
items.answer: Apart from a healthier plant, people gain experience and confidence. They learn to observe what changed, try a solution and wait for a result. That process can be satisfying because the improvement is visible, and the same patience may be useful in other everyday tasks.
items.ideaZh: 植物改善之外获得经验自信；观察尝试等待的耐心可迁移。

items.question: Describe an important decision that you made.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你作出的重要决定。
cueCard: What the results of the decision were
And explain why it was important.
items.answer:
An important decision I made was choosing computer science as my university major. Before making the choice, I knew I enjoyed using computers, but I wasn't sure whether I would enjoy studying how they work.

I looked at information about the courses and tried a few basic coding lessons online. I also talked with my parents about what I liked and what kind of work I might want to do later. Their advice helped, but I wanted the final choice to reflect my own interests.

The result was that I started learning skills I could use to make small programs and solve practical problems. Some subjects have been harder than I expected, but completing a task successfully gives me confidence. This decision was important because it shaped how I spend my time at university and what opportunities I may have afterwards. It also taught me to think carefully about a choice before following other people's opinions.

I looked at information about the courses and tried a few basic coding lessons online. I also talked with my parents about what I liked and what kind of work I might want to do later. Their advice helped, but I wanted the final choice to reflect my own interests.

This decision was important because it shaped how I spend my time at university and what opportunities I may have afterwards. It also taught me to think carefully about a choice before following other people's opinions.
cluesZh: 决定：选择计算机科学大学专业；知道自己爱用电脑，但曾不确定是否喜欢学习原理。
决策过程：查课程、试基础编程网课、与父母聊兴趣和职业；听建议，同时尊重自己的兴趣。
结果与重要性：学会写小程序、解决实际问题，克服难课后获得信心；影响大学时间与未来机会，也学会先思考而非盲从。
translationsZh: 结果是，我开始学习能用来写小程序、解决实际问题的技能。有些科目比我预想的更难，但成功完成任务会给我信心。这个决定重要，是因为它影响了我在大学如何度过时间，以及之后可能获得什么机会。它也教会我，在听从别人的意见之前，先认真思考自己的选择。

items.extension: I don't have every part of my future planned yet. Still, I feel that this subject gives me a useful starting point and room to develop.

items.question: Do you think children sometimes have to make important decisions?
items.questionZh: 孩子有时也需要作重要决定吗？
items.answer: Yes, although adults should support choices with serious consequences. A child may need to decide how to respond to a friendship problem or which activity to commit to. Giving suitable choices helps them practise judgment. They shouldn't have to carry responsibility for major adult problems they cannot control.
items.ideaZh: 需要，例如处理友谊问题或选择活动；成人应提供支持，让孩子练习判断，但不能把重大成人问题的责任压给他们。

items.question: What important decisions do teenagers need to make after graduation?
items.questionZh: 青少年毕业后要作哪些重要决定？
items.answer: They may need to choose further study, a training course or a first job. Some also decide whether to move away from home. These choices involve interests, costs and available opportunities. Good guidance helps, but teenagers should be able to explain their own priorities instead of simply following what friends choose.
items.ideaZh: 继续学习、接受培训、找第一份工作或离家；结合兴趣、费用与机会，理解自身重点，不盲从朋友。

items.question: Who can children turn to for help when making a decision?
items.questionZh: 孩子作决定时可以向谁求助？
items.answer: Parents, teachers and other trusted adults can help them think through options. Friends may understand the immediate situation, but they may not have enough experience for every problem. The best person depends on the question. A teacher may explain a course more clearly, while family can discuss practical support.

items.question: Do you think advertisements can influence our decisions when shopping?
items.questionZh: 广告会影响购物决定吗？
items.answer: Yes, advertisements can make a product familiar or connect it with a feeling we want. That may influence which options we notice first, even if we don't buy immediately. Comparing actual features and price helps. An attractive image can introduce an item, but it shouldn't be the only reason for choosing it.
items.ideaZh: 会增加熟悉感、关联向往的感受，让某些产品更先被注意；还应比较实际功能与价格。

items.question: Do you think the influence of advertising is good?
items.questionZh: 广告的影响是好的吗？
items.answer: It can be useful when advertising explains a genuine benefit and helps people compare options. It becomes less helpful when it exaggerates results or creates pressure to buy unnecessary things. I'd judge the information and how it is presented, rather than call all advertising influence either good or bad.
items.ideaZh: 真实介绍产品、帮助比较时有益；夸大效果或诱导不必要消费时有害，应具体判断信息与表达方式。

items.question: How do people usually make important decisions?
items.questionZh: 人们通常怎样作重要决定？
items.answer: They often gather information, consider the likely results and discuss the options with people they trust. Personal values still matter, because two reasonable people can want different outcomes. For a major choice, I'd also think about whether it can be changed later and what support would be available if problems arose.
items.ideaZh: 收集信息、考虑后果、向可信的人讨论，同时结合个人价值观；重大选择还要考虑能否调整及遇事可获得的支持。

items.question: Describe a time when you got up early.
items.questionZh: 描述一次你早起的经历。
cueCard: And how you felt about it.
items.answer:
A time I got up early was when my girlfriend and I were going to Sanya for a short trip. It was on a weekend last term, and I got out of bed at about six in the morning.

We wanted to catch an early train so we would have more time there. The night before, I had packed a small bag and checked the things I needed. In the morning, I washed, had a quick breakfast and made sure I hadn't forgotten my phone or charger.

At first, I felt sleepy and didn't want to leave my bed. However, once we were on the train, I became more excited about the trip. We later visited Dadonghai Beach, where I took photos of my girlfriend and we walked along the sand. Looking back, getting up early was worth it. We had a more relaxed day because we didn't arrive feeling that we had already lost half of it.

We wanted to catch an early train so we would have more time there. The night before, I had packed a small bag and checked the things I needed. In the morning, I washed, had a quick breakfast and made sure I hadn't forgotten my phone or charger.

We had a more relaxed day because we didn't arrive feeling that we had already lost half of it.

感受变化：起初困、不愿起，坐上火车后期待；到大东海拍照散步，觉得早起值得、一天更从容。

items.extension: I wouldn't want to get up that early every day, but having something enjoyable to look forward to made it easier on that occasion.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：不想每天都那么早起，但有开心的事情可以期待，那一次就容易些。

items.question: Do you know anyone who likes to get up early?

items.answer: My grandfather is the example I'd give. He likes a quiet start and spends some time looking after his plants before the day gets busy. That routine suits him. It also shows that getting up early can be enjoyable when people have a reason, rather than simply being forced to rush.

items.question: Why do people get up early?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人喜欢早起？
items.answer: Some need to travel to work or school, while others want quiet time for exercise or household tasks. An early start can make the morning less rushed. But the benefit depends on their overall routine; getting up early is not automatically useful if they have stayed awake too late.
items.ideaZh: 有人要上班上学，有人享受安静地运动或做事；前提是睡眠充足，不能认为早起必然更好。

items.question: What kinds of occasions need people to arrive early?
items.questionZh: 什么场合需要提前到达？
items.answer: Flights, important exams and job interviews usually require some extra time. Arriving before the required time allows people to find the right place and handle small delays. The amount should be reasonable, though. It is better to check the instructions than assume every event needs the same preparation.
items.ideaZh: 坐飞机、考试和面试需要预留交通及熟悉要求的时间；提前多久取决于具体情况。

items.question: Why do some people like to stay up late?
items.questionZh: 为什么有些人喜欢熬夜？
items.answer: Some enjoy the quiet after daily responsibilities are finished. Others become absorbed in games, films or conversations and lose track of time. Work schedules can be another reason. Staying up late isn't always a deliberate preference, so the explanation may be quite different from person to person.
items.ideaZh: 忙完后终于有安静时间，也可能沉浸在游戏电影中忘记时间；有些人则是工作所迫。

items.question: Is it good to arrive early in any situation?
items.questionZh: 所有场合提前到都好吗？
items.answer: Not always. Being early for an exam is sensible, but arriving much too early at someone's home could interrupt their preparations. I would follow the agreed time and any instructions. If I reached the area early, I could wait nearby instead of expecting the host to be ready immediately.
items.ideaZh: 考试通常要提前，但去别人家太早可能打扰准备；遵守约定，必要时在附近等候。

items.question: What kind of people like getting up early?
items.questionZh: 哪些人通常会早起？
items.answer: People who enjoy a quiet morning or have activities they want to do before work may like it. Some older people have an established early routine, but plenty of younger people do too. I think habits and responsibilities matter more than one particular age or personality type.

items.topic: 喜欢在家或花园种植物的人（版本二）
items.question: Describe a person who loves to grow plants (e.g. vegetables, flowers) at home or in the garden.
items.questionZh: 描述一个喜欢在家或花园种植物的人。
cueCard: And explain why he/she loves growing plants.
items.answer:
Someone I know who loves growing plants is my grandfather. He has a small garden at his home in Hainan, where he grows some vegetables and a few kinds of flowers.

The plants I notice most are the chillies and leafy vegetables, because he sometimes uses them in meals. He doesn't have any complicated equipment. He grows some things in the ground and others in reused containers. He checks the soil regularly and waters the plants when they need it.

When I visit, I sometimes help him carry water or remove dry leaves. He enjoys explaining which plants are doing well. I think he loves gardening because it gives him a calm routine and something to look forward to. Seeing a new leaf or picking something he has grown seems to make him happy. I find that attitude quite appealing. It shows how an ordinary daily activity can give someone a strong sense of satisfaction.
paragraphs: Someone I know who loves growing plants is my grandfather. He has a small garden at his home in Hainan, where he grows some vegetables and a few kinds of flowers.

The plants I notice most are the chillies and leafy vegetables, because he sometimes uses them in meals. He doesn't have any complicated equipment. He grows some things in the ground and others in reused containers. He checks the soil regularly and waters the plants when they need it.

种类与方法：辣椒、叶菜能做饭；不用复杂设备，地里和旧容器都种，定期检查土壤、按需浇水。
相处与原因：我帮提水、清枯叶，他分享长势；种植提供平静日常和期待，新叶与收获带来满足。

items.question: What are the advantages of growing vegetables or flowers at home?
items.questionZh: 在家种植物有什么好处？
items.answer: Plants can make a home feel pleasant and give people a satisfying routine. Growing a small amount of food also helps them appreciate the effort involved. It won't necessarily replace shopping, especially in a small space, but watching something develop can be enjoyable in its own right.
items.ideaZh: 让环境更宜人，照料过程有满足感，也能理解种食物的辛苦；即使不能代替买菜，也有自身价值。

items.question: Describe a story/book with animals in it.
items.questionZh: 描述一个有动物角色的故事或一本书。
cueCard: And explain what you think of this story/book.
items.answer:
A story with animals that I remember is The Tortoise and the Hare. I read it in a collection of Aesop's Fables that I borrowed from a library. I chose the book because the stories were short and easy to follow.

The main animals are a tortoise and a hare, which is similar to a rabbit. They have a race. The hare runs much faster and becomes so confident that it stops to rest. Meanwhile, the tortoise keeps moving slowly and eventually reaches the finish first.

I like the story because its message is simple without being useless. It reminds me that starting well isn't enough if you stop making an effort. I can connect that with learning English. Some people learn more quickly than I do, but regular practice can still help me improve. The story doesn't suggest that speed is always bad. To me, it's more about taking a task seriously and continuing until it's finished.
paragraphs: A story with animals that I remember is The Tortoise and the Hare. I read it in a collection of Aesop's Fables that I borrowed from a library. I chose the book because the stories were short and easy to follow.

The main animals are a tortoise and a hare, which is similar to a rabbit. They have a race. The hare runs much faster and becomes so confident that it stops to rest. Meanwhile, the tortoise keeps moving slowly and eventually reaches the finish first.

I like the story because its message is simple without being useless. It reminds me that starting well isn't enough if you stop making an effort. I can connect that with learning English. To me, it's more about taking a task seriously and continuing until it's finished.
cluesZh: 故事与来源：《龟兔赛跑》，从图书馆借的《伊索寓言》中读到，选择它因故事短而易懂。
情节：乌龟和野兔比赛，兔子快却自信到停下休息，乌龟持续慢行先到终点。
观点与应用：道理简单却实用，开局好不等于能放弃努力；联系英语学习，快不坏，重点是认真坚持到完成。

items.extension: I also like how easy it is to remember the two animals. Their different ways of behaving make the lesson clearer than a long explanation would.

items.question: Should schools teach children about animals?
items.questionZh: 学校应该教孩子有关动物的知识吗？
items.answer: Yes, children should learn about animals' needs and how to treat them responsibly. Lessons can also explain the difference between a pet and a wild animal. Stories may create interest, but factual learning matters too, so children don't expect a real animal to behave like a character in a cartoon.

items.answer: I wouldn't support a complete ban. Some pets can live well in cities if owners provide suitable care and consider neighbours. items.answer: A pet can provide companionship and a shared focus for family members. Looking after one can also encourage a regular routine. items.topic: 喜欢拜访但不想住的家
items.question: Describe a home that you like to visit but do not want to live in.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你喜欢拜访但不想住的家。
cueCard: Why you like to visit it
And explain why you would not like to live there.
items.answer:
A home I enjoy visiting but wouldn't want to live in is my grandfather's house in a village in Hainan. It's a fairly simple house with a small outdoor area where he grows plants.

When I visit, we usually sit together, have something to eat and talk. Sometimes I help him water the plants. The pace of life feels slower there, and I enjoy having time away from schoolwork and computer screens. I also like seeing the small things he has made or repaired around the house.

However, living there every day would be less convenient for me. It's far from my school and the places where I normally meet my friends. Travelling back and forth would take too much time. So my feelings about the house depend on the situation. It's a lovely place for a short family visit, but at this stage of my life, I'd prefer to live somewhere closer to my daily activities.

So my feelings about the house depend on the situation. It's a lovely place for a short family visit, but at this stage of my life, I'd prefer to live somewhere closer to my daily activities.
cluesZh: 地点外观：海南村里的爷爷家，简单房子，带种植物的小户外空间。
拜访的乐趣：一起吃东西聊天、浇花，看爷爷制作修理的小物件；节奏慢，暂离功课和屏幕。
不想长期住的原因：离学校和朋友活动地远，来回费时；适合短暂家庭拜访，但当前生活更需要便利。
translationsZh: 不过，每天住在那里对我来说就不太方便。它离学校和我通常见朋友的地方都远，来回会花太多时间。所以，我对这所房子的感受取决于情境。短时间去看家人时，它是个很好的地方；但在人生现阶段，我更愿意住在离日常活动近的地方。

items.answer: City homes are often closer together and may be apartments, while some countryside homes have more outdoor space. Access to work, shops and transport can differ too. items.question: Describe a plan that you had to change recently.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你近期不得不改变的计划。
cueCard: What made you change the plan
And how you felt about the change.
items.answer:
A plan I had to change recently was a weekend visit to Evergreen Park in Haikou with my girlfriend. We had planned to walk around and take some photos in the afternoon.

However, when I woke up that morning, it was raining heavily. We checked the weather again before leaving, but it didn't look suitable for spending much time outside. Neither of us wanted to walk around with wet shoes and worry about our phones getting wet.

Instead, we decided to visit a library and find somewhere nearby to eat afterwards. We spent some time looking at books and sitting quietly together. It was different from what we had imagined, but it still gave us a break from our usual routine. At first, I felt disappointed because I had been looking forward to the park. Later, I was glad we had changed the plan. Being flexible helped us enjoy the day instead of complaining about the weather.

改变原因：早晨下大雨，出门前再查天气仍不适合户外，不想鞋湿或手机进水。
新安排与情绪变化：改去图书馆、附近吃饭；开始失望，后来觉得能灵活调整、一起换个节奏也很好。

items.question: Do people often change their plans?
items.questionZh: 人们经常改变计划吗？
items.answer: Yes, because plans depend on information that can change. Weather, transport or another person's availability may require an adjustment. Changing a plan isn't necessarily a sign of poor organisation. A useful plan gives direction while leaving room to respond sensibly when circumstances are different from what someone expected.
items.ideaZh: 天气、交通或参与者时间改变时需要调整；这不一定是安排不好，灵活性也很重要。

items.question: How does technology help people make plans?

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: Describe a time when you sent a message or an email to someone but received no reply for a long time.
items.questionZh: 描述一次发信息或邮件后很久没收到回复的经历。
cueCard: Whether you finally received the reply
And explain how you felt about the experience.
items.answer:
A time I waited quite a while for a reply was when I sent my friend Leo a message about playing basketball. I wanted to know whether he was free that weekend, because I needed to arrange my study time around it.

I sent the message in the afternoon and expected a fairly quick answer. However, nothing came through that evening. I checked my phone several times and started wondering whether he had seen it. I didn't want to keep sending messages, though, because the plan wasn't urgent.

He finally replied the next morning. He explained that he had been busy and that his phone had run out of battery. We were still able to arrange the game, so there wasn't a serious problem. I felt relieved and a little silly for checking so often. The experience reminded me that a slow reply doesn't necessarily mean someone is ignoring me. Sometimes people simply have other things to deal with.

结果与反思：次晨回复，原来忙且手机没电，仍能约球；放心又觉得多虑，慢回不一定是忽视。

items.extension: Now, if I need an answer by a certain time, I say that clearly in the message. It helps the other person understand what I need.

items.question: In what situations do people not respond to messages right away?
items.questionZh: 哪些情况下人们不会马上回消息？
items.answer: They may be studying, working or travelling without a convenient chance to answer. Some messages also need thought, so an immediate reply wouldn't be useful. I wouldn't assume a delay is personal. If something is urgent, explaining the time limit clearly is better than repeatedly checking the screen.
items.ideaZh: 工作学习交通或需思考导致延迟；不等于不理人，急事说清时限。

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: What would you do if you hadn't received a reply after sending out a message?
items.questionZh: 发消息后没收到回复，你会怎么做？
items.answer: I'd consider how urgent it was. For a casual plan, I'd wait and send one polite follow-up later. If I needed an answer quickly, I might call. Sending repeated messages without considering the other person's situation would probably create more pressure without making the conversation clearer.
items.ideaZh: 不急的安排先等，稍后礼貌跟进一次；急事可以打电话，不顾对方处境反复催促只会增加压力。
items.vocab: follow-up — 后续跟进；casual plan — 非紧急的日常安排

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: Why do some people prefer sending a message instead of making a call?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人喜欢发消息而不是打电话？
items.answer: A message lets them explain the point without interrupting someone immediately. The other person can reply when they are free, and written details are easy to check later. A call may be better for something urgent or complicated, but not every everyday question needs an instant conversation.
items.ideaZh: 不立即打断对方，对方有空再回，文字细节便于复查；紧急复杂情况则可能更适合通话。
items.vocab: instant — 即时的；interrupting — 打断

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: How do you show your respect in your message?
items.questionZh: 你如何在信息里表达尊重？
items.answer: I keep the purpose clear, use a suitable greeting and say thank you when someone helps. I also consider whether I'm messaging at a reasonable time. Respect isn't only about formal words; it includes not demanding an immediate reply to a question that can comfortably wait.
items.ideaZh: 目的清楚、合适问候、感谢帮助并注意发送时间；尊重也包含不强求对方立刻回答不急的问题。
items.vocab: greeting — 问候；demanding — 强求

items.topic: 很久没收到回复的信息
items.question: Why do some people feel angry when others don't reply to their messages?
items.questionZh: 别人不回复消息时为什么有人会生气？
items.answer: They may interpret the silence as being ignored, especially if they expected a quick answer. That feeling can be stronger when a plan depends on the reply. But expectations often differ. Agreeing on a deadline for important messages is more useful than assuming everyone checks their phone in the same way.
items.ideaZh: 可能把沉默理解为忽视，尤其安排依赖回复时；双方期待可能不同，重要消息宜约定期限。
items.vocab: interpret — 理解为；deadline — 截止时间

items.question: Describe a boring place you have been to.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你去过的无聊地点。
cueCard: And explain why you felt it was boring.
items.answer:
A place I found boring was a small waiting area inside a shopping mall in Haikou. I went there with my father when he needed to have his watch repaired.

The repair was going to take a while, so we sat nearby and waited. There were a few chairs, a plain wall and a television showing the same advertisements repeatedly. I had expected a quick visit, so I hadn't brought anything to read. My phone battery was also quite low.

We talked for a bit, but after that I kept looking at the time. There wasn't much happening around us, and I didn't know exactly how long we would have to stay. I think that uncertainty made the wait feel longer. The place wasn't unpleasant or badly kept; it simply offered very little to do. When the watch was finally ready, I was relieved. Since then, I usually take something to read if I might have to wait.

cluesZh: 地点与同行者：陪父亲修手表，在海口商场内的小等候区等待。
环境与准备不足：几把椅子、空白墙、电视重复广告；原以为很快，没带读物，手机电也低。
无聊的原因与之后改变：聊完后一直看时间，没事做且不知还要多久；不是环境差，而是缺少活动，之后可能等待时就带书。

items.extension: A few magazines or a clear estimate of the waiting time would have helped. Small changes can make a waiting area much more comfortable.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：几本杂志或明确的预计等待时间都会有帮助，小改动就能改善体验。

items.question: On what occasions do people feel bored?
items.questionZh: 人们在哪些场合会无聊？
items.answer: Waiting without knowing how long it will take is a common situation. Repeating a task with no clear purpose can have the same effect. However, boredom depends on attention as well as the activity; a small goal or something useful to notice can change how the time feels.
items.ideaZh: 等待无时限、重复无目的；小目标和注意点可以改变体验。
items.vocab: attention — 注意力；clear — 清楚的
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: Why do students find their teachers' lessons boring?
items.questionZh: 学生为什么觉得老师的课无聊？
items.answer: The material may feel too easy, too difficult or unrelated to anything they care about. A lesson with no chance to ask questions can also make them passive. I'd look at how the topic is explained and whether students can use it, rather than assume they dislike learning itself.
items.ideaZh: 难度不合、无关联、不能互动都影响；改解释和应用，不直接怪不爱学。
items.vocab: rather than — 而不是
items.provenance: 观点示范，不代表统计结论；个人例子未确认的部分为可调整草稿。

items.question: How to avoid feeling bored?
items.questionZh: 怎样避免感到无聊？
items.answer: A small change of activity can help, such as taking a walk, calling a friend or trying a manageable task. It is also worth asking why they feel bored. Someone who needs rest may not benefit from another demanding activity, while someone who lacks challenge may enjoy learning a new skill.
items.ideaZh: 可以散步、联系朋友或完成一个小任务；先分清自己需要休息还是需要新的挑战。
items.vocab: challenge — 挑战

items.question: Why do some people find playing on their phones boring?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人觉得玩手机也无聊？
items.answer: They may keep seeing similar content without getting anything meaningful from it. Scrolling becomes a habit rather than an enjoyable choice. After a while, changing from one app to another doesn't really change the experience. An activity involving movement or a real conversation can provide something different.
items.ideaZh: 重复内容、习惯刷而非享受，换应用不改体验；活动交谈带来变化。
items.vocab: rather than — 而不是；experience — 经历经验

items.question: Describe a piece of news you heard or saw.
items.questionZh: 描述一条你听到或看到的新闻（本栏标题为当地新闻）。
cueCard: Explain how you felt about it.
items.answer:
A piece of local news that attracted people's attention was the introduction of Hainan's restrictions on certain single-use plastic products. The rules took effect in December 2020, so this is an older news story, not something that happened this week.

I read an online report about it while looking for information on the environment in Hainan. The story involved local authorities, shops and ordinary residents, because changing the kinds of bags and other products people use affects daily shopping.

I think people were interested for different reasons. Some wanted to know what they would need to bring when shopping, while businesses needed to understand which products were covered. Others cared about reducing waste near the sea. Living in Haikou, I found the topic easy to relate to and felt hopeful about reducing litter. It showed me that local news can be about small changes in daily habits as well as major events. I also discussed the idea of carrying a reusable bag with my family.

阅读途径与相关者：查海南环境信息时读到网络报道，涉及地方主管部门、商店和居民，影响购物用品选择。
当地相关性与感受：生活在海口容易共鸣，对减少垃圾感到有希望；感受是补写，新闻发生于2020年而非近期。

items.extension: The useful part of a report like this is a clear explanation of what changes for ordinary people. Without that, the headline alone isn't enough.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：报道应清楚解释普通人的生活会怎样改变，只看标题并不足够。

items.question: Do many people talk about local news?
items.questionZh: 很多人讨论当地新闻吗？
items.answer: They do when it affects their routine, such as a transport change or a new facility nearby. People may discuss it with neighbours or in a family group. A story doesn't have to be nationally important to matter; practical information can create a lot of local conversation.
items.ideaZh: 交通设施改变涉及生活时会聊，邻里家庭群；全国不重大也可本地重要。

items.question: Do young people or old people care more about local news?
items.questionZh: 年轻人还是老年人更关心当地新闻？
items.answer: Some older residents may have stronger local connections, while younger people may focus on study or work elsewhere. But the topic matters more than age alone. A change to a bus route near a university can interest students as much as a neighbourhood development interests retired residents.
items.ideaZh: 长者本地联系、青年异地安排可能不同，但具体内容决定，不绝对按年龄分。

items.question: Do people pay more attention to local news or national news?
items.questionZh: 人们更关注地方新闻还是全国新闻？
items.answer: National stories often reach more people, but local information can have a more immediate effect on daily life. Someone might follow both for different reasons. I think relevance matters: a large national event attracts attention, while a small transport announcement may change what a person does tomorrow.
items.ideaZh: 全国传播广，地方影响日常直接；相关性决定，常两者都看。

items.question: Describe a person you know who works in the medical field (e.g. doctor, nurse, vet).
items.questionZh: 描述一个你认识的已经在医疗行业工作的人。
cueCard: What he/she does in their job
And explain how you feel about him/her.
items.answer:
A person I know who works in the medical field is a nurse called Ms Chen. I met her when I went with a relative to a clinic, and I remember how clearly she explained what we needed to do.

Her work includes helping patients prepare for appointments, checking basic information and supporting the other medical staff. What I noticed most was the way she communicated. My relative was unsure where to go next, and she explained the steps patiently instead of making us feel embarrassed for asking.

I don't know every detail of her job, but I could see that it required both practical skills and attention to people. A clinic can feel confusing when you're worried, so a calm explanation makes a difference. I respect her because she treated an ordinary question as worth answering. The experience reminded me that good care involves how people feel as well as getting the practical tasks done properly.

职责与具体表现：协助预约准备、核对基本信息、配合医疗团队；耐心说明下一步，不写诊疗操作建议。
感受和理由：承认不了解全部工作，敬佩专业与细心相结合，温和解释减轻不安。

items.extensionZh: 若再见想道谢，短短互动改善看诊体验。

items.question: Why do some people want to be doctors?
items.questionZh: 为什么有人想成为医生？
items.answer: Some want to help people, while others have been influenced by a doctor who cared for someone in their family. They may also find the human body interesting. As they get older, learning more about the training and daily work can help them decide whether the career really suits them.
items.ideaZh: 想帮助别人、受家人或医生影响，或对人体感兴趣；做决定前应了解训练和实际工作。

items.question: Do you think it is difficult to become a doctor?
items.questionZh: 成为医生很困难吗？
items.answer: I think so, because it requires a long period of study and the ability to use knowledge carefully in real situations. Communication and responsibility matter alongside academic results. It's not only about passing exams; a person also needs to keep learning and work reliably with other professionals.
items.ideaZh: 长期学习、实际应用、沟通责任及团队合作，不止考试成绩。

items.question: Do you think studying biology at school makes students healthier?
items.questionZh: 在学校学生物会让学生更健康吗？
items.answer: It can help them understand the body and why certain habits matter, but knowledge doesn't automatically change behaviour. Students also need practical opportunities and support to use what they learn. I'd see biology as a helpful foundation, rather than assume studying the subject alone guarantees a healthy lifestyle.
items.ideaZh: 知识奠基但不自动变行为，需要实践条件支持；不作健康保证。

items.topic: 钦佩的商业人士（版本二）
items.question: Describe a business person you admire.
items.questionZh: 描述一个你敬佩的商业人士。
cueCard: And explain why you admire him/her.
items.answer:
A business person I admire is Ms Lin, the owner of a small restaurant near my school in Haikou. I got to know her because my friends and I sometimes eat there after playing basketball.

She told us that she started the business because she enjoyed cooking and wanted more control over her working life. She began with a small menu and used money she had saved, instead of opening a large place straight away.

The restaurant serves simple meals at prices students can afford. I think it does well because the food is reliable and the staff treat people warmly. Ms Lin remembers regular customers and listens when someone has a suggestion. The place isn't famous, but people keep coming back, which seems like a good sign. I admire the way she pays attention to ordinary details. Her business shows me that success can come from doing a useful job consistently.

经营时长与动机：约五年前开店，喜欢做饭并希望掌握工作节奏；时长和人物均为草稿。

items.topic: 特殊场合的食物（版本二）
items.question: Describe a special meal/food you eat on a particular occasion.
items.questionZh: 描述一种你在特定场合吃的特别餐食。
cueCard: When and where you eat it
And explain why you eat it.
items.answer:
A food people eat on special occasions is noodles, especially for birthdays. In the version I know from family meals, the noodles are fairly simple, but the occasion gives them meaning.

My mother usually cooks the noodles in water and serves them with vegetables, an egg and a light soup. The important thing is to keep the noodles long rather than cut them into tiny pieces. Long noodles are associated with wishes for a long life, so they fit a birthday celebration well.

We had them at my grandfather's home for his birthday. Everyone sat around the table, shared food and talked, which made the meal feel warm and personal. I like this kind of food because it doesn't need to be expensive or difficult to prepare. The meaning comes from the care behind it. For me, eating it is a way to celebrate someone and enjoy time together as a family.

items.topic: 观看体育赛事的经历（版本二）
items.question: Describe an experience of watching a sports event.
items.questionZh: 描述一次观看体育赛事的经历。
cueCard: When and where you watched it
And explain how you felt about this experience.
items.answer:
A live sports event I enjoyed watching was a basketball match at my school last term. I went with my friend Leo, and we stood beside the court with other students.

The match was between two student teams, so it wasn't a professional event, but the atmosphere was lively. People cheered when someone made a good shot, and we could hear the players calling to each other. The score stayed close for most of the game, which made it exciting to watch.

I liked being there in person because I could see things that are easy to miss in a short online clip. I watched how players moved when they didn't have the ball and how they helped each other. Since I play basketball myself, I found that interesting. We talked about the game afterwards and tried to remember a few useful ideas. It was an enjoyable afternoon that combined learning, excitement and time with a friend.

cluesZh: 背景：上学期学校篮球赛，与 Leo 和其他同学站在场边看。
现场气氛：两支学生队，欢呼和队员呼喊清晰，比分接近，所以紧张精彩。
喜欢原因：能看见短视频易遗漏的无球跑动和配合；自己也打球，赛后讨论技巧，兼有学习、兴奋与朋友相处。
translationsZh: 我喜欢亲自在场，因为能看到网上短片里容易错过的东西。我观察球员不持球时怎样移动，以及他们如何互相帮助。因为我自己也打篮球，所以觉得这很有意思。之后我们聊了这场比赛，试着记住几个有用的想法。这是一个愉快的下午，既学到了东西，又很兴奋，还和朋友一起度过了时间。
items.provenance: 真实背景：爱篮球。拟写与 Leo 在校园现场观看校队比赛、时间、赛况和观众反应；没有将自己打球充当看比赛。
items.extension: The result mattered less to me than the experience of being there. I would happily watch another school match if I had the time.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：结果不如现场体验重要，有时间愿意再看校内比赛。

items.question: Describe a time when you changed a decision.
items.questionZh: 描述一次你改变决定的经历。
cueCard: And explain how you felt about it.
items.answer:
A time I changed a decision was during a computer course. I had decided to complete a small class project on my own because I thought organising everything myself would be simpler than working with someone else.

After I started, I realised there were several parts I didn't understand well. My friend Leo was interested in the same project, so we talked about working together. He suggested dividing the tasks and checking each other's progress. I changed my decision because it seemed more sensible to learn from each other than spend days struggling with the same problem alone.

It was a good result. We finished something that worked, and I understood the process better because I had to explain my part to him. At first, I felt slightly embarrassed about changing my mind. Afterwards, I felt relieved and glad that I hadn't treated my first decision as a promise I could never revise. It taught me that adapting can be a sensible choice.

cluesZh: 原决定：计算机课程项目原打算独立完成，认为自己安排更省事；事件为新草稿。
为什么改变：遇到不熟部分，Leo提出分工和互查；合作比独自卡住更合理。
结果和感受：项目成功、解释过程帮助理解；从不好意思到释然，学会合理调整决定。
items.provenance: 计算机专业背景真实；决定独自做课堂项目后改为与Leo合作、讨论与成功结果均为新草稿。明确是改变decision，而非看电影后改变opinion。
items.extension: I still enjoy doing some work independently, but now I'd think about what the task needs before deciding that working alone is always easier.
items.extensionZh: 仍可独立工作，选择应取决于任务，而非默认单干最易。

items.question: Describe a piece of advertisement which is about a famous person.
items.questionZh: 描述一则有名人参与的广告。
cueCard: When and where you saw it
What the famous person does in the advertisement
And explain how you felt about it.
items.answer:
An advertisement I remember features Michael Jordan, the basketball player. It's an old Nike video about failure, and versions of it can still be found online. I came across it at home one evening last year while looking at basketball videos on my phone.

Jordan appears in the video and talks about setbacks in his career. What interested me was the message. Instead of only showing a famous player winning, the advertisement connects success with making mistakes and continuing to try. The product isn't the part that stayed in my mind. It was the idea that even someone people admire has experienced failure.

I liked that because I sometimes feel embarrassed when I make a mistake on the basketball court. My friend has encouraged me in that situation, so the message felt personal. Of course, watching an advertisement doesn't suddenly make me a better player. Still, it reminded me to focus on the next chance instead of the last mistake. I found it more memorable than an advertisement that simply tells me to buy something.

cluesZh: 广告、何时何地：乔丹Nike的Failure广告，去年一个晚上在家手机刷到；观看时间地点均为补充。
名人做什么与信息：乔丹出现在片中，谈职业生涯的挫折；概述失败后继续努力，不编造逐字原话。
个人联系与评价：球场失误时也会尴尬、得到朋友鼓励；广告不能立刻提高球技，但提醒把注意力放在下次机会。
translationsZh: 我喜欢这一点，因为在篮球场上犯错时，我有时会觉得尴尬。朋友曾在那种情况下鼓励过我，所以这条信息让我很有共鸣。当然，看一则广告不会突然让我变成更好的球员。不过，它提醒我关注下一次机会，而不是上一个错误。我觉得它比单纯叫我买东西的广告更容易让人记住。
items.provenanceType: 新增观看经历加公开事实
items.provenance: 广告为 Nike 的 Jordan Failure 广告；你在家刷到广告、个人反应为拟写，不引用或编造乔丹原话。
items.extension: I wouldn't buy shoes just because a famous player appeared in an advertisement. For me, comfort and price would still matter when making the decision.
items.extensionZh: 延伸：不会仅因名人代言买鞋，仍会考虑舒适度和价格。
